title: Triangulating Python Performance Issues with SCALENE
note: Pure user-space Python CPU/GPU/memory profiler; sampling is signal- and allocator-based so no perf counters or root are needed. Single CPU plus one NVIDIA GPU is exactly its target. Very actively maintained so a delta over the released version must be argued carefully.

title: K9db: Privacy-Compliant Storage For Web Applications By Construction
note: MySQL-compatible single-node storage engine layered on RocksDB; user-space build, workloads are single-machine web-app benchmarks. Concern: the headline contribution is GDPR compliance, so a performance-improvement hypothesis has to target its storage organisation and query path rather than the compliance story.

title: LVMT: An Efficient Authenticated Storage for Blockchain
note: Authenticated key-value storage layer (versioned multipoint trie over an LSM store) evaluated on replayed Ethereum traces on one machine. Rust, user-space, no special hardware. Concern: blockchain framing and a cryptographic (vector-commitment) core, and the AE badge link points at the plotting repo so the benchmark harness above is the substantive artifact.

title: ExoFlow: A Universal Workflow System for Exactly-Once DAGs
note: User-space workflow runtime built on Ray; the contribution (decoupling recovery from execution via task annotations and references) is a runtime design that Ray can exercise with multiple processes on one host. Concern: the paper's evaluation uses AWS clusters and serverless backends, so the team would need to scale the workloads down to a local Ray cluster.

title: VBASE: Unifying Online Vector Similarity Search and Relational Queries via Relaxed Monotonicity
note: Single-node query engine embedding vector indices into PostgreSQL; entirely user-space, CPU-bound, datasets fit the 257 GB of free disk. Concern: the released build is normally driven through containers, so the Dockerfile would have to be ported to a conda/source build. AE artifact mirror is https://github.com/Catoverflow/VBASE-artifacts .

title: Detecting Transactional Bugs in Database Engines via Graph-Based Oracle Construction
note: TxCheck is a user-space fuzzer plus statement-dependency-graph oracle driving TiDB, MySQL and MariaDB locally; no root, no cluster. Concern: it is a bug-finding tool, so an "improvement" hypothesis has to be about oracle coverage or test-generation throughput rather than system performance, and building three DBMS targets in user space is nontrivial.

title: Take Out the TraChe: Maximizing (Tra)nsactional Ca(che) Hit Rate
note: Squarely on-topic: a new cache eviction and prefetching policy (DeToX) driven by transactional dependencies, evaluated with OLTP traces and benchmarks on a single node in user space. Strong fit for a policy-improvement hypothesis with trace-driven replay.

title: TAILCHECK: A Lightweight Heap Overflow Detection Mechanism with Page Protection and Tagged Pointers
note: Implemented as LLVM compiler passes plus an extended mimalloc allocator; relies only on ordinary x86-64 pointer-tag bits and mmap page protection, all reachable without root. LLVM and the SPEC-style benchmarks build in user space. Concerns: the overhead numbers were measured with hardware the report does not fully specify, and the many PROT_NONE guard mappings may bump into the default vm.max_map_count which cannot be raised without root.

title: Cilantro: Performance-Aware Resource Allocation for General Objectives via Online Feedback
note: The contribution is an online-learning resource-allocation policy with confidence bounds - pure Python, simulatable from traces. Concern: every released experiment targets a Kubernetes/EKS cluster and ships a Dockerfile, and this machine has no root and no Docker, so the policies would have to be driven by a locally written trace-driven simulator or by cgroup-v2-limited processes.

title: Karma: Resource Allocation for Dynamic Demands
note: A credit-based generalisation of max-min fairness evaluated with trace-driven simulation over production workloads - precisely the kind of policy work scope.md allows to run on one machine. No hardware dependency. Concern: part of the contribution is a set of game-theoretic proofs, so the improvable surface is the allocation algorithm and its simulation study.

title: AlpaServe: Statistical Multiplexing with Model Parallelism for Deep Learning Serving
note: Model-serving system: placement and parallelisation of many DL models under bursty request arrivals. The artifact ships a discrete-event simulator alongside the real serving path, so the placement-policy contribution can be studied without a GPU cluster. Concern: the real system needs multiple GPUs for inter-op model parallelism, so end-to-end reproduction on one 24 GB A5000 is limited to small models plus simulation.

title: Cocktailer: Analyzing and Optimizing Dynamic Control Flow in Deep Learning
note: DNN compiler that schedules control flow into accelerator kernels; evaluated on a single GPU. CUDA toolchain installable per-user via conda. Concern: the artifact pins a specific CUDA/TVM/ROCm stack and driver 535 caps the native CUDA version at 12.2, so toolchain pinning is the main build risk. Zenodo mirror: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7856472 . Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion/tree/cocktailer_artifact .

title: Welder: Scheduling Deep Learning Memory Access via Tile-graph
note: Memory-access-centric DL compiler with a tile-graph abstraction; single-GPU evaluation, and the memory-bound regime it targets is exactly where a 24 GB Ampere card is representative. Concern: FP16 tensor-core paths work on Ampere but any FP8 kernel path does not, and the artifact expects a pinned CUDA/TVM stack. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion/tree/osdi2023welder .

title: EINNET: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Derivation-Based Transformations
note: Derivation-based tensor program optimizer; evaluated on single V100 and A100 GPUs, so an A5000 is a valid scaled-down target. Code is explicitly released in the abstract and actively maintained. Concern: reported speedups are hardware-specific, so a reproduction will produce different absolute numbers on Ampere consumer-class silicon. AE artifact: https://github.com/zhengly123/OSDI23-EinNet-AE .

title: Hydro: Surrogate-Based Hyperparameter Tuning Service in Datacenters
note: Surrogate model scaling plus job fusion for hyperparameter tuning, built on Ray Tune; the Tuner half (model scaling, parametrization, fusion) is meaningful on a single GPU. Concern: the Coordinator half assumes a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster with ephemeral resources and would have to be simulated or dropped.

title: Optimizing Dynamic Neural Networks with Brainstorm
note: Framework for dynamic (sparsely activated, MoE-style) networks using Cell and Router abstractions plus profile-guided dynamic optimisation; single-GPU inference workloads, and the memory-saving results are attractive on a 24 GB card. Concern: some evaluated models are large MoEs that will need to be scaled down. AE branch: https://github.com/Raphael-Hao/brainstorm/tree/osdi2023ae .

title: BWoS: Formally Verified Block-based Work Stealing for Parallel Processing
note: User-space concurrency library: block-partitioned work-stealing deques for language runtimes, evaluated with Renaissance on Java GC, Go JSON processing and the Rust Tokio HTTP server - all runnable on 16 cores with no root. Concern: the artifact received FUNCTIONAL and REPRODUCED badges but no AVAILABLE badge; the code that is public is the authors' Tokio fork branch referenced from the paper (Tokio PR tokio-rs/tokio#5283), which contains the bwosq implementation but is not a packaged artifact, and the Java/Go integrations are not obviously released. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/jschwe/tokio-rs/tree/bwos_master_lib .

title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
note: Chunked-prefill scheduling to trade throughput vs latency in LLM serving - pure user-space Python on top of vLLM. Paper used A100/A40 but a 7B model in FP16 fits the 24 GB A5000 so single-GPU scale-down is natural

title: ServerlessLLM: Low-Latency Serverless Inference for Large Language Models
note: Core contribution is a fast multi-tier checkpoint loading format plus locality-aware serverless scheduling - checkpoint loading from local NVMe to one GPU is directly reproducible. Concern - the scheduler and live migration parts assume a multi-GPU cluster and would have to be studied with a simulator or multiple processes

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
note: KV-cache offloading to CPU memory with speculative prefetch - designed exactly for one GPU plus large host DRAM. 125 GiB RAM and 24 GB GPU are a good match and no root is needed

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
note: Cross-instance request migration and scheduling for LLM serving built on vLLM - user-space Python. Concern - needs at least two serving instances so a scale-down needs small models sharing the single A5000 or the included simulation harness

title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
note: Prefill/decode disaggregation - user-space Python on vLLM with a published simulator and cost model. Concern - real disaggregation needs 2+ GPUs so on one A5000 the study would be simulator-driven or use tiny models in separate processes

title: Enabling Tensor Language Model to Assist in Generating High-Performance Tensor Programs for Deep Learning
note: Language model that emits tensor-program schedules for TVM/Ansor - learned component inside a compiler. Runs on one GPU. Concern - fine-tuning the tensor language model is compute heavy so a scaled-down model or released checkpoints would be needed

title: Ladder: Enabling Efficient Low-Precision Deep Learning Computing through Hardware-aware Tensor Transformation
note: Low-precision tensor compiler generating custom dtype kernels - evaluated on A100 V100 and RTX A6000 so the Ampere A5000 is a supported class of device. Concern - some dtype paths target newer toolkits and FP8 needs Ada/Hopper so those configurations must be dropped. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/BitBLAS/tree/osdi24_ladder_artifact .

title: Caravan: Practical Online Learning of In-Network ML Models with Labeling Agents
note: Online retraining and labeling pipeline for learned network models. Artifact appendix asks for an 8-core server 16 GiB RAM and one CUDA 12.1 GPU which this machine exceeds. Concern - the optional in-network deployment uses an FPGA testbed and must be skipped

title: nnScaler: Constraint-Guided Parallelization Plan Generation for Deep Learning Training
note: Search-space construction and plan generation for DNN training parallelization - the plan search compiler and cost model are user-space and can be studied on one GPU. Concern - end-to-end speedup claims need multiple GPUs so validation would rely on the cost model or single-GPU memory-saving plans

title: ChameleonAPI: Automatic and Efficient Customization of Neural Networks for ML Applications
note: Application-aware retraining/customization of neural networks behind ML APIs - single-GPU training and inference of modest models no root needed

title: When will my ML Job finish? Toward providing Completion Time Estimates through Predictability-Centric Scheduling
note: GPU-cluster scheduling for predictable completion times - main evaluation is a trace-driven simulator with only a small optional GPU testbed which is exactly the kind of scheduling study this machine supports. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/TuftsNATLab/PCS/tree/osdi24-artifact .

title: μSlope: High Compression and Fast Search on Semi-Structured Logs
note: Compression and search engine for semi-structured logs - CPU-only user-space C++ plus a large disk footprint that fits in 257 GB. Concern - full-scale log datasets used in the paper may need to be subsampled

title: Anvil: Verifying Liveness of Cluster Management Controllers
note: Verus-based liveness verification of Kubernetes controllers - the proofs and the Rust controllers build and check entirely in user space. Concern - the end-to-end controller experiments assume a Kubernetes cluster and Docker is not installed so that part would need a simulated or unit-test harness

title: FairyWREN: A Sustainable Cache for Emerging Write-Read-Erase Flash Interfaces
note: Flash cache that co-designs admission/eviction with garbage collection - a CacheLib fork by the first author is public although the paper itself gives no code link. Concern - the WREN/FDP interface needs a capable SSD and the machine has no root for device configuration so the study would have to be simulation or emulation based on the released carbon and write-amplification models

title: Massively Parallel Multi-Versioned Transaction Processing
note: GPU-accelerated deterministic multi-versioned OLTP engine - a single-GPU user-space CUDA program with YCSB/TPC-C workloads. Concern - CUDA version of the artifact may need a conda-installed newer toolkit on driver 535

title: Detecting Logic Bugs in Database Engines via Equivalent Expression Transformation
note: Equivalent expression transformation for finding logic bugs in DBMS engines - user-space testing tool driving SQLite MySQL PostgreSQL which can all be built or installed in a user prefix

title: Inductive Invariants That Spark Joy: Using Invariant Taxonomies to Streamline Distributed Protocol Proofs
note: Invariant taxonomy tool that streamlines distributed protocol proofs - Dafny toolchain runs entirely in user space on CPU. Concern - an improvement project here is proof automation rather than systems performance

title: IronSpec: Increasing the Reliability of Formal Specifications
note: Automated testing of formal specifications - Dafny and Z3 on CPU only fully user-space and CPU-parallel which suits 32 threads. Concern - proof/specification tooling rather than a performance system

title: dLoRA: Dynamically Orchestrating Requests and Adapters for LoRA LLM Serving
note: Dynamic merging/unmerging of LoRA adapters and adapter-aware batching - the merge/unmerge mechanism and batching policy are meaningful on one GPU with a 7B base model. Concern - the cross-replica migration part needs multiple GPUs

title: Parrot: Efficient Serving of LLM-based Applications with Semantic Variable
note: Semantic Variable abstraction and DAG-aware scheduling for LLM applications - user-space Python serving layer. Concern - published numbers use multi-GPU deployments so experiments need to be scaled to one A5000 with smaller models

title: USHER: Holistic Interference Avoidance for Resource Optimized ML Inference
note: GPU spatial multiplexing for ML inference with a kernel-based resource estimator and operator-graph merging - the estimator and model merging are single-GPU mechanisms. Concern - the placement scheduler is evaluated at cluster scale and would need simulation and MIG partitioning is unavailable on an A5000 so spatial sharing must rely on MPS or CUDA streams

title: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
note: Virtual Token Counter fair-queueing scheduler for LLM serving - a scheduling policy layered on a serving engine which is cheap to reproduce and extend on one GPU with small models

title: MonoNN: Enabling a New Monolithic Optimization Space for Neural Network Inference Tasks on Modern GPU-Centric Architectures
note: Monolithic whole-graph GPU kernel optimization for inference - single-GPU compiler work on NVIDIA hardware. Concern - built on a specific TensorFlow/XLA and CUDA version so toolchain setup in conda is the main risk

title: Basilisk: Using Provenance Invariants to Automate Proofs of Undecidable Protocols
note: Dafny-based invariant-inference tool; artifact is pure user-space CPU software (Dafny 4.2 installs into $HOME) and the 16 protocol benchmarks are self-contained. Concern: it is a formal-methods paper, so an "improvement" would target inference coverage or proof time rather than a runtime system; Dafny/Z3 proof runs can be long on 16 threads.

title: Deriving Semantic Checkers from Tests to Detect Silent Failures in Production Distributed Systems
note: T2C is a JVM static/dynamic analysis framework producing runtime checkers; no kernel, no root. Concern: evaluation drives four large JVM distributed systems (HDFS/HBase/Kafka/ZooKeeper) - must be run pseudo-distributed as multiple processes on the one host, and 125 GiB RAM should suffice but overhead numbers may shift.

title: Quake: Adaptive Indexing for Vector Search
note: Single-node user-space C++/Python vector index with a latency cost model; baselines (HNSW, DiskANN, SVS, ScaNN) are all user-space libraries. Concern: the paper's NUMA-aware intra-query parallelism cannot be studied on a 1-NUMA-node machine; Wikipedia-scale vector sets must fit the ~257 GB free disk. Artifact Available + Functional, not Reproduced.

title: Achieving Low-Latency Graph-Based Vector Search via Aligning Best-First Search Algorithm with SSD
note: PipeANN is user-space SSD-aware software (io_uring/AIO on NVMe), exactly the machine's strength: 2x PM9A3 NVMe. Badges: Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: headline results are billion-scale (SIFT1B/SPACEV1B) which needs ~1 TB; only ~257 GB is free, so experiments must scale down to 100M-point datasets.

title: KPerfIR: Towards a Open and Compiler-centric Ecosystem for GPU Kernel Performance Tooling on Modern AI Workloads
note: Profiling implemented as Triton compiler passes (upstreamed into triton-lang/triton third_party/proton/dialect); instrumentation is intra-kernel clock-based, so it does not need perf or root. Concern: the motivating use case is warp-specialized overlap on Hopper; on an Ampere A5000 some passes may be inapplicable, and Triton builds usually want CUDA 12.x installed via conda rather than the system 11.8.

title: Mirage: A Multi-Level Superoptimizer for Tensor Programs
note: Single-GPU tensor-program superoptimizer, mature public repo, Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: the search plus Z3 probabilistic equivalence check is CPU/GPU heavy and some generated kernels target A100/H100 feature levels - expect to re-tune for sm_86 and 24 GB.

title: QiMeng-Xpiler: Transcompiling Tensor Programs for Deep Learning Systems with a Neural-Symbolic Approach
note: LLM + symbolic-synthesis transcompiler; the toolchain itself is user-space Python and the CUDA target is testable on the A5000. Concern: three of the four evaluated back-ends (Intel AVX512-VNNI, AMD MI HIP, Cambricon BANG) do not exist on this AMD Zen3 + NVIDIA machine, so only a subset of the translation matrix can be reproduced; also needs an LLM API budget. Available + Functional, not Reproduced.

title: Bayesian Code Diffusion for Efficient Automatic Deep Learning Program Optimization
note: Auto-tuning search strategy implemented inside TVM/Ansor; runs entirely in user space on one CPU + one GPU, which is the paper's own evaluation setting. Strong fit: hypothesis-friendly (search-efficiency vs. achieved latency). Concern: full auto-tuning sweeps are long-running, so the 10-week budget must fix a small model set.

title: Training with Confidence: Catching Silent Errors in Deep Learning Training with Automated Proactive Checks
note: TrainCheck is a Python instrumentation/invariant-inference layer over PyTorch; Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: a subset of the 20 reproduced silent-error cases involve DeepSpeed/multi-GPU configurations that cannot be recreated on one 24 GB GPU - the single-GPU subset is still substantial.

title: Neutrino: Fine-grained GPU Kernel Profiling via Programmable Probing
note: Deliberately hardware-counter-free GPU profiler (assembly-layer probes, user-space driver interception), so perf_event_paranoid=3 and the lack of root are not blockers. Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: SASS probing is tied to specific driver/CUDA versions - needs checking against driver 535.216.01 and sm_86.

title: Decouple and Decompose: Scaling Resource Allocation with DeDe
note: Released as a plain Python package; the three case studies (cluster scheduling, traffic engineering, load balancing) are solved offline from traces on CPU only - precisely the "schedulers studied by simulation or traces" case in scope. Concern: baselines rely on a commercial solver (Gurobi academic license needed, user-space install); 16 cores limits the parallel-subproblem scaling claims.

title: Understanding Stragglers in Large Model Training Using What-if Analysis
note: The artifact is a trace-driven what-if simulator, not a cluster - it replays a five-month ByteDance trace on a single machine. Available + Functional. Concern: it is a measurement study, so the improvement angle is a better simulator/attribution method rather than a performance win; check that the released trace subset is large enough to support new claims.

title: Kamino: Efficient VM Allocation at Scale with Latency-Driven Cache-Aware Scheduling
note: Cache-aware request-scheduling algorithm evaluated with a high-fidelity simulator on production traces - simulation-only, so it fits the machine. Concern on code: the artifact carries Available + Functional + Reproduced badges on the OSDI '25 AE results page, but the PDF contains no repository URL, the authors' project page (daviddomingo.com/projects/Kamino) says "more information to be released", and GitHub search found nothing - repo marked unknown rather than out-no-code. Second concern: the Azure production traces are likely not public.

title: Extending Applications Safely and Efficiently
note: bpftime runs eBPF-style extensions entirely in *user space* via dynamic binary rewriting - that is the whole point of the paper, so unprivileged_bpf_disabled=2 does not block it; mature repo, Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: the isolation story uses Intel MPK/PKU, which must be verified on this Zen3 Threadripper; and the kernel-eBPF comparison baselines in the paper need root, so those numbers cannot be re-measured.

title: Building Bridges: Safe Interactions with Foreign Languages through Omniglot
note: Rust FFI-safety framework; the omniglot-mpk runtime targets ordinary Linux userspace libraries with no root (Rust installs into $HOME). Available + Functional. Concerns: the second half of the evaluation is on the Tock embedded kernel with RISC-V PMP hardware, which is out of reach; and the Linux runtime depends on MPK/PKU availability on an AMD CPU.

title: Deterministic Client: Enforcing Determinism on Untrusted Machine Code
note: Pure user-space SFI-style verifier/rewriter and sandbox runtime for x86-64 machine code, evaluated with SPEC-style CPU benchmarks and a smart-contract engine; no kernel, no hypervisor, no counters needed. Concerns: builds on a patched LLVM (long user-space build); the Arm64 half cannot be evaluated on this x86 host; the paper did not participate in artifact evaluation, but the authors' repo is public and self-described as the research artifact.

title: XSched: Preemptive Scheduling for Diverse XPUs
note: Preemption/scheduling framework implemented as a user-space shim over the accelerator command-queue API (CUDA driver level); artifact repo plus a separate xsched-artifacts repo and a Zenodo DOI; Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: the paper's generality claim spans ten XPUs - only one NVIDIA Ampere GPU is available here, and the highest hardware-preemption level may require capabilities the A5000 or driver 535 does not expose.

title: NanoFlow: Towards Optimal Large Language Model Serving Throughput
note: Intra-device (single-GPU) operation overlap for LLM serving - the mechanism is explicitly *within* one device, so it scales down cleanly. Available + Functional + Reproduced; very active repo. Concerns: published numbers use 8xA100-80GB with LLaMA-2-70B; on one 24 GB A5000 the study must drop to 8B-class models, and the hand-tuned CUTLASS/FlashInfer kernels were built for sm_80/sm_90 so sm_86 re-tuning is likely needed.

title: PipeThreader: Software-Defined Pipelining for Efficient DNN Execution
note: DNN compiler with software-defined pipelining, open-sourced inside TileLang; single-GPU by construction (FlashAttention, Mamba2 kernels). Concerns: the headline motivation is the Hopper Tensor Memory Accelerator, which Ampere lacks - the A5000 can only exercise the TensorCore/async-copy subset; also note the repo is the whole TileLang project, so the PipeThreader-specific code must be located within it.

title: DecDEC: A Systems Approach to Advancing Low-Bit LLM Quantization
note: Best machine fit in the venue: the paper's own evaluation uses a single consumer GPU (RTX 4050 Mobile, RTX 4090) with CPU-side residual storage over PCIe, and targets 3-4 bit Llama-3-8B-class models that fit 24 GB comfortably. Concerns: repo does not appear in the OSDI AE results list, so artifact quality is unverified; kernels may assume Ada-class PCIe/GPU behaviour and need checking on Ampere.

title: PoWER Never Corrupts: Tool-Agnostic Verification of Crash Consistency and Corruption Detection
note: Verification technique (Verus/Dafny) plus a verified KV store; the proof side is entirely user-space and reproducible on CPU, and the artifact has Available + Functional + Reproduced badges plus a Zenodo DOI. Serious concern: both CapybaraKV and its baselines target Intel Optane persistent memory, which env.md rules out - the performance half of the paper cannot be reproduced without DRAM-backed PM emulation, so a project here would have to be framed around the verification/proof-effort side.

title: Compass: Encrypted Semantic Search with High Accuracy
note: ORAM + graph-index co-design; client and server are ordinary user-space processes and the paper's own workloads are embedding datasets that fit in 125 GiB RAM / 257 GB disk. Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: "various network conditions" results were obtained across machines - on one host they must be emulated with loopback delay (tc needs root, so an application-level delay injector is required instead).

title: Paralegal: Practical Static Analysis for Privacy Bugs
note: Rust static analyzer (PDG extraction + policy checking); entirely user-space, CPU-only, with a Zenodo artifact DOI and Available + Functional + Reproduced badges. Concerns: needs a pinned Rust nightly toolchain plus rustc internals (installable via rustup into $HOME); the eight evaluated applications are large Rust codebases whose builds are long but single-machine.

title: Strata: Hierarchical Context Caching for Long Context Language Model Serving
note: GPU-HBM / host-DRAM / SSD KV-cache tiering plus a cache-aware scheduler - exactly the 1-GPU + 125 GiB RAM + NVMe shape of this machine. Concern: no dedicated artifact repo found; the paper says Strata "has been integrated into SGLang", so the code is upstream (HiCache path) rather than a standalone release - verify before committing. arXiv preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18572

title: ECHO: Efficient KV Cache Offloading with Lossless Prefetching for Serving Native Sparse Attention LLMs
note: KV-cache eviction/recall inside CUDA graphs + prefetching to host memory; mechanism is per-GPU. Concerns: artifact appendix asks for a server with 8 GPUs and ships as a Docker image (Docker is not installed here - would need porting); native-sparse-attention models must be picked small enough for 24 GB. Zenodo record: https://zenodo.org/records/20376436

title: Simple Is Better: Multiplication May Be All You Need for LLM Request Scheduling
note: A request-router scoring policy (KV-hit indicator x load indicator) - cheap to re-implement and to evaluate against the released Alibaba/Qwen usage traces. Concern: the real setting is several serving instances, so on one GPU it needs small models plus multiple processes, or trace-driven replay of the router only

title: Prism: Cost-Efficient Multi-LLM Serving via GPU Memory Ballooning
note: Elastic KV-cache memory ballooning across co-served models; the balloon driver (kvcached) is released and actively maintained, and multi-model co-serving on a single 24 GB GPU is the interesting regime. Concern: production evaluation uses many GPUs and bursty multi-model traces

title: OBASE: Object-Based Address-Space Engineering to Improve Memory Tiering
note: Compiler + user-space runtime that reorganises the virtual address space so pages become uniformly hot or cold - user-space memory management, no kernel changes. Concern: the paper's testbed has a real slow tier (Optane PMEM); this machine is one NUMA node with no PMEM/CXL, so a second tier would have to be emulated (cgroup limits + NVMe swap/zswap), which changes the measurement

title: Mohabi: Disaggregating and Sandboxing the Firefox JavaScript Engine
note: Pure user-space software fault isolation of SpiderMonkey inside Firefox; no root, no kernel, single machine. Concerns: building Firefox plus a custom SFI/WASM toolchain is a heavy build (clang/LLVM must be installed per-user via conda, tens of GB of disk); browser benchmarking is noisy on a shared machine

title: Cocoon: A System Architecture for Differentially Private Training with Correlated Noises
note: Single-node DP-training framework; the artifact appendix says main experiments ran on **RTX A5000 24 GB** GPUs - the same GPU as this machine. Concern: their box has 4 A5000s and two sockets, so runs must be scaled to one GPU; some results are embedding-table-heavy

title: ValScope: Value-Semantics-Aware Metamorphic Testing for Detecting Logical Bugs in DBMSs
note: User-space DBMS test-oracle generator (SQL query approximation + metamorphic relations); runs entirely against local SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL builds with no root. Concern: the "improvement" metric is bugs found, which is noisy over a 10-week window - a performance/coverage angle would be safer

title: Breaking the Reward Barrier: Accelerating Tree-of-Thought Reasoning via Speculative Exploration
note: Speculative exploration of Tree-of-Thought branches to break the reward-synchronisation barrier - a serving-layer scheduling change, testable with one GPU. Concern: the paper's model set includes Llemma-34B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, which do not fit 24 GB; only the 7B/8B configurations are reachable (possibly with quantization)

title: Controlling Opaque-Component Effects with Semisolates and Try
note: The paper explicitly states try is an *unprivileged*, language-agnostic command built on user namespaces / overlay mounts - bwrap-style sandboxing works on this machine. Clean single-machine performance target (effect capture/commit overhead)

title: Diagnosing Performance Issues in Application-Defined Resources
note: User-space profiler (gigiprofiler) combining LLM semantic inference with static analysis, evaluated on MariaDB/Redis-class applications on one host. Concern: it "integrates with perf to sample hardware counters" - perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks that path, so only the instrumentation/LLM part is reproducible

title: hS: Speculative Script Reordering at Subprocess Granularity
note: Out-of-order speculative execution of shell scripts with runtime effect detection; user-space, no root, benchmarks are local shell pipelines. Zenodo archive 10.5281/zenodo.19832407; artifact-eval branch osdi26-ae. Concern: effect interception may rely on user namespaces/overlayfs - available here, but worth confirming

title: Incr: Faster Re-Execution via Bolt-On Incrementalization
note: Automatic incrementalization of shell/polyglot re-execution - dependency tracking plus intermediate-result caching, all user space on one machine. Natural improvement axes (better caching policy, finer dependency granularity)

title: A Compilation-Based Under-Constrained Execution Engine
note: Compiles individual kernel components into native user-space harnesses and fuzzes them (AFL++) - the *analysis* runs in user space even though the target is kernel code, so no kernel build/boot is needed. Concern: LLVM toolchain must be built per-user; large compile times

title: Arctic: A Practical Lock-Free Adaptive Radix Tree
note: Ideal fit: a lock-free index benchmarked with YCSB and integrated into RocksDB and Turso, all user space, and 16 cores / 32 threads is enough to show scaling. Concern: Rust must be installed in user space (fine via rustup/conda); some scalability claims target higher core counts

title: Shaving the Peaks: Taming Tail Latency for Managed Workloads via Disaggregated Garbage Collection
note: Moves GC work off the mutator's CPU budget to cut tail latency in multi-tenant JVM workloads; single-server, user-space JVM/runtime work, and cgroup v2 cpu/memory controllers are delegated here. Concerns: artifact asks for a dual-socket NUMA Intel server with hyper-threading **disabled** (needs root) and assumes 32 physical cores per socket; this machine is single-socket, 16 cores

title: RLinf: Flexible and Efficient Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning via Macro-to-Micro Flow Transformation
note: The most reusable of the five RL-training papers: a fully open, actively maintained RL framework whose M2Flow placement/scheduling abstraction can be exercised on a single node. Concerns: headline results are many-GPU; on 24 GB only small policies (~1.5B, LoRA) are realistic, and the collocate-vs-disaggregate comparison largely disappears with one GPU

title: Osprey: Transparent and Efficient Virtual Memory for Secure Computation
note: A user-space, runtime virtual-memory layer that pages secure-computation working sets to SSD transparently - user-space memory management plus NVMe, no trusted hardware needed (this is MPC, not TEE). Concern: MPC parties are usually processes on separate hosts; they would have to be co-located as local processes

title: SPADE: Signal-Aware DAG Scheduling and Dynamic Provisioning for Data Processing Clusters
note: Explicitly in-scope form: besides the Spark-on-Kubernetes prototype the authors release a *high-fidelity Spark simulator* driven by Alibaba/TPC-H traces plus carbon/price signals, which runs fine on one CPU-only host. Concern: the 100-node K8s prototype path is out of reach - the simulator is the only usable route. Merge note: the scout's repo-link cell held the PDF URL; the repository given in the scout's prose (https://github.com/umass-solar/adaptive-dag) is used here.

title: Efficient GPU-Centric Evolving Graph Processing at Scale
note: Single-GPU out-of-core graph analytics; the artifact appendix says it was evaluated on an **NVIDIA RTX A4000**, i.e. a smaller Ampere card than ours. Concern: artifact asks for CUDA Toolkit >= 12.4 while the system nvcc is 11.8 and the driver is 535 - a per-user conda CUDA 12.4 toolkit is needed and minor-version compatibility must hold

title: Kairox: Adaptive GPU-CPU Hybrid LLM Inference via Online Neuron Balancing
note: Textbook fit: a llama.cpp-derived hybrid GPU+CPU engine that dynamically rebalances hot/cold FFN neuron groups between a single GPU and host CPU - 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM + 16 cores is the target hardware class

title: MPK: A Compiler and Runtime for Mega-Kernelizing Tensor Programs
note: Mature open compiler/runtime (Mirage Persistent Kernel) that fuses an entire model into one persistent CUDA kernel; single-GPU megakernels are the base case and the AE branch tgx-osdi26-ae plus Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20563064 are pinned. Concerns: the multi-GPU communication-overlap contribution is unreachable; SM-level scheduling was tuned on newer architectures, so Ampere (cc 8.6, no TMA/FP8) may need retuning

title: GraCE: Unlocking CUDA Graphs with Compiler Support for ML Workloads
note: CPU-launch-overhead elimination for short ML kernels via CUDA Graphs - single GPU, TorchBench/HuggingFace/TIMM workloads, and launch overhead is *more* visible on a modest GPU. Concerns: the prebuilt artifact is a Docker image built for CUDA 12.8 (no Docker here, and driver 535 supports CUDA 12.2 natively) - needs a source build in a conda env

title: Nixie: Efficient, Transparent Temporal Multiplexing for Consumer GPUs
note: Best-matched paper in the venue for this machine: a *user-space system service* that time-multiplexes several near-GPU-memory-filling ML jobs on a **consumer GPU** with "no application or driver changes", plus an MLFQ-style scheduler. Eval repo: https://github.com/XOR-op/nixie-eval . Concern: pinned-host-memory pressure experiments assume a large host RAM budget (we have it)

title: Mimesys: Generating Realistic Executable Testing Environments from Resource Usage Traces
note: Synthesises executable contention workloads from resource-usage traces; artifact runs on plain Linux, the diffusion model trains on one GPU, and cgroup v2 cpu/memory delegation supports the contention experiments. Concern: fidelity claims involve memory-bandwidth contention, which is hard to *measure* here without hardware counters

title: SMARTTalk: Teaching SMART Logs to Talk to LLMs
note: Learned component inside a storage system: a representation layer turning SMART telemetry into LLM-consumable form for failure prediction. Public datasets (Alibaba SSD SMART logs, Backblaze) and a 7-8B model fit 24 GB with LoRA

title: Neuro-Symbolic Proof Generation for Scaling Systems Software Verification
note: LLM-guided best-first proof search over Isabelle proof states for seL4-scale verification - CPU-heavy search plus one-GPU model inference/fine-tuning, all user space. Concerns: the seL4 proof corpus and Isabelle builds are large and slow; the paper gives no URL in-line (repo located by search), so confirm it is the official artifact

title: Spain: Succinct Proofs for Numerical Computations
note: User-space prover/front-end toolchain with a clear, reproducible performance target (prover time and constraint count for float-heavy computations); most benchmarks need under 5 GB RAM. Concerns: the artifact is Docker-based (must be ported to conda/source) and the largest GPT-2 configuration needs ~270 GB RAM (we have 125 GiB) - stick to the small benchmarks

title: Learning-Augmented Heuristics: Simple Yet Smart, Robust and Interpretable Cache Eviction
note: Learned *parameters* for static eviction heuristics (S4-FIFO), with released code, pre-trained model, and libCacheSim + CacheLib implementations; evaluation is pure trace-driven simulation over thousands of public traces - perfect for a machine with no root. See also https://libcachesim.com and arXiv 2608.27975

title: RT: Regular Types for the Streaming Shell
note: Overlay type system for shell stream programs; artifact appendix gives the GitHub repo, checking is CPU-only and user space, and the evaluation corpus is hundreds of public shell programs. Concern: contribution is static checking, so "performance improvement" would have to mean checking speed, precision, or coverage

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
note: KV-cache paging plus continuous batching; the canonical single-GPU LLM serving substrate. Runs entirely in user space on one CUDA GPU. Fits the A5000 with 7B FP16 models. Concerns - paper evaluates OPT-13B/66B/175B on multi-GPU A100 nodes so absolute numbers need scale-down to 7B-class; modern vLLM main branch has drifted far from the SOSP artifact (AE snapshot is https://github.com/sosp-ae-39/sosp-ae-astra) so pinning a version matters; recent wheels may want CUDA >12.2 which is a driver-535 risk

title: FIFO queues are all you need for cache eviction (S3-FIFO)
note: Pure trace-driven cache-eviction study plus a C implementation in libCacheSim; CPU only, no root, no GPU. Ideal fit for the machine and for an improvement-style hypothesis on eviction policy. Concerns - the 6594-trace corpus across 14 datasets is far larger than 257 GB free so a documented trace subset must be chosen; the throughput/scalability claims were made at 16 threads which the 16-core Threadripper matches well

title: Paella - Low-latency Model Serving with Software-defined GPU Scheduling
note: User-space GPU kernel-granularity scheduler for DNN inference serving; README states it was tested on NVIDIA driver 535.54 and CUDA 12.2 which matches our driver 535.216 exactly, and CUDA arch is a build flag so sm_86 works. Single GPU by design. Concerns - needs LLVM/Clang 14, Boost, spdlog and a custom TVM fork all built from source into $HOME; the custom TVM build is long; MPS-style kernel interception should work unprivileged but is untested here

title: Sia - Heterogeneity-aware goodput-optimized ML-cluster scheduling
note: Cluster scheduling policy with an explicit trace-driven simulator (sia-simulator) in the artifact, which is exactly the "evaluated with simulators or traces" case the scope allows. Policy improvements can be tested end-to-end on one machine. Concerns - the physical-cluster half of the artifact needs a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster plus AdaptDL/Pollux and is out of reach; only the simulator track is viable, which limits claims to simulated goodput

title: Turbo - Effective Caching in Differentially-Private Databases
note: A caching/admission mechanism (PMW-Bypass) for DP query answering; Python core driven by Ray, CPU only, single machine, no root. Clean target for a policy-improvement hypothesis. Concerns - the artifact packages itself with Docker images which are not installable here, so deps must be replicated by hand with conda/pip; Covid and Citibike datasets must be regenerated by the provided scripts

title: PIT - Optimization of Dynamic Sparse Deep Learning Models via Permutation Invariant Transformation
note: GPU sparse-kernel compiler/runtime for dynamic sparsity; the mechanism is per-GPU and Ampere sm_86 is supported by the CUDA kernels. Concerns - the AE README asks for 8x V100-32GB or 1x A100-80GB and 200-700 GB disk, so models must be scaled down to fit 24 GB and 257 GB; reproduction is shipped as a Docker image that has to be ported to conda; no FP8 paths involved so Ampere is otherwise fine. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/pit_artifact .

title: gSampler - General and Efficient GPU-based Graph Sampling for Graph Learning
note: Single-GPU matrix-centric graph sampler with a data-flow-graph optimizer; AE reference hardware is a single V100 so a 24 GB A5000 is comfortable, and everything is user-space PyTorch/DGL/CUDA. Concerns - the AE instructions ask for 256 GB RAM to preprocess ogbn-papers100M and Friendster in CSC format and we only have ~111 GB available, so the study must stay on ogbn-products and LiveJournal or use out-of-core preprocessing

title: SPFresh - Incremental In-Place Update for Billion-Scale Vector Search
note: On-disk vector index with an in-place rebalancing protocol (LIRE); an SSD-aware user-space storage engine on a single node, and the machine has two NVMe drives. Concerns - the default storage layer is SPDK, and the README explicitly requires secure boot off and kernel lockdown disabled for user-space PCI/NVMe access, which we cannot do without root; a modified-RocksDB backend is offered as an alternative and would have to be used; billion-scale datasets exceed 257 GB so 10M-100M subsets are needed; build uses gcc-9 and several apt-only libs that must be sourced through conda

title: Validating JIT Compilers via Compilation Space Exploration (Artemis)
note: Entirely user-space runtime/compiler testing tool - requirements are only Java >= 11, Python >= 3.9 and Ruby >= 2.7, all installable under $HOME, no root, no GPU, no perf counters. Bug-finding throughput is a clean measurable metric for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - the value metric is bugs-found per unit time which is noisy over a 10-week window; long fuzzing campaigns are CPU-hungry on a shared machine; the AE artifact of record is Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8188346 and the maintained code is the GitHub repo

title: Bagpipe - Accelerating Deep Recommendation Model Training
note: The core mechanism is a lookahead oracle cache that prefetches hot embeddings ahead of the training loop, which is meaningful with one trainer plus one cache process on a single node with one GPU. Kept as borderline per the scope rule. Concerns - serious machine risk: the released AE artifact is an EC2 cluster launcher (ec2_launcher_six_models.py) that provisions a multi-node AWS cluster and the torchrec baseline is distributed, so no single-node scale-down is provided and the team would have to build one; the audit stage should decide whether that is 10-week feasible

title: Apparate: Rethinking Early Exits to Tame Latency-Throughput Tensions in ML Serving
note: Early-exit ramps bolted onto existing serving systems; a pure user-space PyTorch/serving-runtime artifact. Models used (ResNet/BERT/GPT-2 class) fit one 24 GB A5000. Concern: paper evaluates on multi-GPU serving clusters, so a scale-down to one GPU plus a replay of their request traces is needed; goodput numbers will not be directly comparable.

title: Caribou: Fine-Grained Geospatial Shifting of Serverless Applications for Sustainability
note: Placement/scheduling policy for serverless workflows across regions driven by carbon, cost and latency data; the deployment solver is an offline optimizer that can be replayed against their collected carbon/price/latency datasets on one machine. Concern: end-to-end evaluation deploys to AWS Lambda and GCP across many regions, which this environment cannot do - only the solver and its input traces are locally studyable.

title: Cookie Monster: Efficient On-Device Budgeting for Differentially-Private Ad-Measurement Systems
note: Core artifact is a user-space on-device budget manager plus a Python/Rust trace-driven simulator over Criteo and microbenchmark datasets; runs CPU-only, no root. Clear quantitative objective (queries answerable per privacy budget) that an improvement hypothesis can target. Concern: privacy/utility rather than classic OS resource management - topic fit rests on the other-userspace catch-all.

title: Efficient Reproduction of Fault-Induced Failures in Distributed Systems with Feedback-Driven Fault Injection
note: Anduril is a user-space JVM-level fault-injection and search tool; targets (ZooKeeper, HDFS, Cassandra, Kafka) are normally run as several JVMs on a single host, which env.md explicitly allows. Efficiency metric (injections/time to reproduce a failure) is directly measurable. Concern: testing/debugging tooling, not resource management; 125 GiB RAM should hold the multi-JVM setups but runs are long.

title: Morph: Efficient File-Lifetime Redundancy Management for Cluster File Systems
note: Redundancy-transcoding policy for cluster file systems, evaluated largely by trace-driven simulation over Google/production file-lifetime traces - exactly the simulation route env.md permits. Java artifact, user space. Concern: the HDFS prototype half of the evaluation wants a multi-node cluster; the project would have to stay on the simulator and single-node coding microbenchmarks.

title: Icarus: Trustworthy Just-In-Time Compilers with Symbolic Meta-Execution
note: DSL plus symbolic meta-execution engine for JIT compiler transformations; entirely user-space, no root, no special hardware. Companion repo https://github.com/PLSysSec/icarus-firefox integrates with SpiderMonkey. Metric (symbolic-execution time, transformations covered) supports a testable improvement hypothesis. Concern: PL/verification rather than a systems resource-management artifact, and building Firefox from source is a heavy 10-week-budget item.

title: If At First You Don't Succeed, Try, Try, Again...? Insights and LLM-informed Tooling for Detecting Retry Bugs in Software Systems
note: Wasabi is a user-space static-analysis plus fault-injection toolkit for Java/Python systems; runs on one machine, no root. Concern: it needs LLM API access (cost, non-determinism) and its metric is bug-detection precision/recall rather than performance, so a "testable hypothesis" would have to be framed around detection quality or analysis cost. Weakest topic fit of the included set.

title: Improving DNN Inference Throughput Using Practical, Per-Input Compute Adaptation
note: E3 splits and replicates blocks of early-exit models to keep batch size constant; a user-space serving-layer mechanism that can be exercised with one A5000 on BERT/GPT-2 class models. Concern: no artifact found - not in the SOSP 2024 AE results, and no repo on the authors' GitHub accounts (checked dywsjtu, MingyuGuan, ruipan, swapnilgandhi, anandpiyer) or the Georgia Tech NEXS project page. Marked unknown rather than out-no-code because the closely related Apparate artifact from the same group is public and E3 code may live unlinked.

title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
note: Designed for exactly this machine class: one consumer/workstation GPU plus CPU, hot/cold neuron-aware GPU-CPU hybrid inference with offloading. llama.cpp-based, user-space build, CUDA 11.8/12.x friendly, no root. 7B-13B models in the sparsity-aware formats fit 24 GB or spill to the 125 GiB host RAM by design. Strongest single candidate.

title: Practical Verification of System-Software Components Written in Standard C
note: TPot is a user-space SMT-based verifier for C system software; CPU-only, no root, and verification wall-clock time is a clean quantitative target for an improvement hypothesis. Concern: proof engineering rather than resource management; topic fit rests on the other-userspace catch-all.

title: Reducing Energy Bloat in Large Model Training
note: Perseus's core is an offline time-energy Pareto planner over pipeline-stage frequency assignments - a graph algorithm that runs on profiles, so it can be studied and improved without the training cluster. Energy/power readings come from NVML via nvidia-smi, which needs no root and no perf counters. Concern: end-to-end validation in the paper uses multi-GPU pipeline-parallel training; on one A5000 only the planner plus single-GPU DVFS profiling is reproducible, and GPU frequency locking may require privileges. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/ml-energy/zeus/tree/kronos .

title: Reducing Cross-Cloud/Region Costs with the Auto-Configuring MACARON Cache
note: A cache sizing/admission policy paper - squarely in the caching topic - and the authors ship a separate trace-driven simulator (https://github.com/hojinp/macaron_simulator), which is the single-machine evaluation path env.md wants. Concern: the C++ prototype half was evaluated against real S3/cross-region storage; cost-model parameters would have to be taken from the paper rather than measured. Repos have no README or license metadata, so build effort is unverified from a desk check.

title: Sesame: Practical End-to-End Privacy Compliance with Policy Containers and Privacy Regions
note: Rust framework (actively maintained) enforcing privacy policies inside web applications; user space, no root, evaluated as request-latency/throughput overhead against unmodified baselines - a directly measurable performance axis on this machine. Concern: compliance/privacy framing rather than an OS resource-management topic; the evaluation apps need a local database and web stack stood up by hand.

title: SilvanForge: A Schedule-Guided Retargetable Compiler for Decision Tree Inference
note: An ML compiler (MLIR/LLVM-based) that autoschedules decision-tree inference for both CPU and a single GPU - the paper's own evaluation platform is one multicore CPU plus one NVIDIA GPU, matching this machine almost exactly. Concern: needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR toolchain built from source (clang is not installed), which is a real but tractable setup cost. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/asprasad/treebeard/tree/silvanforge .

title: Uncovering Nested Data Parallelism and Data Reuse in DNN Computation with FractalTensor
note: DNN compiler/IR exploiting nested data parallelism; kernels are generated for a single NVIDIA GPU and the artifact builds against CUDA plus cuDNN in user space. Ampere (sm_86) is supported by its CUTLASS/TileFusion-style tiling. Concerns: the AE badge points at https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion while the maintained code lives in microsoft/FractalTensor and is described as "under active refactoring"; some generated kernels may assume newer CUDA than the 11.8 system nvcc, so a conda CUDA toolkit would be needed.

title: Unearthing Semantic Checks for Cloud Infrastructure-as-Code Programs
note: Zodiac is a Python static/differential-analysis tool over IaC programs; runs entirely offline in user space with no cloud credentials for the analysis phase. Concern: detection quality rather than performance is the headline metric, and validating found checks against real cloud providers is out of reach here; topic fit rests on the other-userspace catch-all.

title: Verus: A Practical Foundation for Systems Verification
note: Distinguished Artifact winner; a user-space Rust verifier with a large open codebase and a self-contained AE harness (https://github.com/verus-lang/paper-sosp24-artifact). Verification wall-clock time and SMT query counts are clean, reproducible single-machine metrics, so an "improve the design/performance" hypothesis is straightforward. Rust toolchain installs into $HOME via rustup, no root needed. Concern: verification tooling rather than a resource-management system; the full case-study proof corpus is CPU-hours-heavy.

title: Unlocking True Elasticity for the Cloud-Native Era with Dandelion
note: User-space Rust serverless worker node; the headline claim (sandboxes that cold-start in 100s of microseconds, 96% less committed memory on the Azure Functions trace) is a single-machine, trace-driven result. Concerns - the kvm isolation backend is unusable (no /dev/kvm) and the Firecracker baseline needs KVM, so only the mmu process-isolation backend is reproducible; the mmu worker README asks for an exec-mounted /dev/shm which normally needs root and would need a workaround.

title: HedraRAG: Co-Optimizing Generation and Retrieval for Heterogeneous RAG Workflows
note: Graph-based scheduling of RAG stages onto a single CPU-GPU pipeline - exactly the single-node, single-GPU setting of this machine. Concerns - retrieval index and corpus size must fit in 257 GB of free disk; generator model must be scaled to 7-8B FP16 to fit 24 GB.

title: DiffKV: Differentiated Memory Management for Large Language Models with Parallel KV Compaction
note: KV-cache compression plus an on-GPU allocator that compacts fragmented free lists in parallel; a vLLM-style single-GPU serving artifact and a very clean target for a "better allocator / better compression policy" hypothesis. Concerns - custom CUDA kernels may need a toolkit newer than the system nvcc 11.8 (installable per-user via conda, but driver 535 caps usable CUDA at 12.2).

title: PhoenixOS: Concurrent OS-level GPU Checkpoint and Restore with Validated Speculation
note: Despite the name it is a user-space CUDA-API interception layer, not a kernel change; concurrent checkpoint/restore of a GPU process is demonstrable on one A5000. Well-maintained repo (292 stars, updated 2026-09). Concerns - tightly coupled to specific CUDA runtime/driver versions; driver 535 supports CUDA up to 12.2 only, so the supported-version matrix needs checking before committing.

title: Pie: A Programmable Serving System for Emerging LLM Applications
note: Decomposes the generation loop into handlers driven by user WebAssembly "inferlets"; all sandboxing is user space and the evaluation model sizes fit one 24 GB GPU. Strong candidate for an improvement project (new KV-cache strategies are the paper's own stated extension point). Concerns - none major; needs a Rust toolchain installed in user space.

title: Aegaeon: Effective GPU Pooling for Concurrent LLM Serving on the Market
note: The core mechanism - token-granularity auto-scaling that multiplexes many models onto *one* GPU with fast weight swapping - is inherently a single-GPU idea and the paper itself includes a single-A10 experiment. Official artifact (first author Y. Xiang; also Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16673199). Concerns - the AE README asks for 2x8 H100 nodes, an A100-80GB node, ~512 GB CPU RAM and ~256 GB of model weights; a serious scale-down to a pool of small models on 24 GB is mandatory and the multi-node baselines cannot be reproduced.

title: WASIT: Deep and Continuous Differential Testing of WebAssembly System Interface Implementations
note: Entirely user-space: the tool and all six Wasm runtimes under test install without root and run on one machine. Concerns - it is a testing framework, so an "improvement" hypothesis would be about bug-finding throughput, coverage or oracle precision rather than system performance; the repo is small and lightly documented (2 stars).

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
note: An attention-property-aware KV allocator implemented inside vLLM; single-GPU memory-utilization and throughput claims are directly measurable here, and the allocation policy is easy to perturb for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - several evaluated models (large MoE and multimodal) exceed 24 GB, so the model set must be scaled down; upstream vLLM has moved on, so the AE snapshot may need pinning.

title: KNighter: Transforming Static Analysis with LLM-Synthesized Checkers
note: Artifact is user-space Python plus Clang Static Analyzer checkers; it only needs Linux kernel *source* (compiled, never booted) and LLVM, both installable via conda without root. Active repo (189 stars). Concerns - requires a paid LLM API for checker synthesis, which is a real budget constraint; and the systems tie-in is analysis tooling rather than a runtime, so "performance" means synthesis cost / false-positive rate.

title: Orthrus: Efficient and Timely Detection of Silent User Data Corruption in the Cloud with Resource-Adaptive Computation Validation
note: User-space runtime plus an LLVM compiler pass that re-validates annotated data operators asynchronously on spare cores; the whole experiment (including LLVM-based fault injection, see the companion Orthrus-FaultInjection repo) is single-machine and root-free. Concerns - the README states a minimum of 48 cores for the test scripts and this machine has 16 cores / 32 threads, so the core-scaling experiments must be rescaled and the 4-validation-core points re-interpreted.

title: PrefillOnly: An Inference Engine for Prefill-only Workloads in Large Language Model Applications
note: Storing only the last layer's KV cache drastically cuts GPU memory, which is precisely what makes long-input LLM work feasible on a 24 GB card; JCT-aware scheduling (shortest-prefill-first) is an obvious axis to improve. Concerns - the official artifact is a Zenodo zip of a vLLM fork (vllm_prefill-bowen-artifact-eval.zip) rather than a maintained Git repository, so it will not track upstream vLLM.

title: Mitigating Application Resource Overload with Targeted Task Cancellation
note: Atropos is a user-space overload-control framework integrated into MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch, Solr, Apache and etcd - all single-host, root-free workloads, and 16 cores / 125 GB is ample to reproduce the 16 overload scenarios. The culprit-scoring policy is a clean target for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - per-request resource monitoring may want signals this machine restricts (no perf counters); cgroup v2 cpu/memory/pids are delegated, which should cover the resource-limiting side.

title: Sailor: Automating Distributed Training over Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Geo-distributed Clusters
note: The improvable core - the search-space exploration algorithm and the runtime/memory-footprint simulator - runs entirely on one CPU machine, and simulator accuracy is itself a testable hypothesis. Concerns - the end-to-end throughput and cost claims need heterogeneous multi-node GPU clusters that do not exist here, so only the planner/simulator half is reproducible; the team must scope the project to that half up front.

title: Tempo: Compiled Dynamic Deep Learning with Symbolic Dependence Graphs
note: Single-node DL compiler; the headline numbers (7x over JAX on Llama-3.2-3B decoding, 54x on RL algorithms with 16x lower peak memory) are all measured on one GPU and a 3B model fits comfortably in 24 GB. Compiler passes (tiling, fusion, polyhedral scheduling) are a rich improvement surface. Concerns - the polyhedral/codegen toolchain may need recent LLVM and CUDA installed per-user via conda.

title: Scalable Far Memory: Balancing Faults and Evictions
note: Scope explicitly allows far-memory studied in user space, and this paper implements its three principles in both the Linux kernel *and* a library OS, so the library-OS (user-space) path is the reproducible one. Concerns - the kernel-side half needs root and a custom kernel and is out of reach; the far-memory backend normally needs a second machine or RDMA and would have to be emulated locally; the scalability claims target far higher core counts than 32 threads, so the interesting high-thread regime is partly out of reach.

title: KTransformers: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU/GPU Hybrid Inference for MoE Models
note: A single-GPU-plus-large-DRAM system by construction - the exact shape of this machine (1x24 GB GPU, 125 GB RAM). The Expert Deferral mechanism and the async CPU-GPU scheduler are hardware-agnostic and directly improvable. Very actively maintained (19.5k stars). Concerns - the headline CPU kernels are Intel AMX-specific and this is an AMD Zen3 Threadripper with no AMX and no AVX-512, so the CPU-side speedups will not reproduce as published; and 671B DeepSeek-V3/R1 needs far more than 125 GB, so a smaller MoE (e.g. Mixtral-class or Qwen3-MoE) scale-down is required.

title: TrainVerify: Equivalence-Based Verification for Distributed LLM Training
note: Although the subject is distributed training, the artifact itself is symbolic/SMT equivalence checking that runs on CPU only - no GPUs and no cluster are needed to reproduce the Llama3-405B and DeepSeek-V3-671B plan verifications. Shape reduction and stage-wise verification are well-defined targets for a "verify faster" hypothesis. Concerns - verifying frontier-scale plans may be memory and time hungry even on 125 GB; success is measured in verification time and coverage, not system throughput.

title: Loom: Efficient Capture and Querying of High-Frequency Telemetry
note: Self-contained Rust ingest-plus-sparse-index engine; the repo's usage/ examples drive it with synthetic record generators (rand/rand_distr) rather than live tracers, so the ingest-throughput and query-latency claims are reproducible without any privileged data source. Baselines FishStore and InfluxDB both install in user space. Concerns - the paper's motivating data sources (perf, DTrace, eBPF) are all blocked on this machine, so evaluation must use synthetic or pre-recorded traces, which weakens realism.

title: A Few GPUs, A Whole Lotta Scale: Faithful LLM Training Emulation with CrystalLLM
note: Preprint titled PrismLLM. Emulates thousand-GPU LLM training by running only selected ranks for real and replaying the rest as virtual participants - that hybrid emulation is exactly a single-GPU scale-down. Concern: fidelity claims are validated against real production clusters we cannot access and it builds on CRIU/cuda-checkpoint which may want privileges. No artifact link in the preprint.

title: AgileLog: A Forkable Shared Log for Agents on Data Streams
note: Forkable shared-log abstraction plus the Bolt implementation. User-space C++ log server. Concern: shared logs are normally evaluated on a multi-node cluster - here it would have to be many processes on one host. Repo is the authors lab org (dassl-uiuc) and is public but named -Proto so it may be a prototype rather than the final artifact.

title: Ahead-of-time Analysis of Shell Program Effects
note: SaSh statically analyzes shell scripts with optimistic symbolic execution over a filesystem model. Pure user-space CPU work - no GPU, no root. Official repo found under the authors Brown lab org. Very good fit for a 10-week improvement project (precision or speed of the symbolic engine is directly measurable).

title: Anchor: Mitigating GPU Shallow Disruptions with Decoupled Memory
note: Tsinghua storage group. Title indicates decoupling GPU memory to survive shallow (transient) GPU disruptions - a GPU memory-management mechanism that is plausible to demo on one A5000. Concern: no abstract or preprint is public yet so the scale of the evaluation is unknown. Author group page lists it but the Paper link is not live.

title: Ave: Guiding Agentic GPU Optimization Using Data-Flow Invariants
note: ARGUS - agentic generation of GPU kernels guided by compile-time data-flow invariants, with a tile-based Python DSL. Kernel generation and benchmarking work on a single GPU. Concerns: the DSL exposes modern tensor-core or TMA style instructions that may assume Hopper rather than Ampere sm_86, and reproducing the agent loop costs LLM API calls. No artifact URL in the preprint.

title: Batched in Back: Characterizing and Optimizing Offline LLM Inference in Production with ACDC
note: Offline (batch) LLM inference characterization and optimization. Offline batching is a natural single-GPU workload and scheduling ideas port down easily. Concern: it is a production study at Alibaba so the traces and the 7B-plus model fleet may not be released - the optimization part may still be reproducible on one GPU.

title: Beyond Utilization: Energy-Conscious GPU Sharing for Inference Serving
note: Energy and carbon-conscious spatial GPU sharing for inference serving. Single-GPU colocation is the exact setting. NVML power readings and MPS both work without root on this machine so the measurement methodology is reproducible. Concern: no preprint or artifact link found yet.

title: Computation is Fast, Use Threadlet!
note: Included only because it cannot be screened out on the evidence available. TELOS lab at PKU confirms the acceptance but no abstract, preprint or artifact is public, so neither topic nor machine fit can be judged. Title suggests a lightweight thread or compute-offload abstraction which could be either user space or kernel.

title: DDB: Source-Level Interactive Debugging for Distributed Applications
note: Source-level interactive debugger for distributed applications - user-space tooling, no root needed. Evaluated against systems like LogCabin and Jepsen-style workloads that can be run as several processes on one host. Concern: no artifact URL in the preprint and distributed timeout behaviour may differ when everything is colocated.

title: DiFlow: A System for Micro-Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Workflows
note: LegoDiffusion decomposes text-to-image diffusion workflows into independently scheduled model nodes. SD or FLUX class pipelines fit in 24 GB and the per-model sharing idea is testable on one GPU. Concerns: per-model scaling and adaptive model parallelism are cluster-scale claims that must be scaled down or simulated. No artifact link found.

title: Don't Let AI Agents YOLO Your Files: Information and Control in Agent-Native Filesystems
note: YoloFS - an agent-native filesystem that stages mutations, snapshots, and gates accesses for AI coding agents. FUSE is usable unprivileged on this machine (/dev/fuse world-rw, setuid fusermount3). Code is explicitly open-sourced in the abstract. Concern: the evaluation drives real coding agents so it needs LLM API budget.

title: Efficient GPU Multitasking with Morphable Kernels
note: Morphable kernels for GPU multitasking (Tsinghua). Single-GPU concurrency and kernel-shaping work - an excellent fit for one A5000. Concern: no abstract, preprint or artifact is public; confirmed only through the authors group publication page.

title: Janus: Multi-LLM Serving at Production Scale
note: Multi-LLM serving with dual-timescale scheduling, HBM virtualization (xTensor) and device-to-device model fork. Repo exists. Big concern: deployed on 768 devices in production, so the elastic-scaling and bin-packing results have no direct single-GPU analogue - the request scheduler and xTensor memory virtualization do.

title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
note: Scheduling-based determinism for LLM inference using verified speculation instead of batch-invariant kernels. Runs on one GPU with a 7-8B model. Official Microsoft repo referenced from the preprint. One of the strongest candidates on this list for a 10-week improvement project.

title: LMTracer: Fine-Grained and Real-Time Performance Profiling for Production LLM Systems
note: Fine-grained real-time profiler for LLM serving systems. Profiling and tracing work is user space. Serious concern: GPU-side fine-grained profiling usually needs CUPTI, and on driver 535 CUPTI profiling counters are admin-restricted by default - plus perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks CPU counters here. No preprint or artifact found.

title: M2K: Making the Model-Kernel Interface Explicit for Reliable CUDA Kernel Verification
note: Model2Kernel does model-aware dynamic analysis to catch memory-safety bugs in CUDA kernels used by LLM inference engines such as vLLM. Single GPU is enough to run the checker. Official repo linked from the preprint. Concern: some target kernels may be written for newer architectures than Ampere.

title: On-site, Non-speculative Failure Diagnosis with CLODS
note: On-site non-speculative failure diagnosis (YScope and U. Toronto - the CLP log-compression group, which has a track record of open-sourcing). User-space log and diagnosis tooling needs no root. Concern: no abstract or artifact public yet and the evaluation likely targets production distributed services.

title: RPCShield: Defending Microservices Against Cascading Failures
note: Public repo describes RPCShield as a static analysis tool that infers fail-close versus fail-open RPC dependency relations - static analysis runs fine in user space with no Docker. Concerns: no abstract is public, and the end-to-end cascading-failure evaluation is on Uber production microservices; open microservice benchmarks normally assume Docker which is not installed here.

title: SANDHI: Fine-grained Merging for Memory Efficient Multi-Model Serving
note: Fine-grained merging of model weights to serve several models in less GPU memory. Memory-efficient multi-model serving on one 24 GB GPU is precisely this machine. Concern: no preprint or artifact found yet.

title: Scalable Context Orchestration for Serving LLMs Over Voice
note: Context-management middleware for voice LLM serving - explicitly models speaking rate, noise and packet loss in the context it builds. ASR plus 7-8B LLM plus TTS fits on one A5000 and the middleware itself is CPU-side. Concern: no artifact URL in the preprint.

title: Skill VM: Write Once, Run Everywhere Efficiently
note: SkVM compiles agent skills against model-harness capability profiles and JIT-solidifies them into code at runtime. Official SJTU-IPADS repo plus a project homepage. Pure user-space runtime. Concern: the evaluation spans eight LLMs and three harnesses, so reproduction is bounded by API cost rather than by hardware.

title: State-Aware Fuzzing of JavaScript Engines with LLM-Guided Instrumentation
note: State-aware JavaScript-engine fuzzing with LLM-guided instrumentation. Engine fuzzing is user space and CPU bound - 16 cores and 32 threads make fuzzing campaigns feasible, and coverage or bugs-per-hour is a clean testable hypothesis. Concerns: this is a testing and security tool rather than a resource-management system, no artifact public yet, and the LLM guidance costs API calls.

title: Tamias: Feedback-Guided Systematic Concurrency Exploration for Transparent Distributed System Fuzzing
note: Feedback-guided systematic concurrency exploration for transparent distributed-system fuzzing (Purdue - Fonseca and Yongle Zhang, groups that normally release artifacts). Distributed fuzzing of this kind is usually driven from one host with several processes. Concern: no abstract or artifact public yet.

title: Taming Dynamism on GPUs: Cross-SM Kernel Fusion via SM Cooperation and Just-in-Time Reduction
note: MorphKernel fuses multi-phase dynamic GPU operators (decode attention, MoE expert activation) across SMs with fine-grained SM synchronization. Single GPU by construction. Strong concern: third-party notes say the implementation uses TMA send and recv primitives and GPC-topology-aware communication, which are Hopper sm_90 features - the A5000 is Ampere sm_86 and has no TMA, so a port would be substantial.

title: TensorDex: A Compact, Tensor-Centric Storage System for Modern AI Models
note: TStore - tensor-level delta compression for model hubs, with learned pairwise compressibility prediction instead of lineage metadata. CPU plus disk workload, no GPU needed, and 257 GB free on /home is enough for a scaled-down model corpus. Concern: the paper studies petabyte-scale hubs so the corpus must be subsampled, and no artifact link appears in the preprint.

title: Testing Custom Control Planes Without the Cluster
note: The premise of the paper is testing Kubernetes-style custom control planes without provisioning a cluster, which is exactly the constraint this machine imposes. UCSC (Kuper and Quinn). Concern: no abstract or artifact is public yet, and Go would need a user-space install.

title: Validating Rust Compilers with Trait-Type Constraint Graph
note: Validating Rust compilers by constructing trait-type constraint graphs to generate valid but tricky programs. Compiler testing is user space and CPU bound; Rust installs per-user via rustup with no root. Concerns: this is a PL testing tool rather than a resource-management system, and no artifact is public yet.

title: MariusGNN: Resource-Efficient Out-of-Core Training of Graph Neural Networks
note: Explicitly a single-machine single-GPU out-of-core GNN training system whose whole thesis is that one GPU plus SSD beats multi-GPU baselines. Mature open-source repo with the EuroSys'23 artifact tag. Concern - the largest evaluated graphs need hundreds of GB of disk; 257 GB free means smaller graphs only.

title: FrozenHot Cache: Rethinking Cache Management for Modern Hardware
note: In-memory cache eviction/promotion scalability - pure user-space C++ library plus a trace-driven benchmark harness. Concern - the repo README asks for at least 32 physical cores per socket and around 100 GiB per NUMA node; this machine has 16 cores / 32 threads and 111 GiB free on one NUMA node so absolute numbers will be lower, and cache traces must be downloaded.

title: LogGrep: Fast and Cheap Cloud Log Storage by Exploiting both Static and Runtime Patterns
note: Log compression plus query engine, plain C, single machine, no root. Actively maintained repo with an explicit EuroSys'23 artifact statement plus a companion LogGrep-zstd repo. Concern - the Alibaba log datasets used in the paper may need to be sourced or substituted.

title: DyTIS: A Dynamic Dataset Targeted Index Structure Simultaneously Efficient for Search, Insert, and Scan
note: Learned/CDF-assisted in-memory index compared against learned indexes - user-space C++, single machine, Zenodo artifact mirrored on GitHub. Fits the machine with no privileged features.

title: DRAMHiT: A Hash Table Architected for the Speed of DRAM
note: User-space concurrent hash table built around software prefetching and batching; artifact evaluated, repo still active, has an AMD setup script. Serious concern - scripts/setup_amd.sh pins CPU frequency, enables explicit hugepages and disables hardware prefetchers, all of which need root or MSR access that is unavailable here; the reported numbers may not reproduce without them, so a scaled-down comparison would have to be justified.

title: Fast and Efficient Model Serving Using Multi-GPUs with Direct-Host-Access
note: DL inference serving with model provisioning from host memory - BERT/RoBERTa/GPT-2 class models fit in 24 GB. Best-artifact award, libTorch-based, no kernel or hypervisor dependency. Concern - the second of the two techniques (parallel model transmission across several GPUs) cannot be reproduced on one GPU; only the direct-host-access half scales down.

title: REFL: Resource-Efficient Federated Learning
note: Participant-selection and staleness-aware aggregation policies evaluated in a single-node FL simulator (FedScale lineage) - a pure user-space Python/PyTorch artifact. Concern - the paper's simulations use many worker processes and small vision/NLP models; client counts and model sizes will need scaling down to one A5000.

title: Viper: A Fast Snapshot Isolation Checker
note: Offline black-box checker over recorded transaction histories - a single-machine C++/SAT-solver pipeline with a companion ViperBench workload repo (figshare artifact also released). Performance of the BC-polygraph encoding and solver is exactly the kind of thing a 10-week improvement project can attack.

title: Effective Performance Issue Diagnosis with Value-Assisted Cost Profiling
note: vProf is a user-space profiler built on Clang/LLVM instrumentation plus a modified gprof SIGPROF sampler - notably it does not need hardware performance counters, which are blocked on this machine. Artifact on Zenodo plus a public GitHub mirror. Concern - reproducing the 15 real-world bugs means building four large applications from source.

title: WAFFLE: Exposing Memory Ordering Bugs Efficiently with Active Delay Injection
note: Active delay injection for concurrency bug detection - user-space instrumentation with no kernel, root or perf dependency. Concern - the implementation targets .NET/C#, so a user-space .NET SDK install is required, and the repo has very little activity beyond the artifact drop.

title: Model Checking Guided Testing for Distributed Systems
note: Mocket drives a TLA+ model checker to guide implementation-level testing of Java distributed systems (ZooKeeper and similar); everything runs as ordinary local JVM processes, no cluster needed. Concern - Java must be installed in user space, and state-space exploration time is the main cost, which is itself a plausible improvement target.

title: Groundhog: Efficient Request Isolation in FaaS
note: In-memory process snapshot/restore between FaaS invocations built entirely in user space on fork plus Linux soft-dirty page tracking - the authors state it needs no changes to the OS kernel, language runtimes or functions. Concern - the end-to-end evaluation drives OpenWhisk with Docker containers, which is not installed and cannot be installed without root; the snapshot/restore mechanism itself can still be benchmarked standalone. Repo link is the Zenodo artifact record - no public GitHub mirror was found.

title: With Great Freedom Comes Great Opportunity: Rethinking Resource Allocation for Serverless Functions
note: Resource-allocation policy for serverless functions - the released artifact bundles the serverless applications, the optimization algorithms, analysis notebooks and the full measured performance dataset, so the policy search can be re-run and improved offline on one machine. Concern - collecting fresh measurements would need a cloud FaaS provider; only the trace-driven half is reproducible locally. Repo link is the Zenodo record - no public GitHub mirror was found.

title: Omni-Paxos: Breaking the Barriers of Partial Connectivity
note: Borderline, kept per the borderline rule.
