The artifact is a user-space Rust library whose core is deliberately I/O-free and network-agnostic, so a replica group can be run as several processes (or in-process) on one host and partitions can be injected at the transport layer without root. Concern - every headline result in the paper (partial network partitions, reconfiguration I/O at the leader) was measured on a real multi-node cluster, which this machine cannot provide; a project would have to re-frame the claims as simulation.

title: Minuet: Accelerating 3D Sparse Convolutions on GPUs
note: Single-GPU sparse-convolution engine (segmented sort + binary search instead of hash tables, tile autotuning). Runs on one commodity GPU; point-cloud datasets are small. Concern - autotuned tile sizes were tuned for A100/V100 class GPUs so numbers will shift on an RTX A5000 with CUDA 11.8; that shift is itself a plausible improvement angle

title: Model Selection for Latency-Critical Inference Serving
note: RAMSIS generates model-selection/scheduling policies from a statistical model of query arrivals; policy generation is pure CPU work and serving uses a small ImageNet model zoo that fits 24 GB. Concern - the paper's worker pool is emulated across several GPUs; a single-GPU or simulated-worker scale-down is needed

title: CDMPP: A Device-Model Agnostic Framework for Latency Prediction of Tensor Programs
note: Learned cost model for tensor-program latency - a classic learned-component-inside-a-system paper. The released figshare dataset means the expensive cross-device profiling does not have to be redone; training the predictor fits one A5000. Concern - reproducing cross-device claims needs their published traces, not new hardware

title: Unison: A Parallel-Efficient and User-Transparent Network Simulation Kernel
note: Parallel discrete-event simulation kernel for ns-3 - entirely user-space CPU work, headline result is a 40x speedup on 24 cores, which maps well onto 16 cores / 32 threads. No root, no network hardware, distributed behaviour is simulated by construction

title: Orion: Interference-aware Fine-grained GPU Sharing for ML Applications
note: Intercepts CUDA kernel launches in user space and schedules operators from co-located clients on one GPU. Single-GPU by design and the whole point is contention on one device. Concern - built against a specific PyTorch/CUDA pairing, so pinning a working toolchain on driver 535 / CUDA 11.8 is the main build risk

title: Characterization and Reclamation of Frozen Garbage in Managed FaaS Workloads
note: Desiccant is a freeze-aware memory manager inside managed runtimes (JVM / Node.js) - user-space GC and heap work, buildable from source in $HOME. Concern - the FaaS harness around it likely assumes a container-based platform; the runtime changes themselves can be exercised with plain processes plus cgroup v2 memory limits

title: TraceUpscaler: Upscaling Traces to Evaluate Systems at High Load
note: The core contribution is a trace-transformation algorithm (decouple arrival timestamps from request payloads) - pure user-space trace processing, methodology directly reusable by other trace-driven projects. Concern - the published validation replays traces against real servers; on one host this becomes a loopback/local-process experiment at reduced load

title: Blox: A Modular Toolkit for Deep Learning Schedulers
note: Explicitly a simulator-plus-toolkit for DL cluster scheduling policies, validated by reproducing prior schedulers from traces. Cluster behaviour is simulated, so no multi-node hardware is needed and new policies are cheap to prototype - a near-ideal 10-week improvement target

title: Accelerating Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning With GeniBatch
note: A user-space compiler that rewrites PHE-based ML programs into batched (SIMD-packed) ciphertext programs; built on FATE, all CPU. Concern - cross-silo setting means two or more parties, but they can be run as separate processes on one host; the speedup claims are compute-bound, the traffic claims are not reproducible without a real link

title: WiseGraph: Optimizing GNN with Joint Workload Partition of Graph and Operations
note: GNN training framework with a joint graph/operator partitioning abstraction (gTask). The paper reports separate single-GPU numbers (2.04x) alongside multi-GPU, so the mechanism has a genuine single-GPU meaning. Concern - the largest graphs in the paper may not fit 24 GB, so a smaller dataset subset is needed

title: TTLs Matter: Efficient Cache Sizing with TTL-Aware Miss Ratio Curves and Working Set Sizes
note: Purely trace-driven MRC/WSS algorithms (TTL-aware SHARDS, TTL-aware HyperLogLog) - CPU and RAM only, no privileged access. 28 public cache traces with 113 billion accesses; disk space for the full trace set (~257 GB free) is the only real constraint

title: Trinity: A Fast Compressed Multi-attribute Data Store
note: Best-student-paper; a succinct multi-dimensional trie (MdTrie) plus query algorithms, all a user-space C++ data structure and store. Fits 125 GiB RAM comfortably; comparison baselines (columnar/NoSQL stores) all install without root

title: GMorph: Accelerating Multi-DNN Inference via Model Fusion
note: Graph-mutation search that fuses several pre-trained task-specific DNNs into one multi-task model for cheaper inference. Models are CNN/small-transformer scale and inference is single-GPU. Concern - the search phase is expensive (repeated fine-tuning), so the search budget may have to be cut down

title: LSGraph: A Locality-centric High-performance Streaming Graph Engine
note: Shared-memory streaming-graph engine (hierarchical indexed representation + locality-aware update). Single-machine multicore C++, competitors Terrace/Aspen/PaC-tree are also open source, so head-to-head comparison is cheap. Concern - the largest graphs used are multi-hundred-GB on disk; smaller SNAP graphs are a fine scale-down

title: FLOWS: Balanced MRC Profiling for Heterogeneous Object-Size Cache
note: Spatial-sampling MRC profiler that fixes byte-miss-ratio error for variable-object-size (CDN) traces. Trace-driven, user-space, no hardware requirements. Pairs naturally with TTLs Matter as a two-paper comparison target

title: On the Limitations of Carbon-Aware Temporal and Spatial Workload Shifting in the Cloud
note: Trace/simulation study of carbon-aware batch and interactive workload scheduling across 123 regions; the released artifact is a simulator plus carbon-intensity data, so it runs on CPU alone. Concern - it is a limitations study rather than a system, so it suits the "improve the policy / add nuance" angle more than a pure speedup project

title: ZKML: An Optimizing System for ML Inference in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
note: An optimizing compiler from TensorFlow graphs to halo2 ZK-SNARK circuits - a user-space Rust/Python compiler with a clear performance objective (gadget layout choices swing performance 24x). CPU-bound proving fits 16 cores / 125 GiB. Concern - proving even a distilled GPT-2 is memory- and time-hungry, so a 10-week project should target the smaller vision models

title: Efficient Auditing of Event-driven Web Applications
note: Karousos is a record-replay runtime for Node.js web applications; the improvement axis is the recording/replay overhead, which is a straightforward user-space runtime performance problem on a single host. Concern - framed as a security-auditing paper rather than a classic performance paper, so the hypothesis has to be written carefully around overhead

title: Empowering WebAssembly with Thin Kernel Interfaces
note: WALI extends a user-space Wasm engine to expose Linux syscalls directly - a pure user-space runtime contribution buildable in $HOME. AE badges Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - the paper also targets the Zephyr RTOS which is out of reach here, so only the Linux half is reproducible, and the build needs an LLVM and Rust toolchain installed via conda

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
note: KV-cache fusion with selective recompute for RAG prefill; vLLM-based prototype runs on one GPU and a 7B FP16 model fits in 24 GB. Concern - some paper configurations use larger models and multiple GPUs, so the study must be scaled down to 7B class models

title: DeltaZip: Efficient Serving of Multiple Full-Model-Tuned LLMs
note: Delta compression so many full-parameter fine-tuned models share one GPU; the system is explicitly single-GPU multi-tenant serving. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - custom CUDA quantization kernels must build for compute capability 8.6, and several fine-tuned 7B checkpoints are needed on the 257 GB of free disk

title: SpInfer: Leveraging Low-Level Sparsity for Efficient Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
note: Sparse LLM inference with a bitmap sparse format and SpMM kernel, evaluated on a single GPU with Tensor Cores. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - kernels are tuned for A100 and RTX 4090; they should compile for SM86 but performance tuning constants likely need revisiting, which is itself a plausible improvement angle

title: Empower Vision Applications with LoRA LMM
note: Heterogeneous LoRA adapter batching operator and adapter orchestration for multimodal serving, built on LightLLM; LLaVA-7B class models fit in 24 GB. Concern - evaluated on A100s, so the adaptive-tiling kernel may need retuning for Ampere SM86, and adapter generation needs a fine-tuning step

title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
note: Lookup-table mixed-precision GEMM for low-bit LLM inference entirely on the CPU - no GPU, no root, no kernel support needed, and 16 cores plus 125 GiB is a good target. Concern - the paper emphasizes ARM edge CPUs; the x86 AVX2 path is the weaker one, which is an opening for improvement rather than a blocker

title: Samoyeds: Accelerating MoE Models with Structured Sparsity Leveraging Sparse Tensor Cores
note: Dual-side structured sparsity kernels on Sparse Tensor Cores for MoE models; the A5000 is GA102 and does support 2:4 sparse Tensor Cores. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - MoE checkpoints must be small enough for 24 GB, so a scaled-down Mixtral-class or synthetic MoE is needed

title: Collaborative Text Editing with Eg-walker: Better, Faster, Smaller
note: Collaborative editing algorithm in Rust with a single-process benchmark harness measuring CPU time and memory only - zero hardware dependencies. AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - needs a Rust toolchain via rustup in $HOME, otherwise nothing on the exclusion list applies

title: LOFT: A Lock-free and Adaptive Learned Index with High Scalability for Dynamic Workloads
note: Lock-free learned index with non-blocking retraining; in-memory user-space C++ and a 32-thread scalability study matches this machine exactly. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper may use higher core counts than 16 cores and 32 threads, so scalability claims will have to be re-plotted at smaller thread counts

title: A House United Within Itself: SLO-Awareness for On-Premises Containerized ML Inference Clusters via Faro
note: SLO-aware cross-job resource allocation for ML inference driven by production traces; the optimizer and predictor are user-space Python. Concern - the reference stack is Ray Serve on Kubernetes and there is no root or Docker here, so the k8s layer must be replaced by a local Ray cluster or the paper's trace-driven simulator

title: OHMiner: An Overlap-centric System for Efficient Hypergraph Pattern Mining
note: CPU-only hypergraph pattern mining engine with a redundancy-free compiler; multi-core user space and fits comfortably in 125 GiB. Concern - some hypergraph datasets are large so memory footprint and download size should be checked before committing

title: CAPSys: Contention-aware task placement for data stream processing
note: Contention-aware operator placement plus interaction with the DS2 autoscaler for Flink; AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - the original setup is a multi-node Kubernetes Flink cluster, so on one host the placement problem can only be emulated with several TaskManagers and cgroup v2 CPU limits, which weakens the multi-node story

title: NeuStream: Bridging Deep Learning Serving and Stream Processing
note: Module-granularity batching and two-level scheduling for serving DNNs with control flow, including LLMs and diffusion models; diffusion pipelines and 7B LLMs fit one 24 GB GPU. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper's larger multi-GPU serving configurations must be scaled down to one GPU

title: Towards VM Rescheduling Optimization Through Deep Reinforcement Learning
note: Reinforcement learning policy for VM rescheduling evaluated on released industrial traces in a simulator; no cluster needed and one GPU is ample for the policy network. Concern - only that the trace dataset download should be confirmed; inference-time budget is the paper's own metric so it is measurable with wall-clock timers

title: Groot: Graph-Centric Row Reordering with Tree for Sparse Matrix Multiplications on Tensor Cores
note: Row reordering as a preprocessing pass for SpMM and SDDMM on Tensor Cores; single GPU with standard sparse matrix and GNN datasets. Concern - the repo has no README or description so build effort is unknown, and the kernels are written for SM80 and need an SM86 check

title: AlloyStack: A Library Operating System for Serverless Workflow Applications
note: User-space library OS that shares one address space across serverless workflow functions and isolates them with MPK; the target CPU reports the pku and ospke flags so unprivileged pkey_alloc works. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - needs a Rust toolchain, and the Firecracker or gVisor style baselines need KVM or root so only the LibOS side is reproducible

title: TUNA: Tuning Unstable and Noisy Cloud Applications
note: ML-based outlier removal and denoising to make autotuning converge under performance variability; the tuner is user-space Python and the noise characterization needs only timers. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the paper's premise is cloud noise, and this shared single machine has a different noise profile, which is itself a testable hypothesis

title: Solid State Drive Targeted Memory-Efficient Indexing for Universal I/O Patterns and Fragmentation Degrees
note: Memory-efficient approximate SSD index combining approximate indices with an LSM-tree - an algorithmic, trace-driven storage contribution. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - FTL work of this kind is usually evaluated on FEMU which needs KVM, so the repo must be confirmed to have a pure user-space simulator or trace-replay path

title: Garbage Collection Does Not Only Collect Garbage: Piggybacking-Style Defragmentation for Deduplicated Backup Storage
note: Piggybacking defragmentation onto garbage collection in a user-space deduplicated backup store, evaluated with public backup trace datasets on one host. Concern - the AE-listed GitHub repo currently returns 404 even though the paper carries the Artifacts Available badge, so availability must be re-checked; the backup datasets are also large relative to 257 GB free

title: Heimdall: Optimizing Storage I/O Admission with Extensive Machine Learning Pipeline
note: Learned I/O admission policy with a full ML pipeline; the paper states it is ready for user-level deployment and the evaluation is trace replay with a 28 KB model. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - the in-kernel and distributed deployment variants need root, so the project must stay with the user-level replay path

title: DPack: Efficiency-Oriented Privacy Budget Scheduling
note: Privacy budget scheduler formulated as a knapsack problem and evaluated purely in simulation on a synthetic workload derived from an Alibaba cluster trace; CPU only. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - none significant, which also means gains must come from better algorithms rather than systems engineering

title: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
note: RLHF dataflow framework combining single-controller and multi-controller execution; verl runs end to end on one GPU with 0.5B to 1.5B models using FSDP plus vLLM, so the API and scheduling layer can be studied at reduced scale. Concern - published results use 16 to 128 GPUs, so the 3D-HybridEngine resharding and placement search cannot be evaluated at paper scale on one A5000

title: Eva: Cost-Efficient Cloud-Based Cluster Scheduling
note: Cost-aware cloud cluster scheduler shipped with a large-scale trace-driven simulator alongside the AWS deployment; the simulator runs on a single machine. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - real-cloud validation is out of reach without an AWS budget, so any improvement has to be argued in simulation and with the paper's own cost model

title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
note: Multi-SLO LLM serving via speculative decoding - user-space serving system on GPU. Concern: AE artifact assumes 8x A100 and Docker with CUDA 12.4; would need scale-down to one 7-8B model plus draft model on the A5000 and a non-Docker build

title: Taming Latency-Memory Trade-Off in MoE-Based LLM Serving via Fine-Grained Expert Offloading
note: Fine-grained MoE expert offloading between GPU and CPU memory - exactly the single-GPU plus host-DRAM regime of this machine. 24 GB plus 125 GB RAM fits small MoE models

title: GeDES: GPU-Driven Discrete Event Network Simulator
note: GPU-driven discrete event simulator - single GPU, user space, artifact available. Useful as a simulation substrate and its own optimization target

title: TokenFlow: Responsive LLM Text Streaming Serving under Request Burst via Preemptive Scheduling
note: Preemptive request scheduling plus proactive KV cache swapping between GPU and CPU for text streaming - single GPU plus host memory is a natural scale-down. No official repo found so far

title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Sparsely-Activated Large Language Models on Resource-Constrained Devices
note: Federated fine-tuning of MoE LLMs on consumer-grade GPUs. Concern: multiple participants would have to be simulated sequentially on the one A5000 and no code release was found

title: LoRAFusion: Efficient LoRA Fine-Tuning for LLMs
note: LoRA fine-tuning kernel fusion and multi-adapter batching - the fusion part is a single-GPU kernel contribution. Concern: paper also targets multi-GPU pipelines that will not fit

title: STAlloc: Enhancing Memory Efficiency in Large-Scale Model Training with Spatio-Temporal Planning
note: GPU memory allocator that replaces the PyTorch caching allocator using spatio-temporal tensor lifetime planning - the allocator itself can be studied with small models on one GPU. Concern: paper targets large-scale training

title: LLMFolder: Revisiting Constant Folding in Large Language Models
note: Constant-folding style parameter reduction for LLMs by linearizing activations - pure user-space model or runtime transformation, 7-8B models fit in 24 GB. No code found yet

title: Ethane: Debloating State Data using Compact Trie for Account-based Blockchain
note: Compact-trie redesign of the Ethereum state trie - single-node user-space storage structure. Concerns: needs large Ethereum state or block traces which may strain the 257 GB free space, and no code release found

title: AdaGen: Workload-Adaptive Cluster Scheduler for Latency-Optimal LLM Inference Serving
note: Workload-adaptive scheduling of compute layouts for LLM serving instances - request scheduling logic that can be driven by traces or a small number of local instances. Concern: multi-instance cluster target, no code found

title: DROPS: Managing Serverless Resource Pools in Microsoft Azure Functions
note: Pre-warmed container pool sizing policies for Azure Functions driven by production allocation traces - trace-driven policy work explicitly in scope. Concern: check whether the artifact is a simulator or needs the real platform

title: FlexiQ: Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Latency/Accuracy Trade-Offs in Deep Neural Networks
note: Adaptive mixed-precision quantization with a GPU inference runtime - CV models fit easily on the A5000. Concerns: part of the prototype targets a custom NPU, and no code release was found

title: MFS: An Efficient Model Family Serving System for LLMs
note: Serving a family of same-architecture LLMs with shared and nested parameters - can be scaled down to the small members of a family. Concerns: the paper uses 70B-class models which do not fit, and no code was found

title: FlexiWalker: Extensible GPU Framework for Efficient Dynamic Random Walks with Runtime Adaptation
note: GPU framework for dynamic random walks - single GPU, user space, official repo at AIS-SNU/FlexiWalker

title: Carbon-Aware Continuous Learning for Sustainable Real-Time Machine Learning Analytics
note: Carbon-aware scheduling of continuous retraining for edge ML analytics - retraining knobs and carbon traces can be studied on one GPU. Concerns: carbon intensity traces plus edge server assumptions, and no code found

title: SAS: Sparse Attention Synthesizer for Efficient Language Model Inference
note: Synthesizer that generates sparse attention kernels for LLM inference - a single-GPU kernel-generation contribution and a very natural improvement target. FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere. No code found yet

title: Gopher: Efficient Dynamic Graph Pattern Mining via DAG-Driven Execution
note: Dynamic graph pattern mining engine with DAG-based common subexpression elimination - CPU-only user-space system that fits 16 cores and 125 GB RAM. Not in the AE results list, no repo found

title: Maya: Optimizing Deep Learning Training Workloads using GPU Runtime Emulation
note: Emulates the GPU runtime so unmodified training code can be profiled without real accelerators - this is precisely the kind of artifact that lets a one-GPU lab study large training configurations. No public repo found yet

title: CSnake: Detecting Self-Sustaining Cascading Failure via Causal Stitching of Fault Propagations
note: Fault injection framework that causally stitches single-fault injections to expose cascading failures - user-space instrumentation of JVM distributed systems that can be run as several processes on this host. Concern: target systems are distributed

title: MinatoLoader: Accelerating Machine Learning Training Through Efficient Data Preprocessing
note: General-purpose PyTorch data loader that removes preprocessing stalls - single GPU plus 16 CPU cores is exactly the setting, artifact available. Very strong fit

title: In-Production Characterization of an Open Source Serverless Platform and New Scaling Strategies
note: Serverless scaling strategies evaluated against released production traces - trace-driven policy work explicitly in scope, artifact and traces are public

title: FlashPS: Efficient Generative Image Editing with Mask-aware Caching and Scheduling
note: Mask-aware caching and scheduling for diffusion image editing - single-GPU serving system, artifact available, diffusion models fit in 24 GB

title: Efficient Multimodal Serving via Module Multiplexing
note: Module multiplexing scheduler for multimodal model serving - concurrent scheduling of encoder and LLM modules on one GPU is directly reproducible at small scale. No code found yet

title: CHARM: Chiplet Heterogeneity-Aware Runtime Mapping System
note: User-space runtime that maps tasks to chiplets - this host is a chiplet-based Zen3 Threadripper so the hardware target matches. Concerns: the technique very likely needs PMU-based cache and bandwidth monitoring which is blocked by perf_event_paranoid=3, and no code was found

title: 2DIO: Configurable and Cache-Accurate Trace Generation for Storage Benchmarking
note: Cache-accurate synthetic I/O trace generator with tunable hit-ratio curves - README shows a user-space C++ and Python build with no root requirement. Excellent fit for cache policy work

title: Automated End-to-End Model Serving with Cooperative Compilation and Scheduling
note: Cooperative compilation and scheduling of multiple kernel variants for model serving - single-GPU compiler plus runtime contribution. No code found yet

title: PiLLM: Resource-Efficient LLM Inference Using Workload Prediction
note: Workload prediction driving GPU and KV memory allocation for LLM serving - prediction and allocation policy can be studied on one GPU or from traces. No code found yet

title: High Throughput and Low Latency LLM Serving via Adaptive KV Caching
note: Adaptive partial-token KV caching with parallel recomputation and GPU-CPU offload - the central memory-versus-recompute trade-off is a single-GPU question. No code found yet

title: On-device Semantic Selection Made Low Latency and Memory Efficient with Monolithic Forwarding
note: Training-free early-exit ranking system for cross-encoder top-K selection - the inference technique runs fine on one GPU or CPU, artifact on Zenodo. Concern: paper targets edge hardware

title: MesaFS: An I/O-Efficient Metadata Service for Distributed File Systems
note: Metadata store that removes extra SSD writes from divided updates and layout ordering - the storage engine itself is single-node and user space. Concerns: framed as a distributed file system service and no code was found

title: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents
note: Declarative user-space OS interface layer for LLM computer-use agents - the abstraction and its runtime are user space. Concerns: evaluation needs GUI applications and paid LLM API calls, and no code was found

title: Bridging the GPU Utilization Gap: Predictive Multi-Dimensional Resource Scheduling for AI Workloads
note: Predictive multi-dimensional GPU resource scheduler - schedulers of this kind are normally evaluated with cluster traces and a simulator which fits here. Concerns: multi-tenant cluster target and no code found

title: PARD: Enhancing Goodput for Inference Pipeline via Proactive Request Dropping
note: Proactive request dropping to maximize goodput of multi-model inference pipelines - a scheduling policy that can be evaluated on one GPU or in simulation. No code found yet

title: Low-Compilation-Cost Register Allocation in LLVM-Based Binary Translation
note: Register allocation algorithm that cuts compilation cost in LLVM-based dynamic binary translation - user-space translator work. Concerns: the host architecture is probably not x86-64 so the evaluation may need non-x86 hardware, and no code was found

title: Reducing the GPU Memory Bottleneck with Lossless Compression for ML
note: Lossless compression of ML tensors to cut PCIe transfer time - single GPU plus PCIe is exactly the setting this machine has, artifact available. Strong fit

title: Once Rolling Hashing is Enough: Exploiting Rolling Hash Reuse in Delta Compression
note: Rolling hash reuse across the stages of delta compression for backup storage - CPU-only user-space algorithm, ideal for the 16-core host. No code release found yet

title: Accurate and Ultra-Fast Launch-Time Validation of Idempotency for GPU Kernels
note: Launch-time validation of GPU kernel idempotency - user-space analysis on a single GPU, self-contained. No code found yet

title: TCO-driven Storage Provisioning for Exascale Data Centers
note: TCO model and optimal workload-to-storage-class solver for exascale storage - the artifact is a self-contained user-space model and solver. Concern: it is a modeling and telemetry study rather than a running storage system

title: FicusDB: Scalable Multi-Versioned Authenticated Archival Storage
note: Log-structured multi-versioned archival storage engine for copy-on-write tries with an Ethereum StateDB replay harness - single-node user-space storage engine, implementation is in the artifact repo

title: SwiftFL: Enabling Speculative Training for On-Device Federated Deep Learning
note: Speculative training with gradient prediction for federated learning - the artifact is built on FederatedScope and installs through conda, so clients can be simulated on one host. Concern: paper frames it as on-device FL

title: A Logically Disaggregated Cache for Replicated Storage Systems
note: Disaggregating the embedded caches of storage replicas into one logical cache - artifact implements LDC in a key-value store, so replicas can be run as several processes here. Concern: cross-replica network effects are lost on a single host

title: Million-Scale Text-to-Video Retrieval with Hyperdimensional Computing
note: Binary hyperdimensional video representation with a GPU Hamming-search inverted index - single GPU search system. Concerns: million-scale corpora may strain the 257 GB of free disk, and no code was found

title: PointShuffler: Accelerating Point Cloud Neural Networks on General-Purpose GPUs
note: GPU-friendly point cloud network inference - README confirms CUDA 11.8, PyTorch 2.1 and PyTorch CUDA extensions on a single GPU, pre-trained weights included. Strong fit

title: TAO: Tolerance-Aware Optimistic Verification for Floating-Point Neural Networks
note: Tolerance-aware optimistic verification of floating-point neural network execution - user-space verification running against a local GPU. No code found yet

title: Rose: Reproducing External-Fault-Induced Failures in Distributed Systems with Lightweight Instrumentation
note: Lightweight user-space tracing plus fault schedule generation to reproduce external-fault failures - the instrumentation and replay can run against systems started as local processes, artifact available. Concern: targets distributed systems

title: SecretFlow-SPU: A Performant and User-Friendly Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
note: Frontend compiler plus backend runtime that lowers ordinary JAX/TF ML programs to an MPC IR - a user-space ML compiler/runtime, exactly the ml-systems bucket. All parties can be run as separate processes on one host and the artifact is AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the contribution is heavily cryptographic rather than architectural; the WAN results use link emulation (tc/netem) which needs root, so only LAN/localhost numbers are reproducible here.

title: GLogS: Interactive Graph Pattern Matching Query At Large Scale
note: User-space declarative query compiler plus cost-based optimizer on top of a dataflow engine; the headline 51x-over-Neo4j result is a single-machine number, so the optimizer can be studied without a cluster. Rust/Java toolchain is installable in user space. Concerns: the scalability half of the evaluation is distributed (16 machines) and cannot be reproduced; large LDBC datasets need tens of GB of the ~257 GB free.

title: SOWalker: An I/O-Optimized Out-of-Core Graph Processing System for Second-Order Random Walks
note: Single-machine, out-of-core, user-space C++ system; the contribution (walk matrix, benefit-aware I/O model, block-set walk updating) is pure I/O scheduling policy on local NVMe, which is exactly what this machine can measure with wall-clock timers. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the repo moved from the AE-listed tzphh/SOWalker (now 404) to Teamb507/SOWalker; billion-edge graphs need substantial scratch space.

title: TiDedup: A New Distributed Deduplication Architecture for Ceph
note: Deduplication (selective crawling, content-defined chunking, shared reference back pointers) is squarely in the storage topic, and Ceph OSDs are user-space daemons that vstart.sh can run as a single-node cluster without root. Merged into the Ceph mainline, so the code is unambiguously released. Concerns: building Ceph is a heavy source build whose install-deps.sh normally wants apt/root - every dependency would have to be satisfied via conda or vendored submodules; this is the main feasibility risk. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/ssdohammer-sl/ceph/tree/tidedup .

title: TC-GNN: Bridging Sparse GNN Computation and Dense Tensor Cores on GPUs
note: Single-GPU CUDA/Tensor-Core kernels plus a sparse-graph-translation pass, integrated with PyTorch - no multi-GPU, no root, and Ampere TCUs are present on the RTX A5000 (cc 8.6). AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: evaluated on A100/RTX3090; TF32/FP16 TCU paths work on Ampere but any newer-CUDA-only kernels would need a conda CUDA toolkit on driver 535.

title: Bridging the Gap between Relational OLTP and Graph-based OLAP (GART)
note: In-memory user-space system; the core contributions (mutable CSR, coarse-grained MVCC versioning, flexible property store) are data-structure/locality work measurable with wall-clock timing on one node. Code released both as SJTU-IPADS/vegito branch gart (AE link) and the maintained GraphScope/GART. Concerns: depends on the large Vineyard/GraphScope stack; LDBC SNB dataset generation is time-consuming.

title: Explore Data Placement Algorithm for Balanced Recovery Load Distribution
note: The contribution is an NP-hardness formulation plus a greedy data-placement algorithm - an algorithmic storage-placement result that can be evaluated by simulation/microbenchmark on one machine. Two artifacts released: rcstor/greedy_microbenchmark (the placement microbenchmark) and rcstor/rcstor (the full system); AE Available+Functional. Concerns: the end-to-end recovery-speed numbers came from a real multi-disk cluster, so only the simulated/microbenchmark half is reproducible here.

title: Luci: Loader-based Dynamic Software Updates for Off-the-shelf Shared Objects
note: A drop-in user-space dynamic linker/loader that hot-patches unmodified Debian/Ubuntu shared objects - no kernel changes, no root, and the target distro family (Debian 12) matches the machine. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced, eval harness at https://github.com/luci-project/eval-atc23. Concerns: the AE workflow ships an Ubuntu VM image (ubuntu.ova) for convenience; without KVM that path is unusable, so Luci would have to be run natively on Debian 12 instead.

title: MELF: Multivariant Executables for a Heterogeneous World
note: Purely binary-level (linker plus loader) mechanism for per-function, per-thread compile-time variants; the case studies are SQLite, memcached and MariaDB, all user-space workloads this machine runs well. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the heterogeneous-ISA case study assumes CPUs with differing extension sets - on a single Threadripper the ISA-adaptation experiment can only be emulated, so an improvement would have to target the security/debug-instrumentation isolation use case.

title: zpoline: a system call hook mechanism based on binary rewriting
note: Explicitly advertises "no kernel change and no additional kernel module" - a pure user-space binary-rewriting mechanism, the best possible match for a no-root machine. Code is a small, well-known, actively maintained C repo. Concerns: the trampoline is instantiated at virtual address 0, which requires vm.mmap_min_addr=0; that sysctl needs root, so the team must check whether the documented --enable-mmap-min-addr-workaround/libzphook path suffices or whether this is a blocker.

title: Avoiding the Ordering Trap in Systems Performance Measurement
note: Not a pure measurement study: OrderSage is a released, reusable user-space Python tool that randomizes trial order and runs statistical order-dependence tests, which is directly usable (and improvable) on this machine. Paper artifact at https://github.com/ordersage/paper-artifact. Concerns: the headline empirical result (2.3M measurements over 1,700 CloudLab servers) is not reproducible on one host - an improvement would have to target the tool's statistics/methodology, and validating it on a single shared machine introduces its own noise.

title: Calcspar: A Contract-Aware LSM Store for Cloud Storage with Low Latency Spikes
note: LSM key-value store (RocksDB-derived): fluctuation-aware cache plus a congestion-aware IOPS allocator - user-space C++, no root, and LSM stores are explicitly in the storage topic. Concerns: the premise is Amazon EBS IOPS-contract latency variance, so reproducing it locally requires emulating cloud-storage latency (e.g. an injection layer or a FUSE shim over local NVMe - /dev/fuse is usable here); AE badge is Available only, so build effort is unverified.

title: Adaptive Online Cache Capacity Optimization via Lightweight Working Set Size Estimation at Scale (Cuki)
note: Core artifact is a sketch-like data structure for online working-set-size / item-repetition-ratio / miss-ratio-curve estimation, plus an adaptive cache-capacity tuner - trace-driven cache work, exactly the caching topic, and AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the end-to-end numbers use Alluxio plus Presto (extra repos Cuki-Artifact-Alluxio, Cuki-Artifact-Presto) which are JVM-heavy and normally multi-node; the standalone estimator is trivially runnable on traces, which is the realistic project scope.

title: Arbitor: A Numerically Accurate Hardware Emulation Tool for DNN Accelerators
note: An ML-compiler-based emulator that runs on general-purpose GPUs - it deliberately avoids needing accelerator hardware, and the topic (ML compiler / runtime tooling) is in scope. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the sensitivity study trains ResNet/Transformer/RNN/GNN models; on one 24 GB A5000 only scaled-down models and shortened schedules are feasible, and emulated low-precision arithmetic is slow.

title: Overcoming the Memory Wall with CXL-Enabled SSDs
note: Despite the CXL title, the artifact is MQSim_CXL - a pure user-space C++ simulator driven by real application memory traces. scope.md explicitly allows memory-tiering / far-memory work "studied in user space or by simulation", and no CXL hardware is touched. AE Available+Functional. Concerns: results are only as good as the simulator's fidelity, so an improvement paper has to argue about the model, not measured hardware; trace collection for new workloads would need a tracer that does not rely on perf.

title: LLFree: Scalable and Optionally-Persistent Page-Frame Allocation
note: Allocator design (lock- and log-free, cache-friendly, anti-fragmentation) is squarely in the memory topic, and the core LLFree implementation is a standalone Rust library benchmarked in user space; 16C/32T is enough to show the scaling claims. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: the strongest claims (beating Linux's buddy allocator, memory-compaction page-movement counts) require the patched-kernel variant, which is impossible without root - a project here is limited to the user-space allocator benchmarks.

title: Beware of Fragmentation: Scheduling GPU-Sharing Workloads with Fragmentation Gradient Descent
note: scope.md explicitly allows cluster/GPU schedulers "evaluated with simulators or traces": the paper's 6,200-GPU results come from a Go-based Kubernetes scheduler *simulator* replaying public Alibaba traces, which runs as a normal user process on one machine. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: Go must be installed via conda; the real-cluster deployment half of the paper is not reproducible, and simulator-only results weaken an "improvement" claim unless the fragmentation metric itself is the target.

title: Towards Iterative Relational Algebra on the GPU
note: Single-GPU CUDA library: open-addressing hash table, operator fusion, two deduplication variants, evaluated on transitive closure against cuDF and Souffle. No multi-GPU, no root, no exotic hardware. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: it is a short paper, so the design space is small; the baselines (cuDF via RAPIDS, Souffle) need conda/source installs, and large relations can exceed 24 GB of GPU memory.

title: VectorVisor: A Binary Translation Scheme for Throughput-Oriented GPU Acceleration
note: A user-space WebAssembly-to-GPU binary translator/runtime (continuations for syscalls and recursion, register-file and bandwidth exploitation) running on a single commodity GPU. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: written in Rust (conda install needed) and evaluated on AWS GPU VMs for the throughput-per-dollar claim - on one A5000 only the raw throughput comparison is meaningful, not the cost metric.

title: Starburst: A Cost-aware Scheduler for Hybrid Cloud
note: Cluster/cloud-bursting scheduling policy driven by production traces with a released simulator; waiting-budget policy can be re-studied and improved by simulation on one machine. Concern: the paper also uses a 32-GPU private cluster and real cloud spend, so only the simulator half is reproducible here

title: StreamBox: A Lightweight GPU SandBox for Serverless Inference Workflow
note: GPU sandbox for serverless DNN inference built purely on CUDA streams and user-space memory management - single GPU, no root needed, fits the A5000. Concern: needs a working serverless runtime and a CUDA version compatible with driver 535

title: Fast Inference for Probabilistic Graphical Models
note: Parallel user-space inference engine for probabilistic graphical models, CPU-only C++ with OpenMP; builds and runs entirely in user space on 16 cores, clear speedup metric to improve

title: Balancing Analysis Time and Bug Detection: Daily Development-friendly Bug Detection in Linux
note: LLVM-based bug checker that runs entirely in user space with an explicit analysis-time versus bugs-found tradeoff, an obvious target for improvement; compiling the Linux source as input needs no root. Concern: program analysis rather than a resource-management topic, so topic fit is a judgement call

title: Kivi: Verification for Cluster Management
note: Model checker for Kubernetes controllers and configurations; the artifact is a user-space Python plus model-checking toolchain and the state-space reduction is a clean performance target. Concern: verification tooling rather than a classic OS topic, and the released artifact only earned the Available badge

title: Metis: Fast Automatic Distributed Training on Heterogeneous GPUs
note: The released component is the CPU-only auto-planner plus cost model and profiler, which can be run and improved on one machine against recorded or synthetic device profiles. Concern: end-to-end validation needs a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster, so an improvement would have to be argued from the planner and cost model

title: FwdLLM: Efficient Federated Finetuning of Large Language Models with Perturbed Inferences
note: Backpropagation-free federated fine-tuning: the core mechanism is perturbed forward inference plus load allocation, which can be simulated as many clients on one GPU with small models. Concern: the headline results use mobile devices and NPUs that we do not have, so scale-down to a simulated federation on the A5000 is required

title: SimEnc: A High-Performance Similarity-Preserving Encryption Approach for Deduplication of Encrypted Docker Images
note: Deduplication and compression of container image layers - the artifact is a user-space Go program operating on layer tarballs, and dedup ratio plus throughput are directly improvable. Concern: Docker is not installed, so images have to be pulled through the registry HTTP API rather than the Docker CLI

title: Pecan: Cost-Efficient ML Data Preprocessing with Automatic Transformation Ordering and Hybrid Placement
note: Input-pipeline preprocessing: the transformation-reordering half is a single-node tf.data question and directly testable here. Concern: the placement half assumes disaggregated remote CPU workers and the original evaluation runs on cloud VMs/TPUs, so the hybrid-placement results cannot be reproduced

title: MAGPY: Compiling Eager Mode DNN Programs by Monitoring Execution States
note: Guard and graph-capture design for eager-mode PyTorch programs - a pure user-space compiler/runtime that needs one GPU at most, with graph-completeness and speedup as crisp metrics to beat against TorchDynamo

title: Quant-LLM: Accelerating the Serving of Large Language Models via FP6-Centric Algorithm-System Co-Design on Modern GPUs
note: FP6/arbitrary-bit-width weight-only quantization kernels built on FP16 Tensor Cores, so they run on Ampere sm_86 with CUDA 11.8 - exactly our toolchain. Concern: the paper serves LLaMA-70B on a 40-80 GB GPU, so experiments must scale down to 7B-13B models on 24 GB

title: Evaluating Chiplet-based Large-Scale Interconnection Networks via Cycle-Accurate Packet-Parallel Simulation
note: The artifact is a user-space parallel discrete-event simulator whose headline claim is simulation speed, which is measurable and improvable on 16 cores with no special hardware. Concern: the subject matter is chiplet interconnect architecture rather than systems software, so topic fit needs an audit decision

title: Removing Obstacles before Breaking Through the Memory Wall: A Close Look at HBM Errors in the Field
note: The artifact ships both the released HBM error dataset and the hierarchical failure-prediction pipeline, so it is a fully trace-driven learned-prediction study that runs on CPU here. Concern: it is a field study, so an improvement has to come from better prediction models or features rather than from a system change

title: Data Caching for Enterprise-Grade Petabyte-Scale OLAP
note: Local SSD cache for petabyte-scale OLAP - admission, eviction, quota and page-affinity policies are exactly the caching topic and can be studied trace-driven on one NVMe disk. Concern: the paper is a deployed-systems experience report with no dedicated artifact; the implementation it describes is the local cache inside Alluxio open source, so the mapping from paper to code has to be verified

title: TileClipper: Lightweight Selection of Regions of Interest from Videos for Traffic Surveillance
note: Video-analytics pipeline that selects tiles by bitrate before sending frames to a detector; artifact is user-space Python plus Kvazaar and YOLOv5 and runs on one GPU, with a clear bandwidth-versus-accuracy tradeoff to improve. Concern: the live-deployment numbers used Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano edge devices that we do not have

title: CrossMapping: Harmonizing Memory Consistency in Cross-ISA Binary Translation
note: Memory-consistency primitive mapping in QEMU dynamic binary translation; QEMU TCG needs no KVM and no root, and the ARMv8-to-x86 and RISC-V-to-x86 directions run on our x86 host with PARSEC. Concern: the x86-to-ARMv8 and x86-to-RISC-V directions need ARM or RISC-V hosts we do not have, so only half the configuration matrix is reachable

title: Exploit both SMART Attributes and NAND Flash Wear Characteristics to Effectively Forecast SSD-based Storage Failures in Clusters
note: Learned SSD failure forecasting whose artifact ships both the SMART/flash-wear datasets and the network, so the whole study is a CPU or single-GPU trace-driven experiment. Concern: the artifact is distributed partly as a container image, which must be ported to conda since Docker is unavailable

title: Centimani: Enabling Fast AI Accelerator Selection for DNN Training with a Novel Performance Predictor
note: Learned performance and memory predictor for DNN training - the model and its microkernel benchmarks are user-space Python and a predictor can be retrained and validated for the A5000. Concern: the paper validates across four accelerator types we do not have, and the repository looks like the anonymized artifact containing mainly microkernels, so completeness should be checked

title: Efficient Large Graph Processing with Chunk-Based Graph Representation Model
note: I/O-efficient out-of-core graph engine on NVMe SSDs - a pure user-space C++ system on hardware we have, with I/O amplification and runtime as improvable metrics. Concern: the largest graphs in the paper approach or exceed our 257 GB of free space, so the study must use the smaller datasets

title: JENGA: Enhancing LLM Long-Context Fine-tuning with Contextual Token Sparsity
note: LLM fine-tuning system exploiting contextual token sparsity to cut activation memory; artifact minimum is a single A800 or A40 GPU so smaller OPT/Llama models fit the 24 GB A5000. Concern: scalability experiments used 4x 4090 and long-context runs may need memory scale-down

title: GeneralSparse: Bridging the Gap in SpMM for Pruned Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
note: SpMM kernel generator for pruned LLM inference; evaluated single-GPU on A100 (Ampere, CUDA 12.1) which matches the A5000. Concern: 7B-class models in FP16 fit but larger ones need scale-down

title: The Koala Benchmarks for the Shell: Characterization and Implications
note: Shell benchmark suite plus automation and characterization infrastructure; pure user-space CPU workloads, no root needed. Concern: it is a benchmark artifact, so an improvement project would target shell runtimes measured with it

title: HotRAP: Hot Record Retention and Promotion for LSM-trees with Tiered Storage
note: RocksDB-based LSM-tree with hot-record promotion on tiered storage; evaluated on one 8-vCPU instance with a fast NVMe plus a slow disk. Concern: the slow tier was AWS gp3 and would have to be emulated on the local NVMe

title: Mitigating Resource Usage Dependency in Sorting-based KV Stores on Hybrid Storage Devices via Operation Decoupling
note: DecouKV decouples LSM flush/compaction operations to reduce write stalls on hybrid devices; artifact is RocksDB/MatrixKV/ADOC plus YCSB on a single server. Concern: the fast tier was Intel Optane DCPMM which is unavailable - would need NVMe-vs-SATA emulation

title: Torpor: GPU-Enabled Serverless Computing for Low-Latency, Resource-Efficient Inference
note: Serverless GPU inference with late binding and model swapping between host memory and GPU; core mechanism is per-GPU and the machine has 125 GiB host RAM for the model pool. Concern: paper used a 4-GPU node and API redirection depends on the CUDA runtime version

title: Toppings: CPU-Assisted, Rank-Aware Adapter Serving for LLM Inference
note: CPU-assisted rank-aware LoRA adapter serving built on LightLLM; Llama2-7B is served on a single GPU and the CPU-assist path suits a 16-core/32-thread host. Concern: no artifact URL appears in the paper although the ATC25 AE page awarded Available/Functional/Reproduced - repo not found by search

title: QFactory: Accelerating Quantized Large Language Model Serving with Qtile Graphs
note: Compilation framework generating quantized LLM dequantization kernels; single-GPU kernel work and 4-bit weights help fit 24 GB. Concern: headline kernel numbers were measured on H100, so Ampere retuning is needed and no FP8 path is available

title: Voltrix: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on Tensor Cores with Asynchronous and Balanced Kernel Optimization
note: Tensor-core SpMM kernel with asynchronous pipelining and load balancing; single-GPU CUDA kernel work, Ampere supports cp.async and FA2-style pipelining. Concern: evaluated on an 80 GB A100, so the larger graph datasets must be trimmed to 24 GB

title: LITESHIELD: Secure Containers via Lightweight, Composable Userspace μKernel Services
note: Secure containers built from composable user-space microkernel services serving most Linux syscalls in user space; the LiteShield side needs no root. Concern: baselines (Kata, KVM) need virtualization that is unavailable, so comparisons would shrink to gVisor-class user-space baselines

title: CrossPipe: Towards Optimal Pipeline Schedules for Cross-Datacenter Training
note: Solver-based and greedy pipeline-schedule optimizer with an execution engine that separates scheduling from execution, so the schedule optimization can be studied in simulation. Concern: hardware evaluation used 4x GH200, so only the solver/simulation half is reproducible here

title: SpaceExit: Enabling Efficient Adaptive Computing in Space with Early Exits
note: Early-exit adaptive inference plus resource scheduling for satellite imagery; the artifact lists an ordinary CUDA GPU (tested on RTX 4090) and a multi-core CPU. Concern: the paper also uses a Jetson Orin Nano testbed emulating CubeSat hardware that cannot be reproduced

title: Revealing Floating-Point Accumulation Orders in Software/Hardware Implementations
note: User-space testing tool that reveals floating-point accumulation orders in BLAS/GPU implementations; runs entirely in user space on CPU and one GPU. Concern: it is a diagnostic tool rather than a resource-management system, so an improvement hypothesis would be about coverage or test cost

title: IRHash: Efficient Multi-Language Compiler Caching by IR-Level Hashing
note: Multi-language compilation cache keyed on LLVM IR hashes; CPU-only build-system experiments, and clang/LLVM is installable per-user through conda. Concern: needs a sizeable disk budget for build corpora on the ~257 GB free volume

title: PathWeaver: A High-Throughput Multi-GPU System for Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Multi-GPU graph-based ANNS; section 5.3 explicitly reports single-GPU gains for ghost staging and the direction-guided techniques, so there is a meaningful single-GPU scale-down. Concern: pipelining-based path extension is inherently multi-GPU and billion-scale datasets exceed 24 GB

title: Swift: Fast Performance Tuning with GAN-Generated Configurations
note: Bayesian-optimization tuner that uses a GAN to generate candidate configurations for big-data systems; the tuner itself is user-space Python and can be driven by surrogates or traces. Concern: the paper tuned 4-node Flink and 8-node Spark clusters, so on-machine evaluation must use local-mode or simulated targets

title: SAVE: Software-Implemented Fault Tolerance for Model Inference against GPU Memory Bit Flips
note: Software fault tolerance that splits model inference state across reliable and unreliable GPU memory; single-GPU, user-space bit-flip injection, and it was already evaluated on consumer-class GPUs including a 4090. Concern: the reliable-memory abstraction assumes accelerator features that may need emulation on the A5000

title: Identifying and Analyzing Pitfalls in GNN Systems
note: Reproduction-oriented analysis of accuracy and memory pitfalls in GNN systems, explicitly framed around single-GPU systems and run on one A100 40 GB. Concern: the paper only points at the lab GitHub org rather than a named GraphPy repo, so the exact artifact needs identification

title: Resource Multiplexing in Tuning and Serving Large Language Models
note: Spatial-temporal multiplexing of LLM fine-tuning and inference on the same GPUs; the smallest configuration is Llama-8B on RTX 3090-class 24 GB GPUs which matches the A5000. Concern: several experiments use 4 GPUs and 70B models that will not fit. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/llm-db/llmstation/tree/atc25-artifact .

title: Colocating ML Inference and Training with Fast GPU Memory Handover
note: Colocates inference and training on the same GPU with millisecond-scale memory handover; the core mechanism is intra-GPU spatial sharing and the paper used 16 GB V100s, so 24 GB is ample. Concern: some experiments span 4 GPUs and the memory-reclaim hooks are tied to a specific PyTorch/CUDA version

title: Transparent GPU Sharing in Container Clouds for Deep Learning Workloads
note: OS-layer GPU sharing for DL training that intercepts CUDA driver API calls from user space so two jobs can share the single A5000 - Concern: the artifact is packaged for Docker plus Kubernetes which are unavailable here so it must be ported to plain processes and the transparent-unified-memory path may need driver privileges

title: BGL: GPU-Efficient GNN Training by Optimizing Graph Data I/O and Preprocessing
note: GNN data-loading bottleneck work whose core ideas (feature cache engine plus sampling-order co-design) are a single-GPU-testable caching policy question - Concern: built for multi-GPU multi-node training on billion-edge graphs so it needs scale-down to one GPU and OGB-sized graphs and it pins DGL v0.5.0 which must be built from source

title: Zeus: Understanding and Optimizing GPU Energy Consumption of DNN Training
note: Energy-vs-time tradeoff for recurring DNN training jobs measured with just-in-time profiling on a single GPU - Concern: setting GPU power limits through NVML normally requires root so only the batch-size and job-level knobs may be reachable without the Zeus daemon - repo moved from SymbioticLab/Zeus to ml-energy/zeus

title: The Benefit of Hindsight: Tracing Edge-Cases in Distributed Systems
note: Always-on retroactive distributed tracing implemented as a user-space C library plus agent needing no root perf counters or eBPF - Concern: the reference evaluation drives DeathStarBench microservices under Docker across several nodes so it must be re-hosted as multiple processes on one machine - code lives on MPI-SWS GitLab not GitHub

title: Shockwave: Fair and Efficient Cluster Scheduling for Dynamic Adaptation in Machine Learning
note: ML cluster scheduler whose main evaluation arm is a trace-driven discrete-event simulator that runs entirely on one CPU machine - Concern: the physical-cluster half of the paper used dozens of GPUs so only the simulation results are reproducible or improvable here

title: ModelKeeper: Accelerating DNN Training via Automated Training Warmup
note: Training warmup by transforming weights of previously trained models - the matching plus transformation logic is CPU work and warm-started training of small models fits one 24 GB GPU - Concern: the paper uses a large shared cluster and a big model zoo so the zoo and datasets must be scaled down

title: SPEEDEX: A Scalable, Parallelizable, and Economically Efficient Decentralized EXchange
note: Single-machine parallel batch transaction-processing engine in C++ whose 48-core numbers scale down naturally to 16 cores and 32 threads with no special hardware - Concern: the domain is a decentralized exchange rather than classic OS and the build pulls a large C++ dependency tree that must go into HOME

title: Boggart: Towards General-Purpose Acceleration of Retrospective Video Analytics
note: Retrospective video analytics accelerator combining classical CV indices with sparing CNN invocation - runs as user-space Python on one GPU - Concern: needs large video corpora to be downloaded into the 257 GB of free space and depends on older CUDA-era PyTorch and OpenCV builds

title: Gemel: Model Merging for Memory-Efficient, Real-Time Video Analytics at the Edge
note: Model merging to cut GPU memory for concurrently served edge vision models - a pure user-space memory-management question that fits one 24 GB GPU - Concern: the target is memory-starved edge boxes so the memory budget has to be deliberately constrained on an A5000 and the repo is a research prototype

title: Fast, Approximate Vector Queries on Very Large Unstructured Datasets
note: Vector query engine that builds a per-query error-latency profile - the single-worker path is the interesting mechanism and runs in user space - Concern: headline numbers use DEEP1B on four c5.metal instances so experiments must be scaled to SIFT or GIST million-to-100M datasets to fit 125 GiB RAM and 257 GB disk

title: Arya: Arbitrary Graph Pattern Mining with Decomposition-based Sampling
note: Approximate graph pattern mining that the paper explicitly claims runs on a single machine with a configurable error-latency profile - Concern: the 5-billion-edge single-machine experiments exceed this machine's RAM and free disk so smaller graphs are required and the 32-server distributed arm is out of reach

title: SelfTune: Tuning Cluster Managers
note: Reinforcement-learning auto-tuner for configuration parameters inside cluster managers - the released library is pure Python and C# and runs in user space - Concern: every evaluated target (Kubernetes VPA Azure FaaS DeathStarBench) needs containers or cloud so a locally runnable tunable system must be substituted

title: CausalSim: A Causal Framework for Unbiased Trace-Driven Simulation
note: Causal correction for trace-driven simulation with released code and public Puffer RCT data - fully CPU and single-GPU friendly and a Best Paper - Concern: it is closer to a data-science pipeline than a running system so an improvement hypothesis must target the tensor-completion method or the ABR simulator and the trace download is large

title: DOTE: Rethinking (Predictive) WAN Traffic Engineering
note: Deep-learning replacement for demand prediction in WAN traffic engineering - training and evaluation are entirely offline on released topologies and traces and fit one A5000 - Concern: the domain is network traffic engineering rather than core OS and reproducing the LP baselines needs a solver such as Gurobi

title: Push-Button Reliability Testing for Cloud-Backed Applications with Rainmaker
note: User-space REST fault-injection tool for cloud-backed applications needing no root kernel or hardware support - Concern: the .NET toolchain must be installed under HOME and reproducing the reported bugs needs cloud SDK targets or local emulators such as Azurite rather than real cloud accounts

title: Channel-Aware 5G RAN Slicing with Customizable Schedulers
note: Channel-aware RAN slicing scheduler implemented entirely inside an open-source user-space RAN simulator so the whole evaluation runs on this machine with no radios - Concern: the resource being scheduled is 5G spectrum rather than CPU or GPU which stretches the scheduling topic key and the CQI trace files are large

title: Fast Vector Query Processing for Large Datasets Beyond GPU Memory with Reordered Pipelining
note: GPU-accelerated billion-scale ANN vector search; the paper itself uses a single A100 and streams vectors from host RAM, so the mechanism is single-GPU. User-space CUDA on a Faiss fork. Concern: paper used 40 GB GPU and 1152 GB host RAM for billion-scale sets - on 24 GB GPU plus 125 GiB RAM and 257 GB free disk the study must scale down to 100M-scale datasets. CUDA toolkit newer than 11.8 would need a conda install.

title: MadEye: Boosting Live Video Analytics Accuracy with Adaptive Camera Configurations
note: Live video analytics that adapts PTZ camera orientation; the released repo is trace-driven simulation code plus collected per-orientation datasets, and server-side inference (YOLO-class models) fits the A5000. Concerns: original setup needs physical PTZ cameras and Mahimahi link emulation (Mahimahi needs setuid/root), so work must stay inside the released simulator; datasets are hosted on Dropbox which is an availability risk.

title: Characterization of Large Language Model Development in the Datacenter
note: Six-month LLM development trace from a 2048-GPU datacenter is openly released (109 MB on GitHub, ~80 GB full set on Hugging Face) and supports trace-driven scheduling and failure-recovery simulation on one machine. Concerns: this is a characterization paper - the released artifact is the trace plus analysis code, not the described systems (fault-tolerant pretraining, decoupled scheduling), so an improvement project would have to be simulation-based.

title: Sprinter: Speeding Up High-Fidelity Crawling of the Modern Web
note: Hybrid browser plus browserless web crawler with JS-execution memoization; entirely user space (Node, headless Chrome via CDP), single machine, no root. Concerns: needs a record-and-replay proxy and a page corpus; live crawling is nondeterministic and bandwidth-hungry, so the reproduction plan should pin an archived corpus. Repo has no README on main - code is on the master branch.

title: Finding Adversarial Inputs for Heuristics using Multi-level Optimization
note: Tool that encodes a heuristic and its optimal counterpart for a solver to find worst-case performance gaps; runs entirely in user space on CPU. Concerns: needs Gurobi (free academic license) and the .NET/C# toolchain, neither preinstalled but both installable in $HOME; the contribution is an optimization/encoding framework, so an improvement would be algorithmic rather than systems-performance.

title: OPPerTune: Post-Deployment Configuration Tuning of Services Made Easy
note: RL/bandit-based post-deployment configuration tuning with automatic scoping; released as a Python framework. Concerns: the paper evaluates on Microsoft production services and on microservice benchmarks that normally need Kubernetes, which we cannot run - a local study would have to tune a single-process application or replay offline workloads.

title: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
note: Cache eviction algorithm evaluated on 1559 open traces with a CPU-only user-space simulator (libCacheSim) plus patches to five production cache libraries; no root, no GPU, no network. Strongest fit of this venue-year. Concerns: the full trace corpus is large relative to 257 GB free disk so a subset is needed; throughput/scalability claims were made with 16 threads which matches this machine.

title: Harvesting Idle Memory for Application-managed Soft State with Midas
note: Soft-memory abstraction that lets applications harvest idle memory for caches and memoization; released as a C/C++ user-space library plus a coordinator daemon, and a 125 GiB RAM machine suits the workload. Concern (important): the paper states the coordinator is a user-space daemon plus a privileged kernel module, and the repo contains a koord kernel module - loading it needs root, so cross-application memory rebalancing may not be reproducible and only single-application soft-memory experiments may work.

title: Efficient Exposure of Partial Failure Bugs in Distributed Systems with Inferred Abstract States
note: Fault-injection testing framework using Soot-based static analysis of JVM bytecode and inferred abstract states; the six targets (ZooKeeper, Kafka, HDFS, HBase, Cassandra, Flink) all run as local user-space JVM processes. Concerns: Java toolchain must be installed via conda; running small local clusters is RAM and disk heavy but fits; some fault types used in related work rely on tc (root-only) - FUSE-based faults are available.

title: LitePred: Transferable and Scalable Latency Prediction for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search
note: Transfer-learning approach for DNN inference latency predictors (VAE sampler plus similarity-guided adaptation); models are small and train on one GPU, and code plus latency datasets are released. Concerns: original study spans 85 edge platforms and mobile phones that we do not have, so new-platform measurement is limited to the local CPU/GPU - work must build on the released latency datasets. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/microsoft/Moonlit/tree/main/LitePred .

title: LDB: An Efficient Latency Profiling Tool for Multithreaded Applications
note: Software-only latency profiler using LLVM instrumentation plus a busy-polling stack-scanning thread; explicitly designed to avoid hardware performance counters and kernel support, which matches a machine with perf_event_paranoid=3 and eBPF disabled. Concerns: requires building a custom LLVM 14 in user space (long build); dedicates one core to the scanner (fine on 32 threads); some applications evaluated in the paper are kernel-bypass runtimes that cannot run here, so plain Linux workloads must be substituted.

title: OctoSketch: Enabling Real-Time, Continuous Network Monitoring over Multiple Cores
note: Change-based continuous aggregation that scales sketches across many cores; the repo has separate CPU, DPDK and XDP implementations, and the CPU variant is plain multi-threaded user-space C++ that suits a 16-core machine. Concerns: the DPDK and eBPF-XDP variants need root and eBPF (blocked), so only the CPU variant is usable; packet traces (for example CAIDA) must be obtained separately and the no-DPDK setup changes the achievable packet rates.

title: Solving Max-Min Fair Resource Allocations Quickly on Large Graphs
note: Fast max-min fair allocators evaluated on WAN traffic engineering and cluster scheduling workloads (public Philly traces); Python plus C# with Gurobi, CPU only, trace-driven. Concerns: needs a Gurobi academic license and .NET installed in user space; the contribution is algorithmic, so an improvement project would be about solver formulations and approximation quality rather than systems engineering.

title: ExChain: Exception Dependency Analysis for Root Cause Diagnosis
note: JVM dynamic taint tracking that links causally related exceptions for root-cause diagnosis of exception-handling failures; single machine, user space, no root. Concerns: needs a Java toolchain via conda and specific versions of the target systems (Hadoop, Solr, Cassandra) to reproduce case studies; taint tracking has high runtime overhead so experiments are CPU-bound but fit in 16 cores.

title: Rajomon: Decentralized and Coordinated Overload Control for Latency-Sensitive Microservices
note: Pure user-space Go/gRPC interceptor library implementing a token-and-price admission-control / rate-limiting policy; a resource manager that can be studied as many processes on one host. Concern: paper evaluates on up to 140 cores across a cluster; on 16C/32T the microservice graphs (DeathStarBench-style) must be scaled down, and load generators compete with the services for cores.

title: NDD: A Decision Diagram for Network Verification
note: Self-contained user-space decision-diagram library (BDD/BCDD/ZDD backends) benchmarked against CUDD/BuDDy/JDD; CPU+RAM only, no root, no network hardware. Claimed 100x memory and 100x time reduction is a clear, measurable improvement axis. Concern: none for the machine; the improvement would be data-structure/algorithm engineering rather than a distributed-systems build.

title: One-Size-Fits-None: Understanding and Enhancing Slow-Fault Tolerance in Modern Distributed Systems
note: Artifact is the Xinda fail-slow injection pipeline plus the ADR adaptive-threshold library (adr/ directory in the repo); both are user-space, and slow-I/O injection uses CharybdeFS, a FUSE filesystem - FUSE is usable on this machine. Concerns: the repo ships CloudLab/Ansible deployment scripts and the six target systems (Cassandra, HDFS, Kafka, etcd, ...) are normally multi-node, so everything must be collapsed to multiple processes on one host; some harness pieces assume Docker, which is not installed.

title: Accelerating Design Space Exploration for LLM Training Systems with Multi-experiment Parallel Simulation
note: Multiverse is a GPU-accelerated LLM-training simulator; the artifact README explicitly retains CPU-only execution, and the whole workload is simulation, so no real GPU cluster is needed. One A5000 plus 125 GiB RAM is a plausible platform, and simulator throughput/fidelity is an obvious improvement target. Concern: repo is at "Multiverse 2.0" which may have diverged from the NSDI '25 artifact; input traces are Chakra files that must be sourced.

title: SimAI: Unifying Architecture Design and Performance Tuning for Large-Scale LLM Training
note: Official Alibaba artifact (URL printed in the paper). The analytical and ns-3-backed simulation modes are CPU-only user-space builds, so "simulate a 1k-GPU cluster" costs no GPUs; accuracy-vs-speed of the simulator is a testable hypothesis. Concerns: the SimAI-Physical mode needs a real GPU/RDMA cluster and must be skipped; the build pulls a large ns-3/MPI toolchain that has to be installed under $HOME.

title: ByteCheckpoint: A Unified Checkpointing System for Large Foundation Model Development
note: Checkpoint save/load/resharding is fundamentally an I/O and serialization problem; the repo is a pip-installable PyTorch library with unit tests and demos. Ranks can be emulated with several processes over gloo/NCCL on one GPU or on CPU, and ~257 GB of NVMe is enough for sub-1B-parameter checkpoints. Concerns: the paper's headline numbers come from thousands of GPUs and remote object storage; single-node scale-down measures the resharding/serialization path only, not cluster-wide save throughput.

title: Region-based Content Enhancement for Efficient Video Analytics at the Edge
note: RegenHance is a PyTorch + PyCUDA pipeline (importance prediction, region stitching, super-resolution, detection) that runs on a single GPU; an RTX A5000 is stronger than the edge devices used in the paper, so a scale-down is meaningful and accuracy/throughput are directly measurable. Concerns: the paper evaluates across five heterogeneous edge devices, which cannot be reproduced; the repo README admits it was not reorganized after submission, so build effort is uncertain.

title: Verifying maximum link loads in a changing world
note: Velo is a Rust CPU-only verification prototype (repo URL in the paper) whose evaluation is "generate raw data, then post-process with Python"; runtime and memory on large ISP topologies are the metrics, both improvable on this machine. Concerns: the authors state the industrial case study cannot be released, so only the public-topology experiments are reproducible; Rust must be installed in user space (it is not preinstalled).

title: CEGS: Configuration Example Generalizing Synthesizer
note: A learned component (GNN querier + GNN classifier + LLM-driven synthesis) driving a systems-management task; Python artifact, GNNs train comfortably on one 24 GB GPU. Concerns: the README expects Docker for the Batfish verification service (Docker is not installed - Batfish would have to be built from source or replaced) and an OpenAI API key, which costs money; a local 7-8B model on the A5000 is a plausible but unvalidated substitute.

title: From Address Blocks to Authorized Prefixes: Redesigning RPKI ROV with a Hierarchical Hashing Scheme
note: h2ROV is a C data structure (hierarchical hashing over authorized prefixes) with a makefile and experiment scripts in the repo; claimed 1.7-9.8x validation speedup and 49-87% memory reduction are pure CPU/RAM metrics measurable on one machine with public RPKI/BGP dumps. Concerns: the repo README is essentially empty, so documentation is thin; the routing-convergence emulation part of the evaluation may need more setup than the data-structure benchmarks.

title: Resolving Packets from Counters: Multi-scale Network Traffic Super Resolution via Composable Large Traffic Model
note: Learned model (GPT-2-scale Granular Traffic Transformer tree) applied to a systems problem - synthesizing packet traces from counters; the repo has Train / Infer / data-processing directories and the models are small enough for 24 GB FP16. Concerns: training the full composable tree of GTT models may exceed a 10-week part-time budget on one GPU, so the project would likely target one or two granularity levels; training data must be regenerated from public pcaps.

title: BFTBrain: Adaptive BFT Consensus with Reinforcement Learning
note: Learned (RL) policy that selects among BFT protocols at runtime - a learned component inside a system, with an official, well-organized artifact. Replicas are user-space Java processes, so a 4-16 replica deployment fits in 32 threads with emulated latency. Concerns: the underlying subject is distributed consensus, which sits at the edge of the topic table; co-locating replicas on one host distorts the network/CPU contention that the RL features are built on, so results must be framed as single-host emulation.

title: FastServe: Iteration-Level Preemptive Scheduling for Large Language Model Inference
note: Iteration-level preemptive MLFQ scheduling for LLM serving plus GPU/host KV-cache swapping - the scheduler is the contribution and reproduces on one 24 GB GPU with a 7-8B model. Concern - paper is evaluated on a multi-GPU distributed deployment and the engine is a custom C++ stack rather than vLLM.

title: Pilot Execution: Simulating Failure Recovery In Situ for Production Distributed Systems
note: Pure user-space runtime library plus analysis framework that dry-runs recovery actions in distributed systems - target systems (HDFS, ZooKeeper, Kafka class) can be run as multiple processes on one host. Concern - some case studies assume production-scale deployments.

title: DroidSpeak: KV Cache Sharing Across Fine-tuned Model Variants
note: KV-cache reuse across different fine-tuned variants of the same architecture - a layer-sensitivity study plus selective recompute, and the paper itself measures Llama-3.1-8B on a single A100 so a single A5000 works. Concern - no artifact URL in the paper or on arXiv; authors are the LMCache group so code may live there, marked unknown.

title: HydraServe: Minimizing Cold Start Latency for Serverless LLM Serving in Public Clouds
note: Cold-start latency of serverless LLM serving - model fetch, safetensors loading and pipeline consolidation are all measurable on one GPU plus local NVMe. Concern - the placement and network-contention parts of the design need several GPUs and servers.

title: CacheCatalyst: Enhancing Web Caching for the Latency-Constrained Internet
note: Web cache revalidation policy - early validation during page load; entirely user-space (browser plus Caddy origin) and trace or emulation driven on one host. Concern - realistic latency effects need network emulation which is available only without root-level tc in some setups.

title: Feedback-guided Adaptive Testing of Distributed Systems Designs
note: Feedback-guided fuzzing of formal distributed-system models in the P language - CPU-only, user-space, 94 model configurations; the implementation was upstreamed into the official P repository. Concern - the paper's own artifact URL github.com/aolial/Fest-artifact currently 404s so the upstreamed P code is the usable artifact.

title: JITServe: SLO-aware LLM Serving with Imprecise Request Information
note: SLO-aware LLM request scheduling under unknown response lengths and request dependencies - a scheduling-policy contribution that scales down to one GPU and a small model. Concern - compound-request workloads in the paper assume a larger serving cluster.

title: RollPacker: Taming Long-Tail Rollouts for RL Post-Training with Tail Batching
note: Tail batching - a rollout scheduling policy for synchronous RL post-training; the policy itself is workload-level and can be studied with a 0.5-1.5B model on one GPU or replayed in simulation. Concern - the paper's speedups are measured on multi-GPU veRL and SGLang deployments of Qwen2.5 models.

title: PlanB: Efficient Software IPv6 Lookup with Linearized B+-Tree
note: Linearized B+-tree for IPv6 longest-prefix match - a pure user-space data-structure and memory-layout contribution benchmarked with real BGP FIB dumps; ideal single-machine CPU study. Concern - the paper reports cache-level analysis that we cannot reproduce without hardware perf counters.

title: UpFuzz: Detecting Data Format Incompatibility Bugs during Distributed Storage System Upgrade
note: Upgrade-path fuzzing for distributed storage systems (Cassandra, HDFS class) driven by data-format properties of persisted state - runs as local multi-process clusters, CPU and disk only. Concern - each upgrade test is expensive so a 10-week budget limits the campaign length.

title: FlexLLM: Token-Level Co-Serving of LLM Inference and Finetuning with SLO Guarantees
note: Token-level co-serving of inference and PEFT finetuning on shared GPUs with graph pruning for activation memory - the 80 percent activation-memory saving claim is exactly the kind of thing a 24 GB card can test with LLaMA-3.1-8B. Concern - built on FlexFlow Serve (C++/CUDA) which is a heavy build, and the 32B configurations will not fit.

title: MuxTune: Efficient Multi-Task LLM Fine-Tuning in Multi-Tenant Datacenters via Spatial-Temporal Backbone Multiplexing
