note: Spatial-temporal multiplexing of a shared backbone across concurrent PEFT fine-tuning tasks - the GPU-underutilization problem it attacks is visible on a single A5000 with small adapters. Concern - evaluated in a multi-tenant multi-GPU datacenter setting and uses NVIDIA Transformer Engine which may want a newer CUDA than driver 535 supports.

title: Themis: Detecting Distributed Concurrency Bugs through RPC-Driven Race-Directed Test Generation and Fuzzing
note: Static race detection plus LLM-generated tests plus directed fuzzing for distributed concurrency bugs - the eight target systems run as local processes; no root, no special hardware. Concern - the LLM test-generation stage needs an external API budget or a local model.

title: Phantora: Maximizing Code Reuse in Simulation-based Machine Learning System Performance Estimation
note: Hybrid GPU-cluster simulator that runs unmodified ML frameworks and intercepts GPU/comm calls, explicitly designed so cluster performance can be estimated from a single GPU. Concern - it emulates each GPU server as a container and Docker/Podman are not installed, so the container layer must be ported to bwrap or plain processes.

title: ServeGen: Workload Characterization and Generation of Large Language Model Serving in Production
note: Production LLM-serving workload characterization plus an open workload generator - a reusable artifact (traces plus generator) that is CPU-only and directly useful for driving any serving experiment on this machine. Concern - it is a workload tool, so an improvement project would have to target generation fidelity rather than a serving mechanism.

title: AVA: Towards Agentic Video Analytics with Vision Language Models
note: VLM-based agentic video analytics - event knowledge graph indexing plus agentic retrieval; code and the AVA-100 benchmark are both public and the pipeline is built on LMDeploy so a 7-8B VLM fits in 24 GB. Concern - long-video indexing over the full benchmark is compute-heavy and 24 GB limits VLM size.

title: Heuristic Analysis from Source Code via Symbolic-Guided Optimization
note: Analyzes a heuristic's source code directly with symbolic-guided search to find worst-case inputs - CPU-only user-space tool, released by Microsoft. Concern - the demo domains are traffic engineering and VM placement, so topic fit with the course is indirect; the contribution is the analysis engine, not the network.

title: Fractal: Fault-Tolerant Shell-Script Distribution
note: Fault-tolerant distributed shell-script execution with subgraph-level dependency and progress tracking - MIT-licensed, user-space, and the runtime can be driven with multiple worker processes on one host. Concern - the paper's speedups are measured on 4- and 30-node clusters so absolute numbers will not reproduce; fault-recovery semantics still can.

title: ZipLLM: Efficient LLM Storage via Model-Aware Synergistic Data Deduplication and Compression
note: Model-aware delta compression (BitX) plus tensor-level deduplication for LLM model-hub storage - CPU and disk only, no GPU needed, and Hugging Face model families are freely downloadable. Excellent fit for the 16-core/125 GiB/257 GB machine. Concern - the full Hugging Face characterization is petabyte scale so the study must be scoped to a few model families.

title: Latency-Aware Caching with Delayed Hits: From Bursty Traffic to Pipeline Architectures
note: Pipeline of orthogonal cache policies with adaptive memory split, plus latency-aware handling of delayed hits - trace-driven simulation on top of the Caffeine framework, purely CPU and memory bound. Concern - Java build and large public cache traces need disk, both fine here.

title: ADOC: Automatically Harmonizing Dataflow Between Components in Log-Structured Key-Value Stores for Improved Performance
note: Excellent fit. Pure user-space RocksDB auto-tuning framework that controls write stalls by adjusting thread count and batch size to limit data overflow. Evaluation is single-node RocksDB on NVMe SSDs - exactly the target machine. 16 cores and local NVMe are enough to reproduce the write-stall regimes. Concern: the paper sweeps several device classes (SATA SSD, NVMe SSD, Optane) and we only have NVMe, so device-sensitivity results would have to be narrowed or emulated with cgroup v2 I/O throttling.

title: GL-Cache: Group-level learning for efficient and high-performance caching
note: Excellent fit. A learned cache-eviction policy (group-level learning with XGBoost-style utility models) built on Segcache, evaluated by trace-driven simulation over 118 public block-I/O and CDN traces. Entirely user space, CPU only, no root. Traces (CloudPhysics, Twitter, Wiki/CDN) are public downloads; main cost is disk space for traces, which fits in the ~257 GB free. Strong improvement targets: group formation heuristics, feature set, learning cadence.

title: SHADE: Enable Fundamental Cacheability for Distributed Deep Learning Training
note: Importance-sampling-aware caching layer for the deep-learning training data pipeline, implemented in user space on top of PyTorch's DataLoader plus a key-value cache. Concern: the paper evaluates distributed DLT across multiple nodes and GPUs; here it would have to be scaled down to one node with one RTX A5000, which is a meaningful scale-down but changes the I/O-vs-compute balance the paper leans on. Also assumes a remote/slow backing store - that would have to be emulated locally (e.g. FUSE or cgroup I/O limits), which is doable without root.

title: ParaRC: Embracing Sub-Packetization for Repair Parallelization in MSR-Coded Storage
note: The core contribution is an algorithmic one - a heuristic that trades repair bandwidth against maximum per-node repair load in MSR codes - and the bandwidth/load trade-off curve can be studied purely by simulation on one machine. Concern: the released prototype is a distributed repair system whose end-to-end numbers come from a ~10-node cluster over a real network. On this machine it would have to run as multiple processes on one host, so absolute degraded-read and full-node-recovery times will be distorted; the defensible experiments are the load-balancing heuristic and simulated repair schedules.

title: ConfD: Analyzing Configuration Dependencies of File Systems for Fun and Profit
note: ConfD's core (taint analyzer, dependency analyzer, state generator) is LLVM-based static analysis of file-system source code - it runs entirely in user space with no root and no mounted file systems, and LLVM/clang is installable via conda. Concern: several of the six plugins validate findings by running xfstests and e2fsprogs against mounted ext4/XFS instances, which needs root; those plugins could not be reproduced, so a project here would have to target the static-analysis side (e.g. extending to more file systems, improving false-positive rate) rather than the mount-based validation.

title: Symbiosis: The Art of Application and Kernel Cache Cooperation
note: Dynamically splits memory between an application cache and the kernel page cache for LevelDB, RocksDB and WiredTiger. Entirely user-space: modified KV stores plus a Python/simpy offline simulator, and memory budgets are enforced with cgroup v2, which env.md delegates to the user slice. No root, no kernel changes, single node. Strong improvement target - the sizing policy is a small, self-contained algorithm.

title: Kosmo: Efficient Online Miss Ratio Curve Generation for Eviction Policy Evaluation
note: Pure trace-driven MRC generation for non-inclusive eviction policies (LFU, FIFO, 2Q, LRFU). Rust binaries, public cache traces (Twitter cache-trace, 52 traces), no privileged access and no special hardware. Artifact also archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10569925. Only concern is trace download size against the ~257 GB free on /home, which is manageable by subsetting traces.

title: Metis: File System Model Checking via Versatile Input and State Exploration
note: Model-checking framework plus RefFS, a FUSE reference file system (https://github.com/sbu-fsl/RefFS). Concern: the headline experiments check in-kernel file systems (ext4, XFS, BtrFS) on brd RAM block devices, which needs root for modprobe and mount/unmount - not available here. A scaled-down study over FUSE-only targets (RefFS vs fuse-ext2) is feasible since /dev/fuse is world-rw and fusermount3 is setuid. Memory-hungry (search width x mountable size) but 125 GiB RAM helps. Audit stage should confirm the FUSE-only path is a viable project.

title: IONIA: High-Performance Replication for Modern Disk-based KV Stores
note: Replication protocol exploiting LSM/write-optimized KV-store interface and performance characteristics to get 1-RTT writes and any-replica reads. Concern: it is a distributed protocol normally run on a small cluster. env.md permits emulating distributed behaviour with multiple processes on this host, and 3-5 replica processes over loopback fit easily in 16 cores / 125 GiB; RTT-sensitive latency numbers would be distorted, so a reproduction would need tc-free latency emulation or a focus on the storage-side (background execution, read scalability) claims. No RDMA or special NIC required.

title: Physical vs. Logical Indexing with IDEA: Inverted Deduplication-Aware Index
note: Deduplication-aware inverted term index built on Lucene and the Destor deduplication prototype. Single server, user-space Java/C++, HDD or SSD backing store - their own setup was one 128 GB Xeon box, comfortably below this machine. Concern: the artifact targets Ubuntu 16.04 (old Destor dependencies), so building on Debian 12 may need a conda/source toolchain; no system packages are strictly required.

title: MIDAS: Minimizing Write Amplification in Log-Structured Systems through Adaptive Group Number and Size Configuration
note: Analytical (UID + Markov-chain) model that adapts group count and size to minimize GC write amplification in log-structured systems. Main results come from a user-space simulator, separately released at https://github.com/sungkyun123/MiDAS-Simulation and archived at Zenodo 10409599 - that part runs anywhere. Concern: the hardware prototype needs a Xilinx VCU108 FPGA with custom NAND modules that the authors state are not publicly available, so only the simulation-based claims are reproducible here. That is still a complete improvement target (the WAF/throughput comparisons against state-of-the-art GC are simulator results).

title: ELECT: Enabling Erasure Coding Tiering for LSM-tree-based Storage
note: Hybrid replication/erasure-coding tiering for an LSM-tree KV store, implemented on Cassandra. Borderline on the machine: the artifact appendix recommends at least eight networked machines (six for the EC stripe). Co-locating 6-8 Cassandra JVMs as processes on this single host is possible within 125 GiB and is the standard CCM-style setup, and the headline storage-savings claim is not latency-sensitive; end-to-end throughput/latency numbers would not transfer. Needs Java in user space (not installed, but conda-installable) and Intel ISA-L, which builds from source. Audit stage should judge whether the single-host scale-down is acceptable.

title: COLE: A Column-based Learned Storage for Blockchain Systems
note: Learned-index-based column storage replacing Ethereum's Merkle Patricia Trie, with write-optimized (LSM-like) strategies for disk. Rust, single machine, ordinary NVMe - exactly this hardware class. Clean improvement axes (model choice, merge policy, provenance query cost). No GPU, no root, no cluster.

title: Baleen: ML Admission and Prefetching for Flash Caches
note: ML admission plus prefetching policy for flash caches, trained and evaluated entirely offline on released Meta traces from seven clusters (traces and code at https://www.pdl.cmu.edu/CILES/). Simulation-only, CPU-bound, no root and no flash hardware needed; the A5000 is optional for model training. Ideal single-machine improvement target - policy, the "episodes" residency model, and the Disk-head Time objective are all swappable.

title: Mooncake: Trading More Storage for Less Computation — A KVCache-centric Architecture for Serving LLM Chatbot
note: KVCache-centric prefix cache plus a throughput/SLO-aware request scheduler; policy work is pure user space and the repo is large and actively maintained. Concerns - paper evaluates thousands of A800/H800 nodes with RDMA-based prefill/decode disaggregation; on one RTX A5000 the scale-down is a single-GPU vLLM plus Mooncake Store as a local DRAM/SSD KV tier with the TCP transport, and prefill/decode disaggregation must be emulated by time-slicing or simulated. FP8 paths unusable on Ampere.

title: IMPRESS: An Importance-Informed Multi-Tier Prefix KV Storage System for Large Language Model Inference
note: Importance-informed prefix-KV identification plus multi-tier (DRAM/SSD) KV cache placement to cut TTFT - entirely user-space, single GPU, SSD-bound, a natural fit for the machine. Concerns - no standalone FAST '25 artifact; the released repo is HyperInfer, the same authors' journal extension, which states it keeps the original FlexGen/H2O-based prototype. Paper uses OPT-6.7B/13B/30B; only 6.7B fits 24 GB in FP16 without offload, though offloading is central to the design.

title: 3L-Cache: Low Overhead and Precise Learning-based Eviction Policy for Caches
note: Learning-based cache eviction policy evaluated entirely by trace-driven simulation on top of libCacheSim - user-space C++, CPU only, no root, and the headline metric (CPU overhead vs miss ratio) is exactly the kind of trade-off a 10-week improvement project can attack. Concerns - the paper's 4855-trace corpus is many TB; must subset to a few trace families and argue representativeness.

title: VectorCDC: Accelerating Data Deduplication with Vector Instructions
note: Content-defined chunking accelerated with SSE/AVX - pure user-space C++ benchmark tool (DedupBench), no root, no special hardware, builds with plain gcc. Concerns - Zen 3 Threadripper has SSE-128 and AVX-256 but no AVX-512, so the AVX-512 numbers cannot be reproduced; only hashless CDC variants (AE, MAXP, RAM) are vectorized, and the DEB dataset lives on Kaggle (download size to check).

title: Oasis: An Out-of-core Approximate Graph System via All-Distances Sketches
note: Single-machine out-of-core system that trades memory for SSD I/O when building and querying All-Distances Sketches; user-space C++ with an explicit memory-budget knob, which suits a 125 GiB / NVMe box well. Concerns - large graph inputs plus multi-times-graph-size sketches must fit in ~257 GB free, so the biggest datasets in the paper may need to be dropped.

title: On Scalable Integrity Checking for Secure Cloud Disks
note: Dynamic Merkle Trees are a 5 KLoC user-space C++ data structure on the storage I/O path, driven by synthetic Zipfian and real Alibaba block traces - the algorithmic contribution is reproducible without privileges. Concerns - the paper's block-device integration uses BDUS, which ships an out-of-tree kernel module that cannot be loaded without root; the experiment harness would have to be re-hosted on FUSE or on a pure user-space trace replayer, which changes the absolute numbers.

title: Liquid-State Drive: A Case for DNA Block Device for Enormous Data
note: Block-device design (dual-layer translation table, symbiotic metadata, delayed invalidation) evaluated entirely on a user-space DNA-storage simulator with a small SSD as the metadata tier - no exotic hardware is needed to run it, and the mapping/GC policies are improvable. Concerns - the paper says only the simulator is released, and the SJTU IPADS project host did not respond from this network at check time, so the repo could not be verified; GitHub search for "LiqSD" found nothing. Treat the repo link as unconfirmed.

title: CacheSlide: Unlocking Cross Position-Aware KV Cache Reuse for Accelerating LLM Serving
note: KV-cache reuse policy implemented as a vLLM 0.8.5 extension - pure user space + single GPU. Concern: paper uses A100 80 GB (70B model on 2 A100s); on a 24 GB A5000 only the 7-8B configs fit, so 70B results cannot be reproduced. FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere so the attention path is fine.

title: OdinANN: Direct Insert for Consistently Stable Performance in Billion-Scale Graph-Based Vector Search
note: On-disk graph ANNS index with direct insert; entirely user space, single node, CPU + NVMe. Code is shipped inside the authors' PipeANN repo (README cites the FAST '26 OdinANN paper and notes PipeANN is integrated into OdinANN). Concerns: paper machine has 512 GB RAM and billion-scale datasets; with 125 GiB RAM and ~257 GB free disk the study must scale down to 10M-100M vectors (SIFT100M-class), which the artifact supports.

title: "Range as a Key" is the Key! Fast and Compact Cloud Block Store Index with RASK
note: User-space in-memory range index for block stores, evaluated trace-driven against ten baseline indexes - ideal single-machine, no-root study. Alibaba EBS traces released at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/dataset/218875. Concern: the SJTU-hosted GitLab (ipads.se.sjtu.edu.cn) did not respond from this network when checked; availability should be re-verified at audit time.

title: Holistic and Automated Task Scheduling for Distributed LSM-tree-based Storage
note: HATS co-schedules foreground reads and background compaction in Cassandra; Java user-space prototype, no kernel or special hardware. Concern: it is a distributed KV store - a cluster must be emulated as several Cassandra JVMs on this one host (16 cores / 125 GiB is enough for a 3-5 node ring), and replica-selection results will be less faithful than on real nodes.

title: Preparation Meets Opportunity: Enhancing Data Preprocessing for ML Training With Seneca
note: Cache partitioning + opportunistic sampling in the PyTorch data loader; user-space, storage-bound, one node. Concerns: datasets in the paper range 142 GB-1.4 TB vs ~257 GB free, so a smaller dataset is needed; the paper's multi-node / NVLink configurations are out of reach, and a single A5000 limits how many concurrent training jobs can be co-run.

title: GPU Checkpoint/Restore Made Fast and Lightweight
note: Distinguished Artifact Award; single-GPU system-level checkpoint/restore via CUDA API interception and CPU shadow execution - the mechanism is single-GPU by construction. Concerns worth auditing: the cuda-checkpoint baseline needs a newer NVIDIA driver than the installed 535.216.01, and CRIU-style process checkpointing often needs elevated privileges, which are unavailable here.

title: Sharpen the Spec, Cut the Code: A Case for Generative File System with SYSSPEC
note: Best Paper + Distinguished Artifact. SPECFS runs in userspace via FUSE (confirmed in the paper and in the artifact appendix, which lists fuse/libfuse-dev as the only system requirement) - /dev/fuse and setuid fusermount3 are available on this machine. Concern: the generation pipeline needs an external LLM API key (Gemini or DeepSeek), i.e. network access and some API spend.

title: How Soon is Now? Preloading Images for Virtual Disks with ThinkAhead
note: Data-driven block preloading (prefetch/admission policy) for virtual disk images, evaluated largely by trace-driven simulation; production Alibaba EBS image-boot traces released at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/dataset/216164. Concern: the paper also reports cluster experiments on Alibaba EBS, which cannot be reproduced - only the prediction + simulation half is in reach here.

title: SkySync: Accelerating File Synchronization with Collaborative Delta Generation
note: Reuses storage-layer checksums to cut delta-generation cost; implemented by extending rsync and dsync protocols, fully user space. Client and server can both run on this host. Concern: the WAN numbers need link emulation, and tc/netem requires root - LAN/loopback and CPU-cost measurements are still fully reproducible.

title: ParaSync: Exploiting Fine-Grained Parallelism for Efficient File Synchronization
note: Parallel content-defined chunking + streaming chunk matching + pipelined reconstruction; user-space C++, CPU-bound, benefits from the 16-core/32-thread CPU. Same WAN-emulation caveat as SkySync; chunking speedup (7.6x claimed) is measurable locally with no privileges.

title: DOGI: Data Placement with Oracle-Guided Insights for Log-Structured Systems
note: Lightweight ML predicts block invalidation time to guide data placement and cut GC write amplification; the main evaluation is a simulator plus a near-optimal oracle baseline (NoDaP), which runs fine on CPU with no root. Concern: the secondary prototype runs on a zoned (ZNS) device, which this machine does not have - the simulation track is the usable one.

title: LESS is More for I/O-Efficient Repairs in Erasure-Coded Storage
note: Repair-friendly erasure code construction reducing both bytes read and I/O seeks; the coding core is a user-space library (ISA-L based) and the trade-off can be studied with local microbenchmarks. Concern: end-to-end numbers come from HDFS on a local cluster - here that means a pseudo-distributed / multi-process HDFS on one host, which changes the network/seek balance.

title: Cache-Centric Multi-Resource Allocation for Storage Services
note: HARE is a cache-size-aware multi-resource (cache/IO/CPU) allocation algorithm - a policy problem that is naturally simulated or run in user space, with public Twitter cache traces. Two prototypes also released: https://github.com/WiscADSL/hopperkv and https://github.com/WiscADSL/bunnyfs. Concerns: BunnyFS issues I/O through SPDK, whose setup (hugepages, VFIO binding) normally needs root; HopperKV caches DynamoDB behind Redis and would need DynamoDB-local or an AWS account. The algorithm itself is the tractable target.

title: Cooperative Concurrency Control for Write-Intensive Key-Value Workloads
note: In-memory key-value store concurrency control on multicore CPUs - pure user space  fits 16-core host  AE artifact released on Zenodo

title: Glign: Taming Misaligned Graph Traversals in Concurrent Graph Processing
note: Single-machine concurrent graph-processing runtime - CPU only user space  Zenodo artifact  alignment heuristics are an obvious improvement target

title: Betty: Enabling Large-Scale GNN Training with Batch-Level Graph Partitioning
note: GNN training on a single GPU under memory pressure - batch-level partitioning is exactly a one-GPU memory problem  Zenodo + GitHub artifact

title: Carbon Explorer: A Holistic Framework for Designing Carbon Aware Datacenters
note: Trace-driven datacenter carbon/capacity simulator - pure Python user space  open source  policies are easy to extend

title: ElasticFlow: An Elastic Serverless Training Platform for Distributed Deep Learning
note: DL-training job scheduler with an open trace-driven simulator - simulator runs on CPU; concern the physical testbed uses a multi-GPU cluster

title: EVStore: Storage and Caching Capabilities for Scaling Embedding Tables in Deep Recommendation Systems
note: Multi-layer embedding-table cache for DLRM inference - single node CPU/GPU user space  cache admission/eviction policy is a clean improvement target

title: Hidet: Task-Mapping Programming Paradigm for Deep Learning Tensor Programs
note: DL compiler with task-mapping scheduling - single NVIDIA GPU actively maintained open source  Ampere supported

title: LeaFTL: A Learning-Based Flash Translation Layer for Solid-State Drives
note: Learned-index flash translation layer - ships a trace-driven SSD simulator that runs in user space; concern the full FEMU setup wants KVM which is unavailable

title: Lucid: A Non-intrusive, Scalable and Interpretable Scheduler for Deep Learning Training Jobs
note: DL-cluster scheduler evaluated by trace-driven simulation with public traces - runs entirely on one CPU host

title: NNSmith: Generating Diverse and Valid Test Cases for Deep Learning Compilers
note: DL-compiler fuzzing - pure user-space Python runs against TVM/ONNXRuntime on one machine  widely used open source

title: TensorIR: An Abstraction for Automatic Tensorized Program Optimization
note: Tensorized-program abstraction for TVM - single GPU/CPU auto-scheduling  fully open source and upstreamed into Apache TVM

title: TiLT: A Time-Centric Approach for Stream Query Optimization and Parallelization
note: Stream-query compiler and runtime - CPU only user space  Zenodo AE artifact

title: TLP: A Deep Learning-Based Cost Model for Tensor Program Tuning
note: Learned cost model for tensor-program tuning - trains and runs on one GPU  open source  a natural target for better models or cheaper search

title: VClinic: A Portable and Efficient Framework for Fine-Grained Value Profilers
note: Dynamic-binary-instrumentation value profiler - user space no root or perf counters required  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: WACO: Learning Workload-Aware Co-optimization of the Format and Schedule of a Sparse Tensor Program
note: Learned cost model that co-optimizes sparse tensor format and schedule - CPU only  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Characterizing and Optimizing End-to-End Systems for Private Inference
note: End-to-end characterization and optimization of private-inference serving - client and server can be two processes on one host with one GPU; concern the contribution is partly cryptographic-protocol level

title: DrGPUM: Guiding Memory Optimization for GPU-Accelerated Applications
note: GPU memory profiler built on CUPTI - single GPU user space no root or perf counters  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Efficient Compactions between Storage Tiers with PrismDB
note: LSM key-value store with tier-aware compaction - user-space RocksDB-style engine on NVMe  GitHub + Zenodo artifact; concern the paper uses QLC+SLC tiers that must be emulated here

title: GRACE: A Scalable Graph-Based Approach to Accelerating Recommendation Model Inference
note: Graph-based acceleration of recommendation-model inference on one CPU/GPU node - GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: Heron: Automatically Constrained High-Performance Library Generation for Deep Learning Accelerators
note: Constrained auto-scheduling for tensor libraries - supports NVIDIA tensor-core GPUs and CPUs; concern part of the evaluation uses a Cambricon accelerator we do not have

title: RepCut: Superlinear Parallel RTL Simulation with Replication-Aided Partitioning
note: Parallel RTL simulation by replication-aided partitioning - CPU-only user-space simulator that scales with the 16 cores here  Zenodo AE artifact

title: SparseTIR: Composable Abstractions for Sparse Compilation in Deep Learning
note: Sparse tensor compilation for DL on a single NVIDIA GPU - GitHub + Zenodo AE artifact  well documented

title: TeraHeap: Reducing Memory Pressure in Managed Big Data Frameworks
note: Adds an NVMe-backed second heap to the JVM to cut GC pressure for Spark/Giraph - user-space OpenJDK build on one node  GitHub + Zenodo artifact

title: BaCO: A Fast and Portable Bayesian Compiler Optimization Framework
note: Bayesian autotuner for compiler/scheduling search spaces (TACO RISE HPVM) - pure user-space Python on one CPU/GPU node  open source

title: MiniMalloc: A Lightweight Memory Allocator for Hardware-Accelerated Machine Learning
note: Offline static memory allocator (2D packing solver) for ML accelerator buffers - single-threaded C++ CPU solver with open benchmarks  fully open source

title: RECom: A Compiler Approach to Accelerating Recommendation Model Inference with Massive Embedding Columns
note: Compiler that fuses massive embedding-column subgraphs for recommendation inference on one GPU - open source from Alibaba

title: ShapleyIQ: Influence Quantification by Shapley Values for Performance Debugging of Microservices
note: Shapley-value performance attribution for microservice traces - code and data released; analysis runs offline on traces on one host  concern the original setting is a production cluster

title: Supporting Descendants in SIMD-Accelerated JSONPath
note: SIMD JSONPath query engine in Rust with descendant support - CPU only user space  actively maintained open source with a benchmark harness

title: Amanda: Unified Instrumentation Framework for Deep Neural Networks
note: User-space operator-level instrumentation layer over PyTorch/TensorFlow; pure Python/C++ extension, single GPU is enough. Easy to extend with new instrumentation tools.

title: Loupe: Driving the Development of OS Compatibility Layers
note: Dynamic syscall-usage analysis for OS compatibility layers; user-space ptrace/seccomp tooling plus a public results database. Concern - upstream harness wraps runs in Docker so it must be ported to a conda/bwrap setup.

title: ngAP: Non-blocking Large-scale Automata Processing on GPUs
note: GPU automata-processing engine; artifact was tested on an RTX 3090 (Ampere 24 GB) which matches the A5000 almost exactly. Clear room for scheduling/memoization improvements.

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference via Global Analysis and Tensor Expressions
note: Inter-operator DNN inference compiler; single NVIDIA GPU evaluation. Concern - artifact is packaged with Docker files that must be reproduced with conda/pip since Docker is unavailable.

title: Proteus: A High-Throughput Inference-Serving System with Accuracy Scaling
note: Inference-serving system with accuracy scaling driven by real and synthetic traces. Concern - designed for a small heterogeneous cluster; would need scale-down to one GPU plus CPU workers or trace-driven simulation.

title: TrackFM: Far-out Compiler Support for a Far Memory World
note: LLVM compiler plus user-space runtime for far memory; no kernel changes needed on the application side. Concern - the far-memory backend was run on CloudLab; a local loopback or second-process memory server would be needed here.

title: Compiling Loop-Based Nested Parallelism for Irregular Workloads
note: LLVM/NOELLE compiler plus user-space heartbeat scheduling runtime for nested parallelism on a multicore CPU; 16C/32T Threadripper is a reasonable target. Concern - the interrupt-based rollforward variant may need a signal/timer path that should be checked.

title: GIANTSAN: Efficient Memory Sanitization with Segment Folding
note: LLVM-based memory sanitizer with a new shadow encoding; purely user-space, CPU-only. Concern - headline numbers use SPEC CPU2017 which is licensed; open benchmarks would have to substitute.

title: GMLake: Efficient and Transparent GPU Memory Defragmentation for Large-scale DNN Training with Virtual Memory Stitching
note: GPU virtual-memory stitching allocator inside the PyTorch caching allocator. Concern - paper uses A100 80 GB; on a 24 GB A5000 the study must use smaller models or LoRA/recompute settings, but the fragmentation mechanism is unchanged.

title: MaxK-GNN: Extremely Fast GPU Kernel Design for Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Training
note: Single-GPU SpGEMM/SSpMM kernels plus a nonlinearity for GNN training; Ampere-class GPU is the target. Fits the machine directly.

title: PyTorch 2: Faster Machine Learning Through Dynamic Python Bytecode Transformation and Graph Compilation
note: TorchDynamo/TorchInductor (torch.compile); fully open, runs on a single GPU or CPU. Very large codebase - scope an improvement narrowly (e.g. a guard or fusion heuristic).

title: RAP: Resource-aware Automated GPU Sharing for Multi-GPU Recommendation Model Training and Input Preprocessing
note: Co-running DLRM input preprocessing with training on the same GPU via resource-aware kernel fusion. Concern - paper is multi-GPU, but the co-running cost model and horizontal fusion are per-GPU and can be studied on one A5000.

title: Slapo: A Schedule Language for Progressive Optimization of Large Deep Learning Model Training
note: Schedule language decoupling PyTorch model definition from optimization. Concern - 3D-parallelism results need many GPUs; single-GPU primitives (kernel replacement, activation checkpointing) are still evaluable. Artifact repo is chhzh123/slapo-artifact.

title: TGLite: A Lightweight Programming Framework for Continuous-Time Temporal Graph Neural Networks
note: Lightweight framework and TBlock abstraction for continuous-time temporal GNNs; single-GPU evaluation against TGL.

title: 8-bit Transformer Inference and Fine-tuning for Edge Accelerators
note: Software FP8/Posit8 quantization-emulation library for Transformer inference and LoRA fine-tuning. Concern - Ampere has no native FP8 so numerics are emulated (which is what the artifact does anyway); the accompanying edge accelerator hardware results are out of reach.

title: AUDIBLE: A Convolution-Based Resource Allocator for Oversubscribing Burstable Virtual Machines
note: Burstable-VM oversubscription allocator evaluated by trace-driven simulation over production traces; CPU-only and squarely within the machine budget.

title: CSSTs: A Dynamic Data Structure for Partial Orders in Concurrent Execution Analysis
note: Collective Sparse Segment Trees, a drop-in replacement for vector clocks in dynamic concurrency analyses; user-space CPU-only library with a Zenodo artifact (10.5281/zenodo.10798906).

title: DTC-SpMM: Bridging the Gap in Accelerating General Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Tensor Cores
note: Tensor-core SpMM formats, reordering and pipelining; single modern NVIDIA GPU. Ampere tensor cores are supported.

title: EVT: Accelerating Deep Learning Training with Epilogue Visitor Tree
note: Epilogue Visitor Tree compiler for training-graph fusion built on CUTLASS; single GPU. Concern - CUTLASS templates were tuned for A100 (SM80); SM86 retuning may be needed.

title: Felix: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Gradient Descent
note: Gradient-descent search over a differentiable relaxation of TVM/Ansor schedules; evaluated on single GPUs and finishes searches in minutes, which suits a 10-week budget.

title: Flexible Non-intrusive Dynamic Instrumentation for WebAssembly
note: Non-intrusive bytecode-level dynamic instrumentation in the Wizard WebAssembly research engine; user-space, CPU-only, written in Virgil.

title: Getting a Handle on Unmanaged Memory
note: ALASKA - compiler plus runtime that adds handles to unmanaged C/C++ so the heap can be compacted; drop-in malloc replacement, user-space only. Main repo is nickwanninger/alaska.

title: Going Green for Less Green: Optimizing the Cost of Reducing Cloud Carbon Emissions
note: GAIA carbon-aware batch scheduler; the artifact ships both an AWS ParallelCluster driver and a pure simulation interface, and the simulator alone reproduces most figures on one machine.

title: Hector: An Efficient Programming and Compilation Framework for Implementing Relational Graph Neural Networks in GPU Architectures
note: Two-level IR and CUDA code generator for relational GNNs; single-GPU evaluation against DGL/PyG on OGB heterogeneous graphs.

title: MAGIS: Memory Optimization via Coordinated Graph Transformation and Scheduling for DNN
note: Coordinated graph transformation plus scheduling for DNN memory reduction; single-GPU, and memory-constrained studies are a natural fit for a 24 GB card.

title: Optimal Kernel Orchestration for Tensor Programs with Korch
note: Operator fission plus ILP-based kernel orchestration for DNN inference; evaluated on single V100/A100 GPUs, so an A5000 run is a direct scale-down.

title: PATHFINDER: Practical Real-Time Learning for Data Prefetching
note: Spiking-neural-network data prefetcher evaluated in ChampSim, which is a CPU-only trace-driven simulator that runs fine here. Concern - the paper also has an RTL/hardware cost analysis that cannot be reproduced.

title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
note: Tree-based speculative decoding and parallel verification for LLM serving; the offloading configuration is explicitly single-GPU, so 7B-class models fit in 24 GB. AE repo is goliaro/specinfer-ae.

title: FastGL: A GPU-Efficient Framework for Accelerating Sampling-Based GNN Training at Large Scale
note: GPU-efficient sampling, memory-IO and computation pipeline for large-scale GNN training on a single GPU with host-memory graph storage.

title: MaxEmbed: Maximizing SSD bandwidth utilization for huge embedding models serving
note: Maximizes NVMe bandwidth for SSD-resident embedding tables in recommendation serving; the machine has two PM9A3 NVMe drives. Concern - if the artifact needs SPDK-style raw device binding that requires root, an io_uring path would have to be used instead.

title: VertexSurge: Variable Length Graph Pattern Match on Billion-edge Graphs
note: Single-machine C++/TBB engine for variable-length graph pattern matching; builds with cmake and user-space libraries. Concern - billion-edge LDBC datasets need a lot of RAM and disk, so a smaller scale factor may be necessary.

title: Automatic Tracing in Task-Based Runtime Systems
note: Apophenia auto-traces dependence analysis in a user-space task-based runtime (Legion); runs on one node - concern: evaluated on supercomputers and no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Coach: Exploiting Temporal Patterns for All-Resource Oversubscription in Cloud Platforms
note: All-resource oversubscription policy for cloud VMs driven by Azure traces - can be replayed in a simulator; concern: no public artifact found in GitHub/web search so code availability is unclear

title: DarwinGame: Playing Tournaments for Tuning Applications in Noisy Cloud Environments
note: DarwinGame is a user-space performance tuner that runs tournaments between configurations under interference - interference can be emulated by co-located processes on one machine; Zenodo artifact released

title: Dilu: Enabling GPU Resourcing-on-Demand for Serverless DL Serving via Introspective Elasticity
note: GPU resourcing-on-demand for serverless DL serving - profiling plus 2D co-scaling; concern: paper uses a small GPU cluster but the elasticity mechanism is per-GPU and can be scaled to one A5000

title: Efficient Lossless Compression of Scientific Floating-Point Data on CPUs and GPUs
note: Four new lossless floating-point compressors, pure user-space CPU and single-GPU code; SDRBench inputs are downloadable; ideal scale for the machine

title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
note: Exo 2 user-schedulable scheduling language for high-performance kernels - user-space compiler, CPU targets, 80+ kernels as benchmarks

title: FleetIO: Managing Multi-Tenant Cloud Storage with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
note: Multi-agent RL controller for multi-tenant SSD virtualization - learned policy plus trace-driven evaluation; concern: likely needs an SSD emulator and no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Forecasting GPU Performance for Deep Learning Training and Inference
note: NeuSight predicts DL training/inference latency on unseen GPUs from tile-level models - pure user-space Python, needs only small profiling runs

title: Helix: Serving Large Language Models over Heterogeneous GPUs and Network via Max-Flow
note: Max-flow model placement plus request scheduling for LLM serving; concern: real runs need a heterogeneous 24-42 GPU cluster, but the released artifact contains a cluster simulator that fits one machine

title: Medusa: Accelerating Serverless LLM Inference with Materialization
note: Materialization to remove KV-cache init and CUDA-graph capture cold-start stages in serverless LLM inference - single-GPU mechanism

title: Mint: Cost-Efficient Tracing with All Requests Collection via Commonality and Variability Analysis
note: Trace-volume reduction via commonality/variability analysis, works offline over production trace data; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
note: CPU-GPU-IO pipelined MoE offloading evaluated on a single 16 GB T4 - directly reproducible on one 24 GB A5000. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/caoshiyi/artifacts/tree/asplos25 .

title: Optimizing Datalog for the GPU
note: GPUlog single-GPU Datalog engine with the HISA data structure - user-space CUDA; concern: repo is the authors' GPU-Datalog line (GDlog) so the exact ASPLOS-25 artifact branch needs checking, and some datasets need >24 GB

title: PartIR: Composing SPMD Partitioning Strategies for Machine Learning
note: PartIR SPMD partitioning IR with a predictable rewrite API and a simulator; concern: targets multi-device training and no public repo found by GitHub/web search

title: PCcheck: Persistent Concurrent Checkpointing for ML
note: Persistent concurrent checkpointing for ML training - user-space, works with one GPU and local NVMe

title: RASSM: Residue-based Acceleration of Single Sparse Matrix Computation via Adaptive Tiling
note: Adaptive 2D tiling for single-sparse-matrix CPU kernels (SpMM/SDDMM) - pure user-space CPU library that fits the 16-core machine; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Segue and ColorGuard: Optimizing SFI Performance and Scalability on Modern Architectures
note: Segue uses x86-64 segment bases and ColorGuard uses MPK - both are unprivileged user-space features available on this CPU; Wasm toolchains build from source; concern: the linked repo is the benchmark harness and the compiler changes live in forks of wasm2c/WAMR/Wasmtime

title: Selectively Uniform Concurrency Testing
note: Randomized concurrency-testing algorithm, pure user-space, cheap to run and easy to extend

title: SmoothE: Differentiable E-Graph Extraction
note: Differentiable (relaxation-based) e-graph extraction running on one GPU - a learned/continuous optimizer inside a compiler pass

title: Tally: Non-Intrusive Performance Isolation for Concurrent Deep Learning Workloads
note: Thread-block-level GPU kernel scheduling for concurrent DL workloads, implemented by intercepting CUDA in user space on a single GPU - excellent fit

title: Tela: A Temporal Load-Aware Cloud Virtual Disk Placement Scheme
note: Temporal load-aware placement of cloud virtual disks - trace-driven placement policy that can be replayed in a simulator; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
note: Contiguous virtual KV cache using CUDA virtual-memory APIs - single-GPU; concern: the finest-granularity variant ships a patched nvidia-uvm kernel module that we cannot load, but the 2 MB-granularity path uses only user-space CUDA APIs

title: Accelerating LLM Serving for Multi-turn Dialogues with Efficient Resource Management
note: KV reuse across dialogue turns plus a length-aware scheduling policy to avoid head-of-line blocking - single-GPU mechanism; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Cascade: A Dependency-aware Efficient Training Framework for Temporal Graph Neural Network
note: Dependency-aware batching/scheduling for temporal-GNN training - single-GPU training framework; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
note: W4A4KV4 serving with a mixed-precision W4Ax kernel; INT4 tensor cores exist on Ampere sm_86 so a single A5000 works; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (arXiv 2410.12168)

title: Concurrency-Informed Orchestration for Serverless Functions
note: CIDRE keep-alive/eviction policy for serverless containers evaluated against two production FaaS traces - reproducible as a trace-driven simulation; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: CoServe: Efficient Collaboration-of-Experts (CoE) Model Inference with Limited Memory
note: Serving many small expert models under a memory budget with expert placement/switching across memory tiers - fits 125 GiB RAM plus one GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Dynamic Partial Deadlock Detection and Recovery via Garbage Collection
note: GOLF detects partial deadlocks by reusing the Go GC mark phase - a user-space runtime/GC change, buildable from Go source in $HOME; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (deployed internally at Uber)

title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
note: Einsum Tree IR that globally optimizes data layout for tensor-contraction paths - CPU-only user-space compiler, evaluated on x86 desktop-class machines

title: Embracing Imbalance: Dynamic Load Shifting among Microservice Containers in Shared Clusters
note: Dynamic load shifting among microservice containers instead of load balancing - policy is trace/simulation friendly; concern: original evaluation is on a large shared cluster and no official repo was found

title: EXIST: Enabling Extremely Efficient Intra-Service Tracing Observability in Datacenters
note: Per-mille-overhead intra-service (application-level) tracing - user-space instrumentation and sampling; concern: may rely on hardware tracing support and no official repo was found

title: Gigaflow: Pipeline-Aware Sub-Traversal Caching for Modern SmartNICs
note: Pipeline-aware sub-traversal flow-cache design for vSwitches - the caching algorithm and its trace-driven evaluation are software; concern: the headline deployment is on a SmartNIC, so only the software vSwitch/simulation path is reproducible here

title: Klotski: Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference via Expert-Aware Multi-Batch Pipeline
note: Expert-aware multi-batch pipeline that removes bubbles in offloaded MoE inference - designed for a single memory-constrained GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (arXiv 2502.06888)

title: Load and MLP-Aware Thread Orchestration for Recommendation Systems Inference on CPUs
note: Thread orchestration for recommendation-model inference on CPUs - pure user-space on a 16-core machine; concerns: scheduling decisions may need hardware counters and no official repo was found

title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
note: Checkpointing/fault tolerance specialised for MoE training; the partial-experts checkpoint idea can be scaled down to one GPU; concerns: motivated by 10k-node training and no official repo was found

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference Efficiency through Block Dependency Analysis
note: BlockDepend adds block-level dependency analysis to an ML compiler for inter-operator fusion on one GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Past-Future Scheduler for LLM Serving under SLA Guarantees
note: Peak-memory-aware continuous-batching scheduler using historical output-length distributions - a pure scheduling-policy change inside a serving engine on one GPU; the authors released it inside the LightLLM serving framework

title: POD-Attention: Unlocking Full Prefill-Decode Overlap for Faster LLM Inference
note: POD-Attention is a single fused CUDA attention kernel that overlaps prefill and decode - single GPU, FlashAttention-2 style so Ampere is fine; artifact lives in the vAttention repo under pod_attn

title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
note: Draft-then-verify search plus online cost-model adaptation for tensor-program tuning (TVM/Ansor) - single-GPU, and the learned cost model is exactly the kind of component a course project can improve

title: Relax: Composable Abstractions for End-to-End Dynamic Machine Learning
note: Relax cross-level compiler abstraction with first-class symbolic shapes, upstreamed into Apache TVM - user-space, one GPU is enough

title: TAPAS: Thermal- and Power-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference in Cloud Platforms
note: Thermal/power-aware placement of LLM inference across a cloud fleet - the policy is simulator-friendly; concerns: original evaluation needs datacenter power/thermal telemetry and no public artifact was found

title: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications with Ayo
note: Primitive-level dataflow orchestration of LLM applications (RAG etc.) - user-space orchestration layer over a single-GPU engine

title: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
note: User-space simulation methodology for virtual-memory research - runs entirely on CPU, no root, and is explicitly built as a research platform to extend

title: DeepContext: A Context-aware, Cross-platform, and Cross-framework Tool for Performance Profiling and Analysis of Deep Learning Workloads
note: Cross-stack profiler correlating Python, framework, C++ and GPU contexts for DL workloads; concerns: GPU hardware counters via CUPTI usually need admin-enabled profiling and CPU perf counters are blocked here, and no official repo was found

title: HybridTier: an Adaptive and Lightweight CXL-Memory Tiering System
note: Lightweight user-space memory-tiering policy with probabilistic hotness tracking; concern: the slow tier is a real CXL device in the paper, so on this machine it must be emulated (e.g. with a slower backing store or cgroup limits) since there is only one NUMA node

title: λ-trim: Optimizing Function Initialization in Serverless Applications With Cost-driven Debloating
note: Static analysis plus cost-driven debloating of Python serverless applications - pure user-space pipeline; concerns: end-to-end cost numbers need a real FaaS account and no official repo was found

title: Neuralink: Fast on-Device LLM Inference with Neuron Co-Activation Linking
note: Co-activation-aware neuron placement in flash for sparse on-device LLM inference; the placement/caching idea transfers to NVMe-backed offloaded inference; concerns: original evaluation targets smartphone flash IOPS and no official repo was found

title: Syno: Structured Synthesis for Neural Operators
note: Automatic synthesis of new neural operators with a guided search plus tensor-compiler backend - single-GPU search and evaluation; a separate artifact repo (Yongqi-Zhuo/Syno-AE) also exists. MERGE NOTE: the same paper (identical title and DOI 10.1145/3676642.3736118) is also row 21 of the asplos-2026 report, which notes it was published in ASPLOS 2025 Volume 3 and presented at ASPLOS 2026; the asplos-2026 row was folded into this one. That scout's text: "Structured synthesis of neural operators; search plus single-GPU kernel evaluation. Published in ASPLOS 2025 Volume 3 and presented at ASPLOS 2026."

title: TempGraph: An Efficient Chain-driven Temporal Graph Computing Framework on the GPU
note: Chain-driven temporal-graph framework on one GPU with a Generate-Activate-Compute execution model - user-space CUDA; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Voyager: Input-Adaptive Algebraic Transformations for High-Performance Graph Neural Networks
note: Input-adaptive algebraic (reorder/fuse) transformations for GNN execution on one GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Bullet: Boosting GPU Utilization for LLM Serving via Dynamic Spatial-Temporal Orchestration
note: Single-GPU spatial-temporal sharing of prefill and decode - exactly the kind of intra-GPU serving mechanism one A5000 can host with a 7B model

title: QoServe: Breaking the Silos of LLM Inference Serving
note: QoS-driven scheduling on top of Sarathi-Serve; artifact is the niyama_asplos2026 branch. Concern: paper evaluates an A100 cluster so a single-replica scale-down is needed

title: PAT: Accelerating LLM Decoding via Prefix-Aware Attention with Resource Efficient Multi-Tile Kernel
note: Prefix-aware attention decode kernel; pure CUDA/Triton kernel work that runs on one Ampere GPU. Zenodo AE artifact 10.5281/zenodo.18217189

title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression
note: Lossless weight compression plus fused decompress-GEMM kernels; Tensor-Core path exists on Ampere. Concern: FP8/FP4 variants would need Ada or Hopper

title: SNIP: An Adaptive Mixed Precision Framework for Subbyte Large Language Model Training
note: Adaptive mixed-precision LLM training policy; authors themselves evaluate with a pseudo-quantization proxy because they lack Blackwell, so it is GPU-portable. Concern: pretraining compute must be scaled to small models

title: SpecProto: A Parallelizing Compiler for Speculative Decoding of Large Protocol Buffers Data
note: Parallelizing compiler for Protobuf decoding; CPU-only artifact that targets 16 physical cores which this machine has

title: GFS: A Preemption-aware Scheduling Framework for GPU Clusters with Predictive Spot Instance Management
note: Preemption-aware GPU-cluster scheduler with demand forecasting; policy work that can be studied trace-driven or in simulation. Concern: repo has no README yet and the paper evaluates a real cluster

title: Insum: Sparse GPU Kernels Simplified and Optimized with Indirect Einsums
note: Sparse GPU kernel compiler lowering indirect Einsums through the PyTorch compiler; single-GPU, user-space

title: MoDM: Efficient Serving for Image Generation via Mixture-of-Diffusion Models
note: Caching-based serving for diffusion models; retrieval cache plus small/large model mix. Concern: artifact assumes a 48 GB A40 so SDXL-class models need scale-down or offload on 24 GB

title: FastTTS: Accelerating Test-Time Scaling for Edge LLM Reasoning
note: Test-time-scaling serving framework built as a vLLM plug-in for memory-constrained devices; a 24 GB GPU is a realistic target

title: GS-Scale: Unlocking Large-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Host Offloading
note: Host-offloading 3DGS training explicitly aimed at consumer GPUs; 125 GiB host RAM plus one 24 GB GPU is the intended setting

title: CLM: Removing the GPU Memory Barrier for 3D Gaussian Splatting
note: CPU-offloading for 3DGS on a single consumer GPU - the paper itself targets one RTX 4090

title: Triton-Sanitizer: A Fast and Device-Agnostic Memory Sanitizer for Triton with Rich Diagnostic Context
note: Device-agnostic memory sanitizer for Triton kernels; user-space, single GPU. Concern: the AE scripts assume a ROCm Docker image so the NVIDIA path needs porting since Docker is unavailable

title: Trinity: Three-Dimensional Tensor Program Optimization via Tile-level Equality Saturation
note: Tile-level equality saturation tensor compiler emitting Triton kernels; single-GPU compile-and-benchmark loop

title: Linear Layouts: Robust Code Generation of Efficient Tensor Computation Using F2
note: Linear-algebra formulation of tensor layouts inside the Triton compiler; implementation is upstream in Triton so it builds and runs on one Ampere GPU

title: It Takes Two to Entangle
note: Equivalence checker that relates sequential and distributed ML computation graphs; the artifact itself is a user-space analysis tool. Concern: the motivating bugs come from multi-GPU training runs

title: Tilus: A Tile-Level GPGPU Programming Language for Low-Precision Computation
note: Tile-level GPGPU DSL for low-precision kernels; Ampere is a supported target. Concern: some tutorials target Blackwell-only features

title: LPO: Discovering Missed Peephole Optimizations with Large Language Models
note: LLM proposes LLVM peephole rewrites that Alive2 verifies; entirely user-space and CPU-bound. Concern: needs an LLM API budget and is closer to compilers than to classic systems

title: Nemo: A Low-Write-Amplification Cache for Tiny Objects on Log-Structured Flash Devices
note: Set-associative flash-cache design built as a CacheLib module; runs in user space on the local NVMe drives

title: CacheMind: From Miss Rates to Why – Natural-Language, Trace-Grounded Reasoning for Cache Replacement
note: LLM plus RAG reasoning over cache traces with a released benchmark; trace-driven and CPU-only. Concern: the repo is author-named and not linked from the paper so ownership is unconfirmed

title: LOOPRAG: Enhancing Loop Transformation Optimization with Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
note: Retrieval-augmented LLM loop transformation with compile-and-check validation; CPU-only pipeline

title: cuJSON: A Highly Parallel JSON Parser for GPUs
note: Massively parallel JSON parser for GPUs; user-space single-GPU artifact

title: Lobster: A GPU-Accelerated Framework for Neurosymbolic Programming
note: End-to-end GPU execution of a Datalog-based neurosymbolic language; user-space, single GPU

title: Skyler: Static Analysis for Predicting API-Driven Costs in Serverless Applications
note: Static cost analysis tool for serverless applications; user-space Java/Python tooling. Concern: it is a static analyzer rather than a runtime system so the improvement axis is analysis precision

title: Wax: Optimizing Data Center Applications With Stale Profile
note: Matching stale profiles to new binaries for data-center PGO; user-space compiler work. Concern: collecting fresh profiles normally needs perf/LBR sampling which is blocked, so the project depends on the shipped profiles

title: M2XFP: A Metadata-Augmented Microscaling Data Format for Efficient Low-bit Quantization
note: Metadata-augmented microscaling quantization; the released artifact is a pseudo-quantization and perplexity workflow on vLLM that fits one 24 GB GPU. Concern: the speedup claims rest on a hardware unit that cannot be built here

title: Cheddar: A Swift Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library Designed for GPU Architectures
note: CUDA CKKS library; pure user-space GPU code that fits a single A5000

title: CHEHAB RL: Learning to Optimize Fully Homomorphic Encryption Computations
note: Reinforcement learning to drive an FHE compiler optimizer; CPU-only, user-space learned-tuning system

title: CEMU: Enabling Full-System Emulation of Computational Storage beyond Hardware Limits
note: Emulator for computational-storage devices, a user-space storage research vehicle. Concern: QEMU-based full-system emulation without /dev/kvm falls back to TCG and will be slow

title: Pre-train and Search: Efficient Embedding Table Sharding with Pre-trained Neural Cost Models
note: Learned cost model plus search for DLRM embedding-table sharding - training the cost model and running the search is a single-GPU offline workload driven by the public dlrm_datasets traces - concern - the end-to-end payoff was measured on a production multi-terabyte DLRM so only the benchmark-dataset results are reproducible here

title: FedTree: A Federated Learning System For Trees
note: Tree-based federated GBDT training system in C++ or CUDA - parties are simulated as processes on one host and the datasets are small - concern - homomorphic-encryption modes are slow and the secure-aggregation parts add build dependencies

title: Hotline Profiler: Automatic Annotation and A Multi-Scale Timeline for Visualizing Time-Use in DNN Training
note: Profiler that annotates standard PyTorch or Chrome trace data with DNN training-loop and model structure - explicitly avoids vendor-specific tools so it needs no perf counters and no root - concern - visualization front end plus a Zenodo artifact so check the trace collector still works with current PyTorch

title: GiPH: Generalizable Placement Learning for Adaptive Heterogeneous Computing
note: Learned device-placement policy evaluated on synthetic task graphs and simulated heterogeneous device clusters - the whole evaluation is a simulator plus a GNN policy that trains on one GPU - concern - the simulator fidelity is the main threat to any improvement claim

title: SIRIUS: Harvesting Whole-Program Optimization Opportunities for DNNs
note: Whole-program polyhedral compiler fusing host and kernel code for DNN inference on one NVIDIA GPU - single-GPU evaluation against TensorRT and TVM - concern - the artifact appendix ships the source inside a Docker image mirrored on Zenodo and on Docker Hub as sunqianqi/sirius - Docker is not installed here so it must be rebuilt from source with LLVM 16 and PipLib in user space - the Zenodo record did not respond when checked on 2026-09-13

title: MegaBlocks: Efficient Sparse Training with Mixture-of-Experts
note: Block-sparse GPU kernels for MoE layers - the kernels and the no-token-dropping formulation are single-GPU contributions and the artifact claims a 30 second microbenchmark - concern - paper uses A100 and Docker so it needs a user-space rebuild and the Ampere A5000 has less bandwidth and no A100-class shared memory

title: Safe Optimized Static Memory Allocation for Parallel Deep Learning
note: Static tensor-offset allocation solver that minimizes peak memory for parallel execution streams - a compile-time combinatorial problem that runs on CPU and is a clean target for a better solver - concern - it was upstreamed into MindSpore rather than released as a standalone artifact so locating and rebuilding the solver inside MindSpore is a real cost

title: X-RLFLOW: GRAPH REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR NEURAL NETWORK SUBGRAPHS TRANSFORMATION
note: Reinforcement-learning agent replacing greedy search in tensor-graph superoptimization on top of TASO - runs on one GPU with small models - concern - depends on building TASO which is an older CUDA or cuDNN codebase

title: Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models
note: Selective activation recomputation and sequence parallelism in Megatron-LM - selective recomputation is a per-layer memory-versus-recompute policy that scales down meaningfully to one GPU with a small GPT - concern - the headline results use 530B models on 2240 A100s and sequence parallelism itself needs tensor parallelism so only the selective-recompute half is reproducible here

title: HyperGef: A Framework Enabling Efficient Fusion for Hypergraph Neural Network on GPUs
note: Fused GPU kernels and a workload-aware sparse format for hypergraph neural networks - single-GPU kernel work compared against cuSPARSE - concern - graph datasets must be sized to 24 GB and the kernels may need retuning for Ampere consumer-class shared memory

title: ApproxCaliper: A Programmable Framework for Application-aware Neural Network Optimization
note: Framework that prunes and quantizes networks against application-level goals rather than accuracy alone - the optimization pipeline runs on one GPU - concern - two of the case studies are a commercial agriculture robot and an electric-cart simulation so the application-level feedback loop may not be fully reproducible

title: Transcending Runtime-Memory Tradeoffs in Checkpointing by being Fusion Aware
note: Fusion-aware min-cut rematerialization for gradient checkpointing - a pure single-GPU memory-versus-runtime optimization evaluated on TorchBench with TorchInductor - concern - the implementation was upstreamed into PyTorch AOTAutograd as the min-cut partitioner rather than released as a standalone repo so the baseline is now the default and the improvement must beat current PyTorch

title: Exploiting Hardware Utilization and Adaptive Dataflow for Efficient Sparse Convolution in 3D Point Clouds
note: Sparse-convolution engine for 3D point clouds with a coded-CSR format and adaptive dataflow - single-GPU kernel work with released code - concern - point-cloud datasets such as SemanticKITTI are large and the CUDA code targets older toolkits

title: Learning to Parallelize with OpenMP by Augmented Heterogeneous AST Representation
note: Learned detector for OpenMP-parallelizable loops using an augmented heterogeneous AST - CPU-only training and inference on a released dataset - concern - the contribution is a model plus dataset rather than a running system and only the OMP_Serial dataset is clearly released by the authors so the official model code is uncertain

title: Validating Large Language Models with ReLM
note: System that compiles regular expressions into constrained decoding over an LLM - single-GPU inference on GPT-2 or GPT-J class models and a direct ancestor of todays structured-generation stacks - concern - the largest models in the paper need quantization to fit 24 GB

title: Communication-Efficient Graph Neural Networks with Probabilistic Neighborhood Expansion Analysis and Caching
note: VIP-based caching policy that decides which remote vertex features to cache and which to keep in GPU memory for minibatch GNN training - the caching analysis and the GPU feature cache are meaningful on one GPU with a partitioned graph in host memory - concern - the published speedups come from a multi-machine setting so cross-partition transfers must be emulated between processes

title: Efficient GPU Kernels for N:M-Sparse Weights in Deep Learning
note: GPU SpMV and SpMM kernels for general N to M sparse weights - pure single-GPU kernel work in the nmsparse_artifact branch of SparTA - concern - evaluated on A100 and the artifact uses Docker so it needs a user-space rebuild and retuning for Ampere consumer cards. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/nmsparse_artifact .

title: Cuttlefish: Low-Rank Model Training without All the Tuning
note: Automated low-rank training that picks per-layer ranks from observed stable rank - end-to-end training runs on one GPU on CIFAR or ImageNet-scale vision and small transformer models - concern - the contribution is closer to a training method than a systems artifact and full ImageNet training may exceed the time budget

title: Renee: END-TO-END TRAINING OF EXTREME CLASSIFICATION MODELS
note: End-to-end training system for extreme classification with GPU memory and throughput optimizations - the paper runs on one to four A100s and smaller XC benchmarks fit a single 24 GB GPU - concern - the largest label sets in the paper will not fit so scale-down to medium benchmarks is required

title: Unified Convolution Framework: A compiler-based approach to support sparse convolutions
note: TACO-based compiler that expresses many sparse convolution variants through affine index expressions - CPU and single-GPU code generation with a Zenodo and GitHub artifact - concern - builds a TACO fork with cmake and LLVM which is a user-space build but not a trivial one

title: ALCOP: Automatic Load-Compute Pipelining in Deep Learning Compiler for AI-GPUs
note: Compiler-native multi-stage multi-level load-compute pipelining in TVM plus an analytic performance model for schedule search - entirely single-GPU kernel generation - concern - pinned to an older TVM and CUDA and the pipelining depth assumptions target A100 so Ampere consumer retuning is part of the work

title: GlueFL: Reconciling Client Sampling and Model Masking for Bandwidth Efficient Federated Learning
note: Federated training framework built on FedScale that combines sticky client sampling with bounded-change compression masks - the evaluation is trace-driven FedScale simulation which fits one GPU - concern - the contribution is mostly algorithmic and the reported runs used a multi-GPU simulation cluster so rounds must be scaled down

title: Building Verified Neural Networks for Computer Systems with Ouroboros
note: Training-verification loop that produces neural networks with provable safety properties for systems tasks such as learned indexes and caching - artifact states no specific hardware is required with a 1 to 5 hour experiment time - concern - depends on Julia plus NeuralVerification.jl and the verification step is CPU-heavy

title: Punica: Multi-Tenant LoRA Serving
note: Multi-tenant LoRA serving; the core artifact is the SGMV CUDA kernel plus a batching/scheduling layer, both of which work on one GPU. Concern - the paper's scheduler evaluation uses a small GPU cluster; on a single 24 GB A5000 the scale-down is a 7B base model with many adapters. Kernels are sm_80+ Ampere-friendly.

title: ACROBAT: Optimizing Auto-batching of Dynamic Deep Learning at Compile Time
note: Compiler + runtime for auto-batching dynamic DNNs; paper's own evaluation is a single RTX 3070, so the machine is a superset. Concern - no code URL in the paper; the repo is the first author's undocumented TVM fork (last push 2022), so a from-source TVM/CUDA build is a real risk, and baselines DyNet/Cavs must also be built.

title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
note: Weight-only 4-bit quantization plus the TinyChat W4A16 inference engine - a user-space, single-GPU artifact. Concern - the 70B-on-mobile headline is out of reach; scale-down to 7B/13B on the A5000 is the realistic target. Widely used code, low build risk.

title: Keyformer: KV Cache reduction through key tokens selection for Efficient Generative Inference
note: KV-cache eviction policy (key-token selection) for decode-phase memory/bandwidth - exactly the llm-inference topic and single-GPU by nature. Concern - accuracy evaluation on long-context summarization benchmarks costs GPU hours; 7B-class models only.

title: Atom: Low-Bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
note: W4A4 mixed-precision quantization with custom kernels integrated into a serving path; single-GPU throughput study. Concern - INT4 mma tensor-core paths are supported on sm_86 but the kernels were tuned on A100/RTX4090, so kernel performance on the A5000 needs re-tuning; no code URL in the PDF but the official repo is labelled "[MLSys'24] Atom" by the authors' lab.

title: SiDA: Sparsity-Inspired Data-Aware Serving for Efficient and Scalable Large Mixture-of-Experts Models
note: MoE inference that offloads dormant experts to host DRAM and predicts expert activation - a GPU-memory/host-memory tiering problem that suits 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM very well. Code URL given in the abstract. Concern - training the expert-activation predictor adds an offline cost; largest MoEs in the paper must be scaled down.

title: VQPy: An Object-Oriented Approach to Modern Video Analytics
note: Python front-end plus an extensible backend that builds and optimizes video-analytics pipelines (detector/tracker cascades, frame filtering) - entirely user space, one GPU. Concern - reproducing the query set needs public video datasets and YOLO-class weights; gains are pipeline-optimization gains, so a hypothesis must be framed around the backend optimizer.

title: SLoRA: Scalable Serving of Thousands of LoRA Adapters
note: Unified paged memory pool for adapter weights + KV cache, adapter prefetch from host memory, custom batched-LoRA kernels; the paper explicitly claims single-GPU operation. Strong fit for a memory-management or admission-policy improvement. Concern - tensor-parallel experiments are multi-GPU and must be dropped.

title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
note: Precomputed, reusable attention states for repeated prompt segments - a caching/TTFT problem evaluated on single GPU and even CPU. Small, readable prototype; obvious improvement axes (cache admission/eviction, positional handling). Concern - the schema-based reuse can perturb output quality, so an improvement claim needs an accuracy control.

title: VIDUR: A LARGE-SCALE SIMULATION FRAMEWORK FOR LLM INFERENCE
note: LLM-inference simulator + benchmark suite: schedulers, batching policies and parallelism can be studied without a cluster, which is ideal for a one-machine project. Released profiling data avoids needing the original hardware. Concern - validating the simulator against real runs on an A5000 requires re-profiling operators locally; multi-GPU configurations remain simulation-only.

title: Q-Hitter: A Better Token Oracle for Efficient LLM Inference via Sparse-Quantized KV Cache
note: Joint KV-cache sparsification + quantization (quantization-friendly heavy hitters); repo link is in the paper. Single-GPU, 7B-class models. Concern - much of the released code is accuracy-side; end-to-end throughput/memory gains may need to be wired into a serving engine by the team.

title: Proteus: Preserving Model Confidentiality during Graph Optimizations
note: Partitions a DNN computation graph and hides subgraphs among generated decoys so a third party can still run compiler/graph optimizations - a user-space compiler artifact (artifact repo published, with a Dockerfile that can be read and reproduced via conda). Concern - the headline metric is confidentiality, not speed, so a performance hypothesis has to target obfuscation cost or preserved optimization quality; measuring the latter means running autotuning, which is GPU-hour heavy.

title: QMoE: Sub-1-Bit Compression of Trillion Parameter Models
note: Sub-1-bit MoE compression format with bespoke GPU decoding kernels for compressed inference - the decode kernel and format work on one GPU. Concern - the SwitchTransformer-c2048 headline needs 3.2 TB of weights and a 160 GB output, which does not fit the ~257 GB free disk or the download budget; only the smaller Switch base/large-128 models are realistic, so the project must be framed around the kernel/format at reduced scale.

title: COMET: Neural Cost Model Explanation Framework
note: Explanations for learned basic-block cost models (Ithemal vs uiCA) - a learned component inside a compiler toolchain, CPU-only and cheap to run on 16 cores. Open-sourced in the paper. Concern - ground-truth throughputs come from the published BHive dataset measured on other microarchitectures; re-measuring on this Threadripper is not possible with perf_event_paranoid=3, so the study must stay dataset-based.

title: On Latency Predictors for Neural Architecture Search
note: Learned hardware-latency predictors (device representations, sample selection, operation encodings) trained on published latency datasets - an ML-for-systems artifact that fits one GPU comfortably. Concern - the URL printed in the paper (abdelfattah-lab/nasflat) 404s; the live lab repo nasflat_latency is the released code and should be confirmed at audit. The contribution is measured with prediction-accuracy metrics rather than system throughput.

title: Graph Learning at Scale: Characterizing and Optimizing Pre-Propagation GNNs
note: GNN training-system characterization plus data-loading and training optimizations - artifact is user-space PyTorch/DGL and the PP-GNN design decouples propagation so a single A5000 is enough for medium graphs - concern: largest OGB graphs need tens of GB of disk and host RAM

title: LeanAttention: Hardware-Aware Scalable Attention Mechanism for the Decode-Phase of Transformers
note: Exact decode-phase attention kernel (stream-K style splitting) - pure CUDA kernel work on one GPU - concerns: no standalone repo, the official implementation is the LeanAttention kernel merged into ONNX Runtime contrib_ops/cuda/bert, and paper numbers are on A100/H100 so absolute speedups on Ampere A5000 will differ

title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
note: Measurement plus released tooling for KV-cache compression in serving - artifact is a reusable benchmark harness, paper used a single A6000 so a single 24 GB A5000 works with 7-8B models - concern: a few configs were sized for 48 GB

title: Rubick: Exploiting Job Reconfigurability for Deep Learning Cluster Scheduling
note: DL cluster scheduler exploiting job reconfigurability - artifact ships a cluster simulator driven by pre-measured throughput tables so the scheduling policy can be studied without the 64-GPU cluster - concerns: repo is named Morphling, AE path assumes Docker but conda setup instructions are also provided

title: SparseTransX: Efficient Training of Translation-Based Knowledge Graph Embeddings Using Sparse Matrix Operations
note: Replaces scatter/gather embedding kernels with SpMM in knowledge-graph embedding training - CPU and single-GPU results, low GPU memory footprint - good fit for one node

title: Interference-aware Edge Runtime Prediction with Conformal Matrix Completion
note: Learned interference-aware runtime prediction (conformal matrix completion) - training and evaluation are offline on the released WebAssembly runtime dataset (also on Zenodo record 14977004) so no edge fleet is needed to reproduce the model

title: DiffServe: Efficiently Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Query-Aware Model Scaling
note: Diffusion-model serving with query-aware cascades - cascade and scheduling logic is user-space Python and SD-class models fit in 24 GB - concern: paper evaluates a multi-GPU serving cluster so a single-GPU scale-down changes the resource-allocation experiments

title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
note: Memory-efficient optimizer - drop-in AdamW replacement, 60M-1B LLaMA pre-training runs fit one 24 GB GPU and memory savings are directly measurable - concern: headline 7B numbers need multi-GPU

title: The Hidden Bloat in Machine Learning Systems
note: User-space debloating of ML framework shared libraries including GPU fatbins - no root, no kernel, measures file size, memory and runtime - excellent fit for this machine (repo redirects from negativa-ai/negativa-ml)

title: HyC-LoRA: Memory Efficient LoRA Fine-tuning with Hybrid Activation Compression
note: Activation-compression LoRA fine-tuning - explicitly targets single memory-constrained devices, 7B LoRA with 2-bit buffered activations fits 24 GB - Triton kernels, user space

title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
note: Constrained-decoding engine - grammar compilation is CPU-side and overlapped with GPU decode, runs with any single-GPU serving backend - widely deployed so baselines are easy to get

title: FlexAttention: A Programming Model for Generating Fused Attention Variants.
note: Compiler-driven programming model for fused attention variants - shipped in PyTorch core with attention-gym as the paper artifact, single GPU - concern: Ampere means no FP8 variants and torch.compile kernel quality differs from H100 numbers

title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
note: CPU-offloaded attention and KV cache for online LLM inference - explicitly designed for one GPU plus host CPU, evaluated on T4/A10G which are weaker than the A5000, and the 16-core/125 GB host is exactly the regime it targets

title: AdaParse: An Adaptive Parallel PDF Parsing and Resource Scaling Engine
note: Adaptive PDF-parsing and resource-scaling engine for building training corpora - user-space Python parsers plus a learned parser selector - concern: paper scales on an HPC cluster, so single-node runs need a reduced document set

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
note: Prefix-cache admission and eviction policy for hybrid LLMs - the artifact is a trace-driven Python simulator so the whole evaluation runs on CPU, with the GPU only needed for optional end-to-end checks - ideal project target

title: Venn: Resource Management For Collaborative Learning Jobs
note: Resource manager for collaborative-learning jobs - conda-based simulator over device traces, no cluster needed - repo name Venn matches the paper even though the system is called Auxo in the text

title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
note: 3-bit MoE quantization with low-rank compensators and Tensor-Core kernels - Ampere supports the INT-based kernels - concern: Mixtral-8x7B at 3 bits is roughly 20 GB so it only just fits 24 GB and calibration-free quantization still needs large host RAM

title: FastTree: Optimizing Attention Kernel and Runtime for Tree-Structured LLM Inference
note: Radix-tree-aware attention kernels and runtime on top of SGLang - artifact states the Triton kernels use no Hopper-specific features, so an Ampere GPU works with reduced absolute numbers

title: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
note: Memory-efficient cascade training for federated adversarial training - evaluation is a single-machine FL simulation with per-device memory budgets - concern: more an algorithm/system hybrid, and edge-device memory claims are emulated rather than measured on real devices
