title: Efficient LLM Inference using Dynamic Input Pruning and Cache-Aware Masking
note: Dynamic input pruning plus cache-aware masking for memory-bound decoding - predictor-free, evaluated with simulated memory hierarchies so it runs on one GPU - concern: Phi-3-Medium at FP16 exceeds 24 GB, use the 7-8B configurations

title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
note: Row and field reordering to maximize KV-cache reuse for batch LLM analytics queries - works against a single-GPU vLLM instance with Llama-3-8B and the win is measured as job completion time - reordering algorithm itself is CPU-side. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory/branch https://github.com/lynnliu030/artifact-eval/tree/llmsql .

title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
note: Unified static plus dynamic sparse attention for long-context serving - Llama-3-8B fits 24 GB and the kernels are Ampere-compatible INT/FP16 - concern: shared OmniServe repo with QServe, and the longest-context configs assume 40-80 GB GPUs

title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
note: Customizable attention engine with block-sparse KV layouts and JIT templates - single GPU, Ampere supported, integrated into vLLM/SGLang so both baselines and improvement targets are easy - concern: some kernels are tuned for Hopper

title: QServe:W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
note: W4A8KV4 quantization with co-designed GPU kernels - INT4/INT8 Tensor Cores exist on Ampere (no FP8 needed) and 7-8B models fit 24 GB - concern: paper headline results use A100/L40S, and the repo is shared with LServe

title: CDLM: Consistency Diffusion Language Models for Faster Sampling
note: Diffusion-LM sampling acceleration with block-causal masks that restore KV-cache compatibility - pure inference-side systems angle. Concern: the consistency fine-tuning stage targets 7-8B diffusion LMs and likely needs more than one 24 GB GPU; released checkpoints make the inference/KV-cache half reproducible on the A5000

title: Massive-Scale Out-Of-Core UMAP on the GPU
note: Out-of-core GPU UMAP with an explicit single-GPU result (22.7x); batching/spilling strategy is the contribution and is squarely user-space CUDA. Concerns: multi-GPU is optional but is where the headline 74x comes from and the largest datasets exceed the ~257 GB free on /home so scale-down is needed

title: GriNNder: Breaking the Memory Capacity Wall in Full-Graph GNN Training with Storage Offloading
note: Full-graph GNN training on a single server by offloading to NVMe SSDs - designed exactly for the limited-GPU-memory single-node setting. Concerns: NVMe is software RAID and shared and only ~257 GB is free so the largest graphs will not fit; uses kvikio/GPUDirect-style paths that may fall back to buffered I/O without privileges

title: ExecuTorch - A Unified PyTorch Solution to Run ML Models On-Device
note: PyTorch-native on-device runtime - memory planning, operator/backend registry, quantization workflows are all user-space and buildable from source. Concerns: most of the evaluation is on phones, NPUs and MCUs that are unavailable; only the portable/XNNPACK/CUDA backends can be exercised here

title: EarthSight: A Distributed Framework for Low-Latency Satellite Intelligence
note: Ground-station query scheduler plus dynamic filter ordering, evaluated with a Python constellation simulator, so the scheduling contribution is trace/simulation driven and fits one machine. Concerns: the paper says EarthSight is open-sourced but no repository URL appears in the PDF, hyperlinks or GitHub search, so the repo is unknown

title: XProf: An Open, Scalable, and Extensible Profiling System for the Modern ML Stack
note: Open profiler for the OpenXLA stack; host-side trace collection, roofline analysis and the pluggable PJRT profiler API are user-space. Concerns: GPU-side counter collection goes through CUPTI, which NVIDIA restricts to admin users by default, and the paper's value proposition is fleet-scale TPU profiling that cannot be reproduced

title: Breaking the Ice: Analyzing Cold Start Latency in vLLM
note: Near-ideal fit: characterizes vLLM cold-start as a predominantly CPU-bound six-step process on one GPU, ships benchmark scripts and an analytical model. Improvement axis (cutting startup latency, better prediction) is directly testable on the A5000

title: FlashInfer-Bench: Building the Virtuous Cycle for AI-driven LLM Systems
note: Closed-loop harness for LLM-generated GPU kernels with correctness/performance checks and hot-swap into vLLM or SGLang; a single GPU is enough to run the loop. Concerns: several curated traces and reference kernels assume Hopper-class features that Ampere lacks, and agent runs need paid LLM API budget

title: Stream2LLM: Overlap Context Streaming and Prefill for Reduced Time-to-First-Token
note: Streaming-context scheduling and preemption for LLM serving with a Zenodo-archived artifact and public workload datasets. Concern: the design assumes prefill-decode disaggregated deployments, so reproducing it on one 24 GB GPU needs small models and two co-located instances

title: SkipKV: Selective Skipping of KV Generation and Storage for Efficient Inference with Large Reasoning Models
note: Training-free sentence-level KV eviction plus steering-vector generation control for reasoning models; single GPU, released code. Concern: the strongest results use large reasoning models, so 7-8B or quantized variants are needed to stay within 24 GB

title: Wave: A Symbolic Python DSL And Compiler for High-Performance Machine Learning
note: Python-embedded kernel DSL and compiler that automates matrix-core address computation; open source under iree-org and buildable in user space. Concerns: the primary backend is AMD CDNA, so NVIDIA Ampere support is the risk to check first, and the toolchain needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR build

title: Automated Algorithm Design for Auto-Tuning Optimizers
note: LLM-synthesized optimization algorithms for auto-tuning search spaces; BLADE plus Kernel Tuner run entirely in user space and the tuning targets include ordinary CUDA kernels. Concerns: the paper sweeps six hardware platforms - only one GPU is available here - and generation requires LLM API budget

title: Event Tensor: A Unified Abstraction for Compiling Dynamic Megakernel
note: Compiler abstraction for dynamic megakernels that removes launch overhead in LLM inference; the mechanism is single-GPU persistent-kernel scheduling and fits the A5000 well. Concerns: the paper only states ETC was 'incorporated into a major open-source system' without naming a repository, so the code location is unknown

title: MLCommons Chakra: Advancing Performance Benchmarking and Co-design using Standardized Execution Traces
note: Open trace schema plus collection/generation/replay tooling with an mlsys26 branch and Zenodo archive; trace analysis and ASTRA-sim style simulation run on one machine. Concerns: the traces themselves come from large production clusters, so any new work here is simulation- or replay-based rather than measured

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
note: Systematic vLLM-based study of n-gram, EAGLE/EAGLE-3, draft-model and MTP speculative decoding, with a released vLLM fork and simulator - a clean reproduction-or-improve target. Concerns: the study's large-batch and large-model points need more than 24 GB, so the hypothesis must be re-tested at a smaller scale

title: BatchLLM: Optimizing Large Batched LLM Inference with Global Prefix Sharing and Throughput-oriented Token Batching
note: Offline large-batch inference with global prefix identification and throughput-oriented token batching, released as a vLLM 0.6.4 fork. Throughput-oriented offline batching is one of the few serving regimes that a single 24 GB GPU can study honestly. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/microsoft/MixLLM/tree/batchllm_vllm_064 .

title: SwiftGS: Algorithm and System Co-Optimization for Fast 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
note: Single-GPU 3D Gaussian Splatting co-optimization (adaptive early sorting, axis-shared rasterization, dynamic thresholding) against the gsplat baseline, with code and a Zenodo benchmark archive. Ampere is a supported target

title: Accelerating Large-Scale Reasoning Model Inference with Sparse Self-Speculative Decoding
note: Self-speculative decoding using a sparse-attention draft plus unified scheduling, delayed verification and dynamic KV management - all single-GPU systems mechanisms. Concern: headline numbers use 32B-class reasoning models that do not fit 24 GB in FP16, so scale-down or quantization is required

title: StreamDiffusionV2: A Streaming System for Dynamic and Interactive Video Generation
note: Training-free streaming video-diffusion serving with an SLO-aware batching scheduler, block scheduler and rolling KV cache; the scheduling core runs on one GPU. Concern: the near-linear FPS scaling claim depends on multi-GPU pipeline orchestration that cannot be reproduced here

title: Pylo: Towards Accessible Learned Optimizers in PyTorch
note: CUDA-accelerated learned-optimizer kernels exposed through torch.optim; the reported throughput gains are single-GPU ViT-B/16 training numbers. Concern: the large-scale pre-training claims assume more compute than one A5000

title: MAC-Attention: a Match--Amend--Complete scheme for fast and accurate attention computation
note: Attention-reuse scheme for long-context decode (match, amend, complete) that composes with paged-KV managers and GQA; model-agnostic and single-GPU. Concern: the 128K-context evaluations need either a small model or host-memory KV offload to fit 24 GB

title: Spira: Exploiting Voxel Data Structural Properties for Efficient Sparse Convolution in Point Cloud Networks
note: Single-GPU sparse-convolution engine for point-cloud networks with released code and clear baselines (torchsparse, spconv). Kernel-map construction is a self-contained, improvable CUDA artifact

title: Efficient, VRAM-Constrained xLM Inference on Clients
note: Best-matched paper on the list: pipelined sharding for CPU-GPU hybrid inference explicitly under a VRAM budget, built on llama.cpp, with an MLSys26 artifact repo and a Zenodo archive. The A5000 plus 125 GiB host RAM is exactly the target regime

title: TeleRAG: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation Inference with Lookahead Retrieval
note: Lookahead retrieval that prefetches IVF clusters from CPU to GPU under tight GPU-memory budgets; the single-query latency results are single-GPU. Concern: the multi-GPU prefetch/cache scheduler parts cannot be reproduced

title: MorphServe: Efficient and Workload-Aware LLM Serving via Runtime Quantized Layer Swapping and KV Cache Resizing
note: Runtime quantized layer swapping plus pressure-aware KV-cache resizing on Vicuna and Llama models, driven by public Azure and BurstGPT traces which the authors already downscale to fit modest hardware. Single GPU, released code

title: NEST: Network- and Memory-Aware Device Placement for Distributed Deep Learning
note: Dynamic-programming device-placement planner that jointly models network, compute and memory; the planner itself is a user-space solver that can be studied and improved offline. Concern: validating the predicted throughput needs real multi-GPU clusters, so the project would have to stay in the planner/simulation half

title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
note: Hierarchical KV-cache manager on top of vLLM that classifies KV heads as stable or unstable and offloads cold pages to host memory; explicitly aimed at cutting GPU memory. Single GPU plus large host RAM is the ideal setup, and there is a Zenodo-archived artifact

title: MixLLM: LLM Quantization with Global Mixed-precision between Output-features and Highly-efficient System Design
note: Global mixed-precision quantization with a two-step dequantization and software-pipelined GEMM; the kernels are ordinary Tensor Core code that runs on Ampere. Concern: the headline accuracy numbers use Llama 3.1 70B, which does not fit 24 GB, so evaluation must move to 7-8B models

title: ContextPilot: Fast Long-Context Inference via Context Reuse
note: Context indexing, alignment and de-duplication to raise KV-cache reuse for long-context prefill, with a modular interface to existing engines. Prefill-bound, single-GPU workloads are well within the A5000's reach

title: PLA-Serve: A Prefill-Length-Aware LLM Serving System
note: Prefill-length-aware dual-queue scheduling and CUDA-Graph-based clustering on SGLang, with a documented artifact including scheduler docs and data. Concern: the multi-instance spatial-disaggregation results need several GPUs; temporal disaggregation on one prefill instance is still reproducible

title: ApproxMLIR : Accuracy-Aware Compiler for Compound ML System
note: Accuracy-aware MLIR dialect and optimizer for compound AI systems; the whole toolchain is user-space and MLIR/LLVM can be built into HOME. Concern: needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR build since clang is not installed

title: DynaFlow: Transparent and Flexible Intra-Device Parallelism via Programmable Operator Scheduling
note: Intra-device parallelism via programmable operator scheduling - by construction a single-GPU contribution, integrated into six ML systems with released code, and compatible with CUDA Graphs and TorchInductor. Very strong fit

title: Flashlight: PyTorch Compiler Extensions to Accelerate Attention Variants
note: PyTorch compiler extension that auto-generates fused FlashAttention-style kernels for arbitrary attention variants, compared against FlexAttention. Single GPU; FlashAttention-2 style kernels are supported on Ampere

title: Optimizing PyTorch Inference with LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
note: Comparative framework for LLM multi-agent PyTorch optimization on KernelBench, with code and a Zenodo archive. Concerns: reported speedups are H100 baselines that must be re-measured on Ampere, and agent search needs LLM API budget

title: From Tokens to Layers: Redefining Stall-Free Scheduling for MoE Serving with Layered Prefill
note: Layer-group scheduling that removes chunked-prefill expert reloads in MoE serving; a pure scheduler change with released code. Concern: only small MoEs (a few B active, ~15B total or quantized) fit in 24 GB, so the memory-traffic claim must be re-validated at that scale

title: AgenticCache: Cache-Driven Asynchronous Planning for Embodied AI Agents
note: Plan-transition cache with an asynchronous background updater for embodied agents - a genuine cache admission/eviction/validation policy question, evaluated in user-space simulators with released code. Concern: needs an LLM backend, either a local 7-8B model or API budget

title: BLASST: Dynamic BLocked Attention Sparsity via Softmax Thresholding
note: Training-free blocked sparse attention driven by a single softmax threshold, with drop-in kernels for prefill and decode across MHA/GQA/MQA/MLA and a calibration procedure. Concerns: the artifact is delivered as a Docker or Singularity image and neither is installed, so dependencies (TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer) must be rebuilt with conda; some kernels may assume Hopper features

title: Hawkeye: Reproducing GPU-Level Non-Determinism
note: Bit-exact CPU replay of NVIDIA Tensor Core matmuls; the paper explicitly tests Ampere along with Hopper and Lovelace, so the target GPU is a validated platform. Pure user-space tooling with no privileged access required - an unusually clean fit

title: LEANN: A Low-Storage Overhead Vector Index
note: Storage-efficient vector index that recomputes embeddings on the fly instead of storing them, explicitly targeted at personal devices and single machines. Released code, clear storage/latency/recall trade-off to push on

title: Kitty: Accurate and Efficient 2-bit KV Cache Quantization with Dynamic Channel-wise Precision Boost
note: 2-bit KV quantization with dynamic channel-wise precision boost, page-centric layout and Triton dequantization kernels; single GPU and released code. Triton on CUDA 12.x wheels over driver 535 is the only setup risk worth flagging

title: TriInfer: Hybrid EPD Disaggregation for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Model Inference
note: Encode-prefill-decode disaggregation for multimodal LLM serving with stage-level batching, released code and vLLM/SGLang baselines. Concern: the three stages are meant to run on separate heterogeneous instances, so a single-GPU study means co-locating stages or using MPS

title: TreeLine: An Update-In-Place Key-Value Store for Modern Storage
note: Single-node update-in-place KV store on NVMe as a RocksDB alternative; C++ user-space build, io_uring/O_DIRECT only, dataset fits the 257 GB free space

title: Frequency Domain Data Encoding in Apache IoTDB
note: Frequency-domain lossy encoding for time-series storage; pure Java single node. Concern: artifact is a personal Apache IoTDB fork branch not upstream. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/543202718/iotdb/tree/research/descend .

title: SHiFT: An Efficient, Flexible Search Engine for Transfer Learning
note: Search engine over a pretrained-model zoo with cost models and caching; one A5000 suffices for the small models. Concern: full model zoo plus datasets is a large download

title: Serving and Optimizing Machine Learning Workflows on Heterogeneous Infrastructures
note: ML-workflow serving and placement optimizer. Concern: original evaluation spans an edge-cloud heterogeneous cluster - on one host it must run as co-located processes or the placement optimizer studied offline from profiles

title: Optimizing Video Analytics with Declarative Model Relationships
note: Declarative video analytics that exploits model-relationship hints to trade accuracy for speed; single-GPU inference, AE-reviewed artifact repo

title: Dalton: Learned Partitioning for Distributed Data Streams
note: RL-learned partitioning for stream operators. Concern: built on Apache Flink - the distributed setup must be emulated with local task managers on the 32 threads

title: Can Learned Models Replace Hash Functions?
note: CPU-only study of learned models as hash functions in hash tables and joins; strong reproduce-then-improve target, no GPU or special hardware

title: TOD: GPU-accelerated Outlier Detection via Tensor Operations
note: GPU outlier detection with provable memory-aware batching; explicitly designed for one GPU, PyTorch, fits 24 GB

title: FILM: a Fully Learned Index for Larger-than-Memory Databases
note: Learned index for larger-than-memory data; single node, only RAM plus local disk needed

title: Toward Quantity-of-Interest Preserving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data
note: Quantity-of-interest preserving error-bounded lossy compression on top of SZ3; CPU-only C++. Concern: reference scientific datasets are tens of GB to download. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/szcompressor/SZ3/tree/qoi_error_control .

title: SubStrat: A Subset-Based Optimization Strategy for Faster AutoML
note: Data-subset strategy that accelerates AutoML search; pure Python CPU workload, small footprint

title: Excalibur: A Virtual Machine for Adaptive Fine-grained JIT-Compiled Query Execution based on VOILA
note: Adaptive fine-grained JIT-compiled query execution VM; C++ single node, LLVM is conda-installable. Concern: research-grade build with heavy dependencies

title: Making Cache Monotonic and Consistent
note: Cache admission and eviction policy that keeps cached query results monotonic and consistent; trace-driven single-node evaluation

title: SkinnerMT: Parallelizing for Efficiency and Robustness in Adaptive Query Processing on Multicore Platforms
note: Parallel RL-based adaptive query processing on multicore; Java, 16 cores/32 threads is a sensible scale-down of the paper's machine. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/cornelldbgroup/skinnerdb/tree/skinnermt .

title: On Efficient Approximate Queries over Machine Learning Models
note: Approximate query processing that minimises expensive ML model invocations using cheap proxy models; one GPU is enough

title: FederatedScope: A Flexible Federated Learning Platform for Heterogeneity
note: Event-driven federated learning framework; the standard mode simulates many clients as processes on one node with one GPU

title: Blink-hash: An Adaptive Hybrid Index for In-Memory Time-Series Databases
note: In-memory hybrid hash/tree index for time-series ingestion on multicore; C++ DRAM-only. Concern: paper's best numbers use a 4-socket server, we have 1 socket and 16 cores

title: Scalable and Robust Snapshot Isolation for High-Performance Storage Engines
note: MVCC/snapshot-isolation redesign inside the LeanStore storage engine; single-node NVMe C++, benchmarks via BenchBase. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/mvcc .

title: Lero: A Learning-to-Rank Query Optimizer
note: Learning-to-rank query optimizer for PostgreSQL; PostgreSQL builds from source into $HOME, model training is small enough for one GPU or CPU

title: Robust Query Driven Cardinality Estimation under Changing Workloads
note: Robust learned cardinality estimation evaluated on the CEB benchmark; PostgreSQL user-space build plus PyTorch on one GPU

title: The Case for Learned In-Memory Joins
note: Learned in-memory sort/hash joins; CPU-only C++ with SOSD-style datasets. Concern: paper uses AVX-512 in places, our Zen3 has only AVX2

title: Elf: Erasing-based Lossless Floating-Point Compression
note: Erasing-based lossless floating-point compression for time-series storage; Java, single node, modest datasets

title: LOGER: A Learned Optimizer towards Generating Efficient and Robust Query Execution Plans
note: Learned query optimizer generating robust plans on PostgreSQL; GPU-optional training, single node

title: Sim-Piece: Highly Accurate Piecewise Linear Approximation through Similar Segment Merging
note: Piecewise-linear lossy compression for time series; Java, CPU-only, small datasets - easy to reproduce and extend

title: BASE: Bridging the Gap between Cost and Latency for Query Optimization
note: RL query optimizer bridging cost and latency on PostgreSQL; same footprint as Bao/Lero, single node

title: Learned Index: A Comprehensive Experimental Evaluation
note: Comprehensive experimental evaluation of learned indexes; CPU-only benchmark harness, a natural reproduction or extension target

title: What Modern NVMe Storage Can Do, And How To Exploit It: High-Performance I/O for High-Performance Storage Engines
note: User-space high-IOPS NVMe I/O engine (io_uring, many threads) for storage engines; no root needed. Concern: paper uses 8 enterprise SSDs, we have 2 PM9A3 in software RAID so absolute IOPS will be lower. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/io .

title: The FastLanes Compression Layout: Decoding >100 Billion Integers per Second with Scalar Code
note: Bit-packing/compression layout decoded with auto-vectorizable scalar code; CPU-only C++. Concern: headline numbers are from AVX-512 and SVE machines, Zen3 gives AVX2 only

title: Towards Designing and Learning Piecewise Space-Filling Curves
note: Learned piecewise space-filling curve for multidimensional indexing; Python plus C++, single node

title: MiniGraph: Querying Big Graphs with a Single Machine
note: Out-of-core graph processing engine explicitly designed for a single machine; C++ user space, disk-resident graphs fit 257 GB

title: DILI: A Distribution-Driven Learned Index
note: Distribution-driven learned index; C++ single node, SOSD-style datasets

title: LEON: A New Framework for ML-Aided Query Optimization
note: ML-aided query optimization framework on PostgreSQL; single node, small models

title: SEIDEN: Revisiting Query Processing in Video Database Systems
note: Video database query processing that re-plans around expensive model inference; single GPU, part of the EVA ecosystem

title: Extract-Transform-Load for Video Streams
note: ETL pipeline for video streams that schedules model inference under resource limits; single GPU sufficient for a scaled-down stream count

title: LRU-C: Parallelizing Database I/Os for Flash SSDs
note: Buffer-pool replacement and I/O parallelisation for flash SSDs; user-space DBMS buffer manager on NVMe, no kernel changes needed

title: Scaling a Declarative Cluster Manager Architecture with Query Optimization Techniques
note: Declarative cluster manager (Kubernetes scheduler) reduced to constrained optimization; evaluated with trace-driven simulation and an emulated cluster. Concern: real Kubernetes needs root or containers, so only the simulated/emulated path is usable. Merge note: scout linked release tag https://github.com/vmware/declarative-cluster-management/releases/tag/vldb23 .

title: REmatch: a novel regex engine for finding all matches
note: User-space regular-expression engine enumerating all matches with output-linear delay; C++ library, CPU-only

title: ADOPT: Adaptively Optimizing Attribute Orders for Worst-Case Optimal Join Algorithms via Reinforcement Learning
note: RL-based adaptive attribute ordering for worst-case optimal joins; Java/C++ single node

note: frequency-based lossless encoder for periodic time series - compression artifact, CPU only - concern: domain-specific and no repo located

title: GPS: Revisiting the Data Layout for Disk-based High-Dimensional Vector Search
note: disk-block layout and adjacency-list cache for on-SSD vector search, beating PipeANN - the contribution is data layout and caching for SSD - concern: TB-scale datasets need scale-down - no repo located

title: HotHash: Hotness-Aware Consistent Hashing for Cloud Databases
note: hotness-aware consistent hashing for query scheduling and cache locality in cloud databases - a scheduling/load-balancing policy that can be studied by simulation or multiple local processes - concern: no repo located

title: Kangaroo: Efficient Lossless Floating-Point Compression via Dynamic Reference Selection
note: lossless floating-point time-series compression with dynamic reference selection - CPU-only compression artifact - concern: the located repo holds the datasets, the codec repo may be separate

title: KVDrive: A Holistic Multi-Tier KV Cache Management System for Long-Context LLM Inference
note: multi-tier KV-cache management across GPU memory, host DRAM and SSD for long-context inference - tiering plus pipeline scheduling - arXiv preprint 2605.18071 - concern: no repo located, long-context runs need a small model

title: L3: A GPU-Native Co-Designed Data Format for Learned Lossless Lightweight Compression
note: GPU-native learned lossless lightweight compression format with warp-cooperative decoding - compression plus GPU kernels, runs on one Ampere GPU

title: LICO: An SIMD-Aware High-Performance Learned Inverted Index Compression Framework
note: SIMD-aware learned compression of inverted indexes with error-bounded models - compression plus learned data structure, CPU only

title: LINE: A Learned Index with Group-Enhanced Leaves and Cache-Optimized Inner Tree
note: learned index with group-enhanced leaves and a cache-optimized inner tree - learned system component - concern: no repo located

title: Meep Hashing: Ultrafast and Compact Minimal Perfect Hashing for Practical Large-Scale Lookup Systems
note: minimal perfect hashing with integrated alien-key filtering for large-scale lookup systems - small user-space data-structure library - concern: no repo located

title: Modeling Concurrency Control as a Learnable Function
note: concurrency control modelled as a learnable function mapping database states to CC actions - a learned component inside a transactional system

title: NeurBench: A Benchmark Suite for Learned Database Components with Drift Modeling: [Experiments & Analysis]
note: benchmark suite with controllable data/workload drift for learned database components - reusable harness for learned-systems experiments

title: On Self-Designing Learned Indexes
note: self-designing learned index that searches its own structure with RL and meta-learning - learned system component, in-memory and on-disk

title: ReStore: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Data Migration in Multi-Tiered Storage
note: reinforcement-learning page-level migration policy for multi-tiered storage - a learned storage policy, evaluated with real SSD tiers or traces

title: Serving Hybrid LLM Loads with SLO Guarantees Using CPU-GPU Attention Piggybacking
note: LLM serving system that offloads best-effort attention to CPUs to protect latency-sensitive SLOs - CPU-GPU co-scheduling for inference - concern: motivated by shared clusters - single-GPU co-location still reproducible - no repo located

title: SPALM: A Sparsity-Pattern-Adaptive Library for Matrices
note: sparsity-pattern-adaptive matrix multiplication library integrated as a DuckDB operator - a CPU user-space numerical/systems library - concern: no repo located

title: To Adapt or Not to Adapt, That is the Ski Question
note: online ski-rental strategy deciding when an adaptive filter should pay the I/O to adapt - storage filter artifact with released code

title: Translytical Processing via DB-OS Co-designed Buffer: Cross-Engine Isolation and Tunable Update Visibility for HTAP
note: DB-OS co-designed buffer virtualization using huge-page-backed segments remapped read-only between PostgreSQL and DuckDB - implemented as a user-level library - concern: explicit huge pages normally need root, only transparent huge pages are available here - no repo located

title: Zeno Filter: To Infinity in Tiny Steps
note: in-place expandable filter that grows by less than 2x - compact storage data structure - concern: no repo located

title: Optimistic No-regret Algorithms for Discrete Caching
note: Prediction-assisted (oracle/NN-guided) discrete caching policies with a new optimistic Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader family; evaluated trace-driven on MovieLens and similar request traces. Pure CPU Python, no root, no GPU needed - a natural fit for the machine. Improvement angle - the policies are O(N) per request in the number of files and the paper itself trades performance against complexity; a faster implementation or a real cache integration is a testable hypothesis. Concern - the paper is theory-heavy and the released code is a numerical-experiment harness rather than a cache system so a reproduction may feel thin without extending it to a real workload trace

title: Smash: Flexible, Fast, and Resource-efficient Placement and Lookup of Distributed Storage
note: Object placement and lookup for distributed object stores using a space-efficient lookup structure instead of hashing; claims full placement flexibility with under 60 percent of the DRAM of Ceph/MapX. Core artifact is a self-contained user-space C++ library built with cmake and gcc 12 which the machine has. Concern - the paper's headline evaluation was run in a public cloud with multiple storage nodes, so a single-machine study would have to fall back to multi-process emulation plus data-structure microbenchmarks (memory cost, lookup latency, recovery time); the repo has no CI and was last pushed in 2021, so build friction is a real risk

title: DiffForward: On Balancing Forwarding Traffic for Modern Cloud Block Services via Differentiated Forwarding
note: Separates burst from stable write traffic at the client of a cloud block service and routes burst traffic round-robin into a decentralized log store to remove the proxy-layer imbalance. Official code released by the first author (Python, client/server/manager/utils). In-topic as a storage-engine/IO-path policy that is trace-driven. Concerns - the system is inherently multi-role (client, proxy servers, distributed log store) so on one host it can only be run as co-located processes; no README or build instructions in the repo and no open-access PDF found, so the burst-detection mechanism would have to be reconstructed from the ACM DL version

title: Agents of Autonomy: A Systematic Study of Robotics on Modern Hardware
note: RoWild is an open-source cross-platform user-space robotics benchmark suite (C++/Python, CPU and CUDA) that the paper profiles end-to-end on everything from embedded CPUs to server GPUs; one 16-core CPU plus one A5000 covers the high-end configuration. Concern: the paper is a characterization study and its own conclusions argue for hardware changes, so an improvement project would have to target the software side (kernel fusion, batching, data structures in the motion-planning and SLAM workloads). Second concern: the published characterization leans on architectural counters that perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks, so a reproduction would be limited to wall-clock timing.

title: The Online Pause and Resume Problem: Optimal Algorithms and An Application to Carbon-Aware Load Shifting
note: A suspend/resume scheduling policy for batch compute workloads, evaluated trace-driven on real grid carbon-intensity traces that ship with the repo - squarely the "policies evaluated with simulators or traces" case, and it runs on CPU in pure Python in minutes. Concern: the core contribution is a competitive-ratio proof for double-threshold algorithms, so the artifact is a numerical simulator rather than a system; an "improvement" here would be algorithmic or an empirical extension (e.g. driving it with real checkpoint/restore costs measured on this machine) rather than a systems build.

title: CarbonScaler: Leveraging Cloud Workload Elasticity for Optimizing Carbon-Efficiency
note: Elastic resource-allocation policy for batch jobs driven by carbon intensity, with a greedy marginal-allocation scheduler, released code, carbon traces and job scaling profiles; the analytic/trace-driven half is fully reproducible on one machine, and ML-training and MPI scaling profiles can be re-measured locally on 16 cores plus one GPU. Concern: the reference prototype is a Kubernetes autoscaler evaluated on a commercial cloud, and this machine has no root, no Docker and no second node, so the k8s prototype path is closed and the project would have to live in the simulator or in a local process-level re-implementation.

title: Machine Learning Systems are Bloated and Vulnerable
note: MMLB is a user-space measurement and debloating-analysis framework for ML software stacks that quantifies package-level bloat and links it to CVEs; the repo is actively maintained and the analysis itself is plain Python plus vulnerability scanners, which fit the machine easily. Concern: the objects of study are Docker images (TensorFlow/PyTorch/NVIDIA containers) and Docker is not installed and needs root here, so reproduction would require daemonless user-space image tooling (skopeo/umoci/bwrap) to pull and unpack the layers - a real porting risk that the audit stage should weigh.

title: NetDiffusion: Network Data Augmentation Through Protocol-Constrained Traffic Generation
note: A user-space generative data pipeline: a fine-tuned Stable Diffusion plus ControlNet model with protocol-constraint post-processing, sized for a single consumer GPU, so a 24 GB A5000 is sufficient for both fine-tuning (LoRA) and inference; the repo is popular and maintained, and generation cost per trace is the paper's acknowledged weak point, which makes a performance-improvement hypothesis natural. Concern: topic fit is the weakest in this list - it is generative ML applied to networking data rather than a core systems artifact, so the audit may prefer to drop it. Second concern: FlashAttention-2 works on Ampere but FP8 kernels do not, which caps some inference-speedup options.

title: Shrinking VOD Traffic via Renyi-Entropic Optimal Transport
note: Cache-efficiency work: it proposes Renyi entropy as a proxy for the cache footprint of a video catalogue, proves that minimizing it maximizes soft cache hit ratio, and evaluates on a real VOD request trace. Entirely CPU-side optimal-transport computation over a request trace, so the machine is not a constraint. Concern: no official implementation found - I searched the GitHub repository API for the system name and for "optimal transport / soft cache hit ratio" phrasings, checked the ACM DL landing page and the Edinburgh and Surrey institutional repository records, and found no code or Zenodo artifact link; the Edinburgh open-access PDF is behind a Cloudflare challenge from this host, so I could not read the first-page footnote and cannot rule out a link there. Listed as repo unknown per the code-check rule rather than out-no-code.

title: BONES: Near-Optimal Neural-Enhanced Video Streaming
note: A Lyapunov-based controller that jointly schedules a GPU super-resolution enhancement queue against network downloads - a GPU resource manager studied in simulation with real network traces, with code explicitly released in the abstract. Runs on one GPU and CPU-side trace replay. Concern: topic fit is partly video streaming/ABR rather than classic OS scheduling, and the strongest results come from a trace-driven simulator, so a systems improvement would mean strengthening the GPU-side scheduling model (batching, multi-tenant enhancement) rather than the streaming control law.

title: Using Lock-Free Design for Throughput-Optimized Cache Eviction (Mobius)
note: Lock-free FIFO-queue cache eviction policy (SIEVE-like) evaluated for concurrent throughput and hit ratio; pure user-space C++ integrated into CacheLib and RocksDB. Ideal fit for a 16-core/32-thread box. Second official repo is RocksDB-with-Mobius under the same account. Concern: the artifact account is an anonymized handle with no README-level build docs visible; scaling claims were made on a higher-core-count cluster so absolute numbers will differ.

title: ScaleOPT: A Scalable Optimal Page Replacement Policy Simulator
note: Parallel trace-driven simulator for Belady/OPT page replacement; plain C, CPU-only, compares directly against libCacheSim and webcachesim. Runs entirely in user space on cache traces. Concerns: evaluated on a 72-core machine, so our 16-core/32-thread CPU is a meaningful scale-down (speedup ceiling will be lower); repo has had no pushes since Oct 2024 and the ACM paper is closed-access so the trace list must be recovered from the repo.

title: Improving Multiresource Job Scheduling with Markovian Service Rate Policies
note: Multiresource job scheduling policy class evaluated by trace-driven simulation on the Google Borg trace; C++ simulator, user space, no cluster needed. Concern: the paper's core contribution is queueing-theoretic (throughput optimality, response-time bounds) and the simulator is a supporting artifact, so an "improvement" project would be partly analytical; the Borg trace download is large and must be budgeted against ~257 GB free.

title: Learning-Augmented Competitive Algorithms for Spatiotemporal Online Allocation with Deadline Constraints (ST-CLIP)
note: Carbon-aware spatiotemporal scheduling of delay-tolerant batch jobs across datacenters, evaluated as a trace-driven simulation (carbon-intensity traces) in Python/Jupyter - no cluster or root needed. Concern: primarily an online-algorithms paper (competitive ratio, consistency-robustness trade-off); the artifact is a notebook-based simulation harness, so the project would be a policy/prediction improvement rather than a systems build.

title: A Case Study for Ray Tracing Cores: Performance Insights with BFS and Triangle Counting in Graphs
note: Repurposes GPU RT cores (OptiX BVH + ray casting) for graph BFS, triangle counting and set intersection, compared against CUDA baselines. Single GPU, user space, CUDA code in the repo. Our RTX A5000 is Ampere (CC 8.6) and does have 2nd-gen RT cores plus OptiX support, so the mechanism reproduces. Concerns: the paper's result is largely negative (RT cores lose to CUDA except at high skew), which suits the "reproduction with nuance" fallback; OptiX version may want a newer driver than 535, and large graphs must fit in 24 GB.

title: Diffusion-Based Generative System Surrogates for Scalable Learning-Driven Optimization in Virtual Playgrounds (DiffNEST)
note: Diffusion model that generates synthetic system traces so that RL-based system optimizers can be trained without physical hardware; Python/PyTorch, single-GPU training fits 24 GB. Repo URL is stated in the abstract, so it is unambiguously official. Concerns: the two case studies (task-aware adaptive DVFS, multi-core cache partitioning) actuate hardware knobs that need root here - DVFS via cpupower and CAT/pqos are both blocked - so only the surrogate-training and offline-evaluation half is reproducible; repo is small and was pushed only once (Mar 2025).

title: CertainSync: Rateless Set Reconciliation with Certainty
note: Rateless IBLT-based set reconciliation library with guaranteed (not probabilistic) success; evaluation is a single-machine simulation of communication overhead, no network or root required. Repo title matches the paper exactly. Concerns: contribution is closer to coding theory / distributed protocols than to the topic table's systems categories, and the motivating deployment is blockchain mempool sync - an audit may judge it out of topic.

title: UniCache: Unifying Prefix Cache Eviction for Heterogeneous LLM Serving Workloads
note: Prefix KV-cache eviction policy for LLM serving. Trace-driven prefix-cache simulator plus a vLLM implementation - both run on one 24 GB GPU with a 7-8B model. Ideal improvement target: swap in a better eviction policy and re-run the simulator

title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
note: Symbolic-property analysis of DRL agents used inside systems - video streaming, wireless allocation, congestion control. Pure user-space Python plus DNN verification backends such as Marabou; CPU-bound and fits 16 cores. Concern: verification queries can be slow, so scale the models down

title: Performance Analysis of the Randomized SIEVE/CLOCK cache replacement algorithm
note: Randomized SIEVE/CLOCK with multiple access bits plus a mean-field model and trace simulations - textbook fit for a cache-policy improvement project and needs only CPU. Concern: no public repository found. I searched GitHub repositories for SIEVE CLOCK cache and the authors, checked Van Houdt's and Desnoyers' pages, and could not reach the ACM DL full text, so artifact status is genuinely unknown rather than confirmed absent

title: CAPSULE: A Storage Prefetcher Harnessing Spatio-Temporal Locality for Cloud-Scale Workloads
note: Clustering-based storage prefetcher evaluated purely by replaying 729 public block traces - MSR, CloudPhysics, Tencent, Alibaba, Meta. No root, no special hardware; artifact repo is explicitly labelled as the paper artifact. Concern: downloading the full trace corpus may exceed the 257 GB free, so pick a subset

title: Cache Your Prompt When It’s Green — Carbon-aware Caching for Large Language Model Serving
note: Carbon-aware KV/context-cache sizing on top of LMCache, driven by Azure LLM traces and carbon-intensity data. Concern: headline numbers use Llama-3 70B which will not fit in 24 GB, so the reproduction has to scale down to a 7-8B model or run the solver in trace-driven simulation

title: HealthServe: A Public Health-Aware Inference Framework
note: Health- and carbon-aware scheduling for LLM inference across geo-distributed GPU pools. Concern: the paper evaluates a heterogeneous multi-region cluster, so a single-node reproduction has to run the scheduler against simulated regions; the optimizer itself is user-space Python

title: Better than Optimal: Improving Adaptive Stochastic Quantization Using Shared Randomness
note: Adaptive unbiased quantization with shared randomness for gradient and tensor compression. Self-contained numeric code plus a distributed-mean-estimation case study that runs fine as multiple processes on one box; no special hardware

title: ACALSim: A Scalable Parallel Simulation Framework for High-Performance System Design Space Exploration
note: Parallel discrete-event simulation framework in ~26k lines of C++ aimed explicitly at single-node multi-core scaling - the 16-core/32-thread Threadripper is the paper's own target class. Clear improvement hypotheses around thread management and synchronization. Concern: the reference repo ships a Docker workspace, so deps must be installed by hand

title: Pittacus: Optimizing LLM Serving on Cloud Data Centers with Forecast Aware Auto-Scaling
note: Forecast-aware autoscaling and routing for LLM serving, evaluated mainly by replaying 10M Microsoft 365 production requests through a simulator plus an ILP. The simulation and forecasting path is CPU-only. Concern: the real-run portion uses multi-region GPU VMs and has no single-node equivalent

title: Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference: Theory and Practice
note: SLO-aware prefill/decode scheduler with a throughput-optimality proof and a practical scheduler. Already evaluated with Mistral-7B on a single 48 GB RTX 6000 Ada - the closest of any paper here to the target machine. Concern: 7B in FP16 plus KV cache is tight in 24 GB, so shorter contexts or a quantized model

title: Auxo: Efficient Federated Learning via Scalable Client Clustering
note: Cohort-identification algorithm layered on FedScale; evaluation is trace-driven FL simulation that runs on one GPU. Pure user-space Python/PyTorch. Concern: paper reports large simulated client populations, so a scaled-down client count will be needed to fit 24 GB and 10 weeks. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/SymbioticLab/FedScale/tree/master/examples/auxo .

title: OneAdapt: Fast Adaptation for Deep Learning Applications via Backpropagation
note: Configuration adaptation for DNN inference on streaming video using gradients through the codec; single-GPU inference pipeline, user space. Code URL is cited in the paper itself (reference [8]). Concern: repo has no README and many SLURM-oriented batch scripts, so setup effort is real; video datasets must be downloaded.

title: A Comparison of End-to-End Decision Forest Inference Pipelines
note: Benchmark and optimization study of decision-forest inference across ONNX, TreeLite, HummingBird, lleaves, FIL, TFDF plus in-database UDF-centric vs relation-centric execution. All components install in user space via conda/pip plus a user-built PostgreSQL. Fits one CPU socket and one GPU. Concern: FIL/cuML path needs a CUDA build compatible with driver 535.

title: LatenSeer: Causal Modeling of End-to-End Latency Distributions by Harnessing Distributed Tracing
note: Offline, trace-driven modeling tool (Python) that estimates end-to-end latency distributions from distributed traces; no root, no kernel, no cluster needed for the core contribution. Concern: the repo also ships DeathStarBench setup scripts for collecting fresh traces, which would need containers; the released Alibaba/DSB traces avoid that.

title: CAMEO: A Causal Transfer Learning Approach for Performance Optimization of Configurable Computer Systems
note: Causal-structure transfer learning for configuration tuning; the method is user-space Python and can be driven from the authors' offline configuration-measurement datasets. Concern: original target environments include NVIDIA Jetson TX1/TX2/Xavier hardware we do not have, so live-measurement experiments must be restricted to x86 or GPU workloads reproducible on the A5000.

title: Is Machine Learning Necessary for Cloud Resource Usage Forecasting?
note: Shows LSTM forecasts of cloud resource usage are effectively a one-step shift and that a trivial persistence forecast matches them, on Alibaba/Azure/Google/Bitbrains traces. Entirely CPU/GPU-optional Python notebooks on public traces - an ideal reproduce-and-extend target. Concern: it is a 11-page vision-track paper, so an improvement project must add its own downstream evaluation (e.g. autoscaling policy driven by the forecast).

title: How Does It Function? Characterizing Long-term Trends in Production Serverless Workloads
note: Releases two Huawei production FaaS traces (7+ months, 1.4T invocations) with loading/analysis notebooks; trace-driven scheduling and cold-start simulation studies fit the machine exactly. Concern: industry characterization paper - the artifact is data plus notebooks, not a system, so the improvement must come from a simulator or policy the team builds on top of the traces.

title: tf.data service: A Case for Disaggregating ML Input Data Processing
note: Input-data pipelines are explicitly in scope; the system is open source inside TensorFlow (paper states so and cites the TensorFlow GitHub project). Dispatcher and workers are ordinary user-space processes that can all be co-located on the 16-core host with one A5000 to study input-bound training. Concern: the paper's headline results are Google-fleet-scale; only a single-node, multi-process scale-down is possible, and the released code is a production subsystem rather than a paper artifact.

title: Parrotfish: Parametric Regression for Optimizing Serverless Functions
note: Online parametric-regression rightsizing of serverless function memory; the learner itself is a small Python 3.12 package that fits the machine trivially and is still actively maintained. Concern: the measured exploration loop invokes real AWS Lambda (or GCP) functions, which env.md's "single machine only" does not provide - the project would have to drive the regressor from recorded duration-vs-memory sweeps or a local function emulator, which is a real risk.

title: Flame: Simplifying Topology Extension in Federated Learning
note: Topology abstraction (TAG) for composing FL architectures; the Python SDK data plane runs standalone and the docs state the control plane is optional for running SDK examples, so multi-topology FL can be emulated with local processes on one host. Concern: the full system ("flame-in-a-box") expects minikube/Docker and Go tooling - Docker is unavailable, so only the SDK-level path is usable, and Go must be installed via conda.

title: FileScale: Fast and Elastic Metadata Management for Distributed File Systems
note: Three-tier HDFS metadata architecture (in-memory tier plus distributed DBMS tier); all Java/user space, no root needed, and the paper's distinguishing claim - matching single-machine in-memory performance at small scale - is exactly the regime this host can test. Concern: the linear-scalability half of the evaluation needs several nodes; it can only be approximated with multiple JVMs on the 16-core host, and Java must be installed per-user.

title: Plexus: Optimizing Join Approximation for Geo-Distributed Data Analytics
note: Join-sampling algorithms plus weight approximation and heterogeneity-aware allocation; the artifact is a Scala/sbt client-server program, so the algorithmic contribution is testable as several user-space processes. Concern: the setting is wide-area - realistic WAN emulation normally needs tc/netem, which requires root, so latency/bandwidth heterogeneity would have to be injected in application code; borderline, flagged for the audit stage.

title: Queue Management for SLO-Oriented Large Language Model Serving (QLM)
note: Request-group queue ordering plus an LP-backed virtual-queue model on top of vLLM - squarely an LLM serving / scheduling artifact. Concern - paper evaluates on heterogeneous multi-GPU setups (A100/A10G) and several models; scale-down to one 24 GB A5000 with a 7B model is straightforward but changes the SLO-attainment numbers. Python repo, actively pushed through 2025.

title: FedCaSe: Enhancing Federated Learning with Heterogeneity-aware Caching and Scheduling
note: The contribution is an importance-aware on-device cache admission/eviction policy plus a client scheduler - a cache-policy paper wearing an FL hat. FL client populations are emulated on a single host (FedScale-style), so it fits the machine. Concern - the paper's scale (thousands of simulated clients) needs the storage/RAM budget checked; GPU use is light.

title: Scheduling for Reduced Tail Task Latencies in Highly Utilized Datacenters (Murmuration)
note: Decentralized task scheduler evaluated both on a cluster and with a trace-driven simulator over public Google/Alibaba traces. scope.md explicitly allows cluster schedulers studied by simulation. Concern - the k8s prototype (csesmita/murmuration_prototype, plus csesmita/kubernetes-helper) needs a real multi-node cluster; only the simulator path is usable here, so any improvement must be argued in simulation.

title: KACE: Kernel-Aware Colocation for Efficient GPU Spatial Sharing
note: Single-GPU spatial-sharing interference predictor plus a colocation policy - the whole mechanism targets one GPU, an unusually good fit for this machine. Concerns - artifact was built on a V100 32 GB with Docker; offline kernel-metric profiling uses CUPTI/Nsight, which on stock drivers needs NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0 (root) - the released metric CSVs and the model-training/figure path do run without it. A5000 has no MIG, so only MPS-style sharing is reproducible.

title: A Data Optimizer for Region-Aware Self-describing Files in Scientific Computing (RASTER)
note: User-space C++ middleware that reorganizes self-describing (HDF5/NetCDF-style) files into region-aware variable groups - runs entirely in user space over ordinary files. Concern - the paper's three evaluation platforms are Optane PMEM, Huawei OceanStor and Sunway TaihuLight; none are available, so the study would have to be re-baselined on local NVMe, which changes the headline speedups.

title: Rethinking State Management in Actor Systems for Cloud-Native Applications (SmSa / SnapperX)
note: A user-space data-management layer over Orleans with new logging and concurrency-control algorithms for cross-actor dependencies - a runtime/concurrency artifact, no kernel or hardware dependency. Concerns - artifact README asks for Docker Desktop and AWS multi-region credentials; a single-host Orleans silo cluster is possible but needs porting, and .NET 8 SDK has to be installed into $HOME (no apt).

title: Memory Management in Complex Join Queries: A Re-evaluation Study
note: Re-evaluates 1990s memory-distribution policies across join operators using a modified AsterixDB - user-space memory budgeting, single node, JVM only (Java installable via conda). Directly matches the course's fallback "careful reproduction" track and leaves obvious room for an improved memory-distribution policy. Concerns - original runs were on AWS HDD/SSD instances, so device-level results will differ; it is a study paper, so the "improvement" angle has to be supplied by the team.

title: Oneiros: KV Cache Optimization through Parameter Remapping for Multi-tenant LLM Serving
note: Remaps memory holding model parameters into KV cache instead of swapping; pure user-space change on top of vLLM. A 7-8B FP16 model plus KV cache fits the 24 GB A5000. Concern - the multi-tenant results assume several resident models, so the study must be scaled down to small models or quantized ones. Also check that the CUDA 12.x wheels it needs run on driver 535.

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
note: Adaptive draft length, confidence-prior verification and an SLO-aware efficiency estimator - all scheduling logic inside a single-GPU serving loop. Draft plus target model pair fits 24 GB. Ampere supports FlashAttention-2 so no FP8 dependence. Concern - trace replay assumes a certain request rate, may need rescaling.

title: 10Cache: Heterogeneous Resource-Aware Tensor Caching and Migration for LLM Training
note: Tensor caching, prefetch and migration across GPU, pinned CPU memory and NVMe, built on DeepSpeed offloading. The machine profile (1 GPU, 125 GiB RAM, NVMe) is exactly the tiering target. Concern - paper trains larger models than 24 GB allows, so model sizes must be scaled down.

title: Balancing Fairness and Performance in Multi-User Spark Workloads with Dynamic Scheduling
note: User Weighted Fair Queuing plus runtime partitioning, implemented as a patched Spark 3.5.5 (JVM, entirely user space) with a companion benchmark tool and a Zenodo artifact. Concern - the original evaluation uses a multi-node cluster; on this machine it must be reproduced with a single-host standalone Spark deployment and multiple executors across the 32 threads. Java must be installed via conda.

title: VLCs: Managing Parallelism with Virtualized Libraries
note: Virtual Library Contexts partition library resources inside one process via custom dynamic linking - no kernel, no root, no special hardware. Benchmarks are OpenMP, OpenBLAS and LibTorch on a single node, which this 16-core machine can run. Concern - likely needs a recent clang/LLVM, installable per-user through conda.

title: Hydra: Virtualized Multi-Language Runtime for High-Density Serverless Platforms
note: The Hydra runtime colocates many function sandboxes in one process using GraalVM Native Image Isolates plus Truffle, with per-sandbox checkpoint/restore - all user space, installable in $HOME. Concern - the Hydra *platform* half compares against OpenWhisk and Knative, which need Docker/Kubernetes and root, so the project would have to stay at the runtime/density level.

title: FailLite: Failure-Resilient Model Serving for Resource-Constrained Edge Environments
note: Heterogeneous replication with smaller failover model variants, warm/cold replica placement and progressive failover across 27 small vision models - all fit comfortably in 24 GB. Concern - originally evaluated on a multi-device edge testbed; here it must be emulated with cgroup-v2-limited processes on one host (cgroup cpu/memory controllers are delegated, so this is possible).

title: Hybrid Learning and Optimization-Based Dynamic Scheduling for DL Workloads on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters
note: RLTune combines an RL prioritizer with MILP job-to-node mapping and is trained and evaluated entirely on public traces (Microsoft Philly, Helios, Alibaba) - a trace-driven simulation that needs no GPU cluster. Repo URL is cited in the paper itself. Concern - repo quality and MILP solver licensing were not verified beyond a desk check.

title: Understanding GPU Resource Interference One Level Deeper
note: CUDA microbenchmark suite that isolates interference on block schedulers, compute units, L1/L2 and memory bandwidth, plus a vLLM fork for colocated LLM token generation. Single GPU, fully user space. Concerns - this is an 8-page measurement study rather than a system, so an improvement project would have to extend the methodology or build a policy on top of it; and some GPU counter collection may require admin-enabled profiling, which is unavailable here.

title: CoMPI: Coordinated Model Merging and Parallel Inference at Edge
note: Jointly optimizes model merging (parameter sharing to cut GPU memory) and parallel deployment for multi-model edge inference under memory pressure - the memory-pressure regime maps well onto one 24 GB GPU. Repo description matches the paper and was last pushed 2025-11-21, the SoCC presentation date. Concerns - repository authorship was inferred from the description and timing rather than from a link in the paper; the paper assumes a small multi-GPU edge cluster, so a single-GPU scale-down is needed.

title: A Fast, Efficient, and Strongly-Consistent Object Store
note: Storage-engine paper from the Northeastern group behind LSVD. Included rather than rejected because the abstract could not be retrieved - the ACM DL is unreachable from this host and no preprint or author copy was found, so neither the artifact status nor the exact hardware assumptions could be checked. Concerns - a strongly-consistent object store is likely evaluated on a multi-node cluster and may build on RADOS/Ceph, which would need root; repo is unknown after searching GitHub for LSVD/object-store repos and the authors' pages. Verify before committing to it.

title: Characterizing Distributed Machine Learning Workloads on Apache Spark (Experimentation and Deployment Paper)
note: Studies the interplay of Spark platform parameters vs. ML hyper-parameters over 13 learning methods and 6 datasets; the headline claim (platform parameters matter more than hyper-parameters for model quality) is a clean testable hypothesis and Spark MLlib is pure user-space JVM code that runs in local/standalone mode on 16 cores and 125 GiB RAM. Concerns - the paper is a characterization study run on two multi-node clusters so absolute numbers will not reproduce on one node; the released artifact is mostly workload scripts plus traces rather than a system to improve; an improvement angle would have to be an auto-tuner built on their traces. Traces are also archived separately (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14151075)

title: Pravega: A Tiered Storage System for Data Streams
note: Tiered stream storage - hot append-only tier plus automatic migration to long-term object/file storage, with elastic per-stream segment scaling. Mature, fully open-source Java implementation with a documented single-process standalone mode; the tiering and auto-scaling policies are exactly the kind of user-space mechanism that can be re-designed and measured. Concerns - the paper evaluates a distributed deployment on AWS against Kafka and Pulsar, and the full stack pulls in Zookeeper plus Apache BookKeeper and an S3/NFS tier; a single-node scale-down (all three systems in one host, MinIO or local FS as tier 2) is plausible but needs to be validated early, and Java has to be installed through conda

title: Glider: Serverless Ephemeral Stateful Near-Data Computation
note: Ephemeral storage for serverless analytics that adds "storage actions" - stateful near-data operators plus an I/O streaming interface - so intermediate data is not shuffled through object storage. Core artifact is a user-space Java storage service (an Apache Crail fork) plus example applications in a second repo (https://github.com/CLOUDLAB-URV/glider-examples); shuffle/aggregation offload placement is a natural improvement target. Concerns - Crail is built for RDMA/NVMf hardware and Glider is normally driven by FaaS functions on a cloud platform; the project would have to stand on Crail's TCP tier and drive it with Lithops' localhost backend or plain processes, which is untested here

title: DynaCut: A Framework for Dynamic and Adaptive Program Customization
note: Binary-level, runtime code debloating - rewrites the image of a live process to disable unused or already-executed (e.g. initialization) code and re-enable it on demand, guided by execution-trace differential analysis. Entirely user-space, single-machine, and evaluated on ordinary server binaries such as Redis and Nginx that fit this box easily. Concerns - the process rewriter is a modified CRIU plus CRIT, and CRIU checkpoint/restore normally needs root or CAP_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE; unprivileged operation would have to go through a user namespace (bwrap is available), so feasibility of the very first checkpoint must be confirmed before committing to this paper

title: On the Semantic Overlap of Operators in Stream Processing Engines
note: User-space JVM stream processing engines and purpose-built micro-SPEs; all throughput numbers are single-host. Paper carries an explicit "Artifact Availability" statement pointing at this repo. Concern: baselines are Flink/Storm-class engines that need a JDK installed via conda, and the claim to improve is operator-level throughput rather than a distributed property.

title: sMVX: Multi-Variant Execution on Selected Code Paths
note: In-process monitor plus custom loader, entirely user space, no kernel module and no root; repo builds libmonitor.so / liblmvx.so with plain make and evaluates on user-space server applications. Concern: isolation of the monitor relies on Intel MPK. The Threadripper PRO 5955WX is Zen 3, which does expose protection keys, but the pku CPU flag must be confirmed before committing; without it the MPK path would have to be stubbed or emulated.

title: Amalgam: A Framework for Obfuscated Neural Network Training on the Cloud
note: Model/dataset augmentation for obfuscated training; repo URL is printed in the abstract. Vision and NLP models used are modest and fit a single 24 GB A5000; the "cloud" framing is only a deployment story and the measured quantity is per-GPU training overhead, which reproduces locally.

title: zkStream: a Framework for Trustworthy Stream Processing
note: Official artifact repo from the authors' lab, described as "the artifact accompanying our paper". Rust, CPU-only proving and verification, benchmarked with NEXMark-style streaming workloads on one host. Concern: Rust is not installed and must come from rustup in $HOME; the repo ships a Dockerfile but cargo builds work without Docker; ZKP proving is memory-hungry, though 125 GiB RAM is ample.

title: QuickDrop: Efficient Federated Unlearning via Synthetic Data Generation
note: Headline metric is unlearning wall-clock time (463x vs retraining), i.e. a systems-efficiency claim, and FL clients are simulated as processes on one machine over CIFAR-scale datasets. Repo description names this Middleware'24 paper. Concern: the arXiv preprint appears under the earlier title "Efficient Federated Unlearning by Integrated Dataset Distillation".

title: RoleML: a Role-Oriented Programming Model for Customizable Distributed Machine Learning on Edges
note: Python programming model plus runtime; roles are ordinary processes and can be co-located on a single host, and the paper's headline claim is low runtime overhead of the abstraction. Repo is by the first author. Concern: the automatic role-offloading mechanism is built on containerization and Docker/Podman are not installed, so that sub-feature would need porting to plain processes or bwrap.

title: SeqCDC: Hashless Content-Defined Chunking for Data Deduplication
note: Best machine fit in the venue: pure user-space single-threaded CPU chunking measured as MB/s on local files. The official DedupBench tool from the authors' lab lists SeqCDC and cites this exact paper, and the evaluation dataset is published on Kaggle. Concern: only ~257 GB free on /home, so the larger corpora must be subsetted.

title: Towards Affordable Reproducibility Using Scalable Capture and Comparison of Intermediate Multi-Run Results
note: Hash/Merkle-tree comparison of checkpoint data with error bounds; the artifact is a user-space C++/Kokkos library whose README cites this paper by DOI. The hashing, tree construction and I/O-reduction mechanisms are all measurable on one node. Concern: the paper drives the system from HACC cosmology runs on an HPC cluster, so a single-machine study needs scaled-down or synthetic checkpoint streams; build needs Kokkos, io_uring and optionally ADIOS2, all installable in $HOME.

title: Deep Optimizer States: Towards Scalable Training of Transformer Models Using Interleaved Offloading
note: Mechanism is CPU-GPU interleaved offloading of optimizer state driven by intra-iteration GPU memory fluctuation, which is meaningful with one GPU plus large host RAM - exactly this machine's shape (24 GB GPU, 125 GiB RAM). Artifact URL is printed in the paper and the directory contains run scripts and sample logs. Concern: the paper evaluates 7B-70B models across many GPUs, so a scale-down to a ~1B-class model is required; the DataStates DeepSpeed/Megatron-DeepSpeed forks may want a CUDA newer than the system 11.8, which conda can supply within driver 535's compatibility window. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/DataStates/artifacts/tree/main/deep-optimizer-states .

title: FreeRide: Harvesting Bubbles in Pipeline Parallelism
note: Middleware that detects idle pipeline-parallel bubbles and schedules generic GPU side tasks into them with MPS-based resource capping. Concern: evaluated on 4x RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) plus a second server; pipeline parallelism needs >=2 stages, so a single-GPU scale-down means emulating 2 stages as separate processes on the one A5000 with a small model (nanoGPT-class). Concern: the side-task isolation path uses Docker, which is not installed and would need replacing by cgroup v2 + MPS (both usable unprivileged here). Core mechanism itself is per-GPU and user space.

title: Adjusted Objects: An Efficient and Principled Approach to Scalable Programming
note: Pure user-space Java concurrency library (DEGO) of "adjusted" shared objects, exactly the "runtimes / concurrency libraries" case in the topic table. Evaluated on a single server-class multicore with JMH-style microbenchmarks plus a Retwis-like workload; 16c/32t and 125 GiB RAM are adequate. JDK installs in user space via conda. No GPU, no root, no kernel features needed. Concern: original numbers come from a machine with more hardware threads, so absolute scalability curves will differ.

title: Clair Obscur: The Light and Shadow of System Call Interposition - From Pitfalls to Solutions with K23
note: x86-64 system call interposition by binary rewriting; target ISA matches the Threadripper host and the artifact is user space. Also ships a systematic critique of zpoline/lazypoline, so a reproduction fallback is natural. Concern: the hybrid design combines binary rewriting with "multiple Linux interfaces" - if one of those is seccomp user notification it may need CAP_SYS_ADMIN or a no_new_privs path, and ptrace scope is governed by a sysctl this user cannot change. Worth confirming at audit. Repo URL taken from the paper text.

title: xMem: A CPU-Based Approach for Accurate Estimation of GPU Memory in Deep Learning Training Workloads
note: The estimator itself runs CPU-only (dynamic analysis of allocator behaviour), so the expensive half of the pipeline needs no GPU at all; the single A5000 is only needed to collect ground-truth peak memory. Their 25-model suite is CNN/Transformer training, most of which fits in 24 GB at reduced batch size. Concern: a few of the 25 models may not fit in 24 GB, so the validation set will have to be trimmed; 5209 runs is a lot of wall-clock on one GPU and would need subsampling.

title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
note: Proximity is an LSH-based approximate key-value cache in front of a RAG vector database - squarely a cache admission/eviction/approximation policy study, and the clearest single-node fit in the venue. Rust implementation, MMLU and MedRAG benchmarks, embedding model and a 7-8B generator both fit in 24 GB FP16. Rust is not installed but rustup into $HOME needs no root. Concern: the MedRAG corpus plus index is a multi-tens-of-GB download against ~257 GB free.

title: Roadrunner: Accelerating Data Delivery to WebAssembly-Based Serverless Functions
note: Rust sidecar shim doing near-zero-copy, serialization-free transfer between WasmEdge VMs using vmsplice/splice - ordinary unprivileged syscalls, no eBPF, no kernel module, single host. Inter-function latency and throughput microbenchmarks are the headline results and are reproducible locally. Concern: the artifact packages functions as OCI bundles for containerd and the paper positions it inside Knative/OpenFaaS; with no Docker or root, the shim would have to be driven directly or through rootless tooling built in $HOME.

title: Tiaccoon: Unified Access Control with Multiple Transports in Container Networks
note: Go middleware that hooks socket-API system calls and transparently substitutes a faster transport while keeping one access-control policy - a user-space syscall-interposition artifact, and the UNIX-domain-socket fast path plus the policy engine are testable on one host. Borderline, kept per the "note the concern" rule. Concern: the RDMA transport cannot be exercised at all here, and the container-overlay baselines assume a container runtime that is not installed and cannot be apt-installed; network namespaces via unprivileged user namespaces would have to stand in. Repo is marked "[Experimental]" by the author.

title: A Hybrid Runtime for Function-as-a-Service at the Edge
note: RUNE combines containers and WebAssembly (WasmEdge) in one FaaS runtime and trades cold-start latency against idle-container memory - a user-space runtime/placement-policy question that is a natural single-node improvement target (better hybrid placement policy, measured as p99 latency vs. memory). Concern: repo is unknown - the paper states RUNE is open source but no URL surfaced from GitHub search on the system name, the authors' handles (Adam Hall, Umakishore Ramachandran, Georgia Tech), or web search, and the ACM full text is unreachable from this host. Concern: the container half of the hybrid needs a container runtime that is not installed and requires a rootless port. Both must be settled at audit.
